Group-level reflection on the policy's own verified rollouts, contrasting successful and failed trajectories, produces capability-aligned guidance that outperforms baselines in agentic RL.
This reflective guidance refines turn-level credit assignment beyond what coarse terminal rewards provide, and beyond what external or single-trajectory skills can supply.

Personalized AI research ideation that tailors candidate directions to fine-grained researcher profiles and jointly reduces redundancy across a community's portfolio can diversify research directions against AI-induced homogenization without sacrificing researcher-direction fit.

Multimodal latent reasoning is better supervised by distilling the reasoning process of a privileged multimodal chain-of-thought than by aligning latent states to compressed visual features, and this approach outperforms existing visual-latent methods.

Binary support-or-oppose judgments of AI policy proposals can be replaced by a transparent, multi-attribute instrument that surfaces priorities and tensions across policy attributes without itself judging effectiveness or desirability.
A TPACK-guided scaffold can align a multi-agent AI tool's affordances with requirements quality learning goals in master-level requirements engineering education.
Students used the AI tool selectively as analytical support rather than as an automated substitute for their own requirements work.
The learning benefits of the AI-supported approach were uneven across requirements quality dimensions, strongest for value articulation and mixed for negotiability.

Synthesizing controllable egocentric manipulation videos from a pretrained video generator, using geometry-aware conditioning, can substantially improve downstream world-action model generalization where real egocentric data is scarce.
Anchored projective memory and action-3D rotary position embedding are geometry-aware conditioning mechanisms that keep long egocentric rollouts visually faithful.

Attributing general intelligence, hallucination as cognitive failure, agency, sentience, and alignment to language models is a category mistake, because these properties belong to human communicative practice and a language model cannot bear them.

Agents should reconstruct retrieved experiences to fit their current state rather than replay them verbatim, because verbatim replay ignores the gap between abstract stored experience and concrete decision-time states and frequently causes negative transfer.
Conditioning a policy's critique of retrieved experience on the current state, as MemHarness does, yields agents that outperform pure RL baselines on ALFWorld and WebShop.

Speech recognition should emit intent-preserving clean text during ongoing speech, because existing spoken-to-written methods cannot revise already-emitted text, and the AgenticSR approach achieves this and attains the highest AASR-Bench scores across multiple ASR front ends.

Calibrating post-training quantization of World Action Models to the model's structure, closed-loop rollout distribution, and task objective, rather than open-loop objectives and non-deployment calibration data, preserves near-FP16 simulation performance while reducing memory and speeding up the targeted video and action blocks.

Replacing the Epps-Pulley regularizer in LeWorldModel with quantile-quantile matching better controls heavy-tailed latent deviations, because quantile matching keeps corrective gradients active for isolated tail samples where Epps-Pulley gradients vanish, and this improves Gaussian alignment and planning success.

Unsupervised alignment of flow-matching models for 3D atomic structure prediction, using group-relative policy optimization with a dual reward for latent structural modes and thermodynamic stability, can outperform fully supervised alignment that relies on noisy ground-truth coordinate matching.

Current vision-language-model judges of computer-using agent trajectories are not yet reliable, because even state-of-the-art judges fall short of an ideal judge and share a leniency bias that mislabels failed runs as successes.
Reliable judges are too expensive to run at scale and open models lag far behind them, so a standardized benchmark and an open reward model are needed to evaluate and close that gap.
The OSReward benchmark and the OS-Shepherd open reward model provide that standardized evaluation, and OS-Shepherd matches commercial judges.

Preference optimization that penalizes confrontation during motivational interviewing lowers LLM counselors' goal persistence below parity, so the attunement gained comes at a measurable cost to persistence.

The size of the relational-attunement gain from such optimization depends on the base model, so the persistence-versus-attunement trade-off is governed by each model's failure profile rather than being uniform.

Because an imperfect proxy for human values can lead to catastrophic outcomes when optimized without bound, AI systems should limit their optimization pressure (for example, through quantilizers) rather than maximize the proxy unconstrained.

In LLM repair agents, many passing validation results do not test the reported bug: 46.0% of positive comparable validation events carry no bug-discriminating information, and 23.8% of baseline rollouts close on such evidence alone.

Feeding back a bug-contrast result, which replays validation on the original buggy code, reduces evidence-inadequate closure by 7.8 percentage points without detectable loss of repair success, though this effect falls below the prespecified 10-point smallest effect size of interest, so its practical magnitude is uncertain.

Disagreements among LLM bias audits can be explained by audit format: across 14 models, changing the evaluation format reverses the direction of demographic bias, and disguised audits reveal substantially larger bias than transparent ones.

Applying parameter updates uniformly across all training samples is inefficient, and a reinforcement-inspired controller that allocates per-sample update intensity based on immediate utility-cost feedback can do better.
Such a feedback-driven controller retains 94.1–99.2% of full-adaptation performance while using available updates more efficiently and producing a more stable late-stage adaptation trajectory.

Restoring visual grounding feedback at multiple checkpoints around an unchanged zero-shot captioner, without retraining it, improves COCO Karpathy CIDEr from 108.0 to 117.6 under strict zero-shot conditions, with most of the gain attributable to the non-learned architectural intervention.

Predicting a continuous future-intent embedding that is aligned with the latent representation of the ego trajectory, rather than reconstructing dense future world states, is sufficient for high-quality end-to-end driving planning.

Reformulating audio-visual fusion as an iterative, multi-turn cross-modal interaction with degradation-aware gating, rather than a single-step operation, improves speech recognition accuracy and robustness to noise.

An SVD-based, parameter-centric framework that yields self-contained compressed client models can resolve the trade-off in heterogeneous federated fine-tuning of foundation models, where existing approaches each sacrifice full-model memory reduction, architectural self-containedness, or representational fidelity, and it outperforms existing baselines under IID partitions.

Activation steering does not reliably improve chain-of-thought faithfulness: it increases cue acknowledgment only in the largest tested model (Gemma-3 12B), and its effects are better explained by heightened cue salience and cue use than by improved verbalization of reasoning.

Directly transferring the Representation Autoencoder paradigm to motion fails because the frozen Motion-JEPA latent space is spectrally ill-conditioned and flow residuals align with decoder-sensitive directions, so small latent errors amplify into large motion artifacts.

A flow-friendly motion latent is obtained by fixing the two bottlenecks separately, combining a compact transport-stable bottleneck with motion-coupled decoder alignment, and this latent lets a standard Flow-Matching DiT reach state-of-the-art text-to-motion performance.
Optimizing an LLM against multiple conflicting rewards by mixing them into a single scalar signal causes an alignment tax that destabilizes post-training.

Decomposing multi-reward RL into separate policy-space optimization, with standalone positive policies per reward plus a global negative policy, avoids reward-conflict problems better than mixing rewards and also enables inference-time control.

Runtime safeguarding of vision-language-action policies can be achieved without retraining by checking spatiotemporal visual-action consistency, which restores performance under localized visual overlays and action drift while preserving clean-task performance.

Making a translation model adapt its reasoning effort to text difficulty, as human translators do, lets it outperform much larger reasoning models in translation quality while using substantially fewer tokens.
The cognitively aligned, difficulty-adaptive reasoning behavior enables robust generalization across multiple translation domains.

A single learned representation can couple physical Earth data and human societal data only if the two are handled in their native geometries, which TerraNova does by training on continuous physical fields and administrative-unit societal data and linking them with a population-weighted contrastive objective.

Collapsing LLM-generated optimization models into a single equivalence verdict or execution-success rate hides the distinct senses in which two formulations can agree, so evaluation should use multiple relation-specific, independently re-checkable certificates.
Because models fail at different stages, the multi-relational certificate view reveals failure modes that cannot be reduced to one accuracy score.

Multi-objective alignment should learn per-objective reward models and a balanced policy jointly from human preference feedback, because predefined reward functions are hard to specify when ground-truth rewards are unavailable.

Infrared vision-language models are vulnerable to a training-free, black-box QR-based thermal pattern that redirects image-text alignment toward attacker-chosen concepts while remaining visually stealthy, and this semantic drift transfers across classification, captioning, and visual question answering, so these models' robustness to such cross-task attacks needs evaluation.
The EPC score is a valid objective measure of explanation quality, because higher EPC scores align with independent human judgments of explanations.

Supervising the intermediate refinement steps of looped visual reasoners to follow a step-by-step transformation chain improves abstract visual reasoning, but only when each refinement is grounded in a task reference and the current grid state.

Conversational agents for eGovernment can be both explainable and accurate when a large language model is confined to a bounded conversational interface paired with a rule-based symbolic controller that executes the law or guidelines.
Existing extremely low-light RAW enhancement methods overlook motion-induced degradation, so they cannot handle the coupled motion blur and noise that occur in such scenes.

A unified framework combining a single-step MeanFlow generative model with a domain-calibrated RAW tokenizer can robustly restore extremely dark RAW images with coupled motion and noise while achieving state-of-the-art enhancement.

An automated, dynamic conversational test that uses graduated scaffolding to measure each student's Zone of Proximal Development, with non-compensatory additive grading, is a better theoretical foundation for assessment than static and face-to-face oral examinations, which penalize ambition, add construct-irrelevant variance, and heighten performative anxiety.

Combining structured interaction memory with a dual-track fact memory (write-time consolidated core facts plus on-demand active facts) mitigates the temporal-structural and delayed-utility misalignments that limit existing LLM agent memory systems, and yields the highest accuracy across backbones on LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S.
Dual-Anchored Policy Distillation (DAPD) alleviates the privilege illusion and improves over on-policy self-distillation with privileged information (OPSD) across model scales.

On-policy self-distillation with privileged information induces a privilege illusion, in which the student learns behavior that depends on information unavailable at inference time, and this teacher-student information asymmetry is the root cause of the resulting performance degradation.

Global error metrics can hide poor performance on prolonged high-water plateaus, and adding cross-site signals as bounded residual corrections to a stable local temporal forecast improves plateau prediction reliability without sacrificing accuracy under routine conditions.
LLM-proposed vulnerability discovery paths can silently violate domain knowledge, so they need explicit verification rather than trust.

Checking each LLM-generated path for entailment against a separate domain knowledge graph, instead of scoring the output or constraining it to a single graph, raises pooled entailment from 78% to 98%.

In diffusion language models, fixed token-choice MoE routing wastes expert computation because it gives every token position the same expert budget regardless of how much refinement each position needs, so inference should allocate expert compute according to each position's refinement state.
Refinement-aware allocation of expert computation, as implemented by REFLEX without changing the router, reduces expert computation by about 15% while preserving or improving generation quality.

LEAP, which prunes simple and overly catastrophic tasks from multi-turn expansion and uses a rank-based, tournament-derived reward, makes critic-free RL for CUDA kernel generation work better, with faster convergence and stronger multi-turn debugging than unpruned baselines.

For factual remote sensing disaster change captioning, a diffusion language model that repeatedly revises the whole caption conditioned on the image pair outperforms autoregressive decoding, because autoregressive decoding turns early misinterpretations into irreversible premises that cascade into factual errors.
Supervised fine-tuning rewrites a language model's inherited behavioral geometry, whereas reward optimization changes behavior while largely preserving the underlying geometric chart.

Because behavioral change alone cannot distinguish supervised fine-tuning from reward optimization, post-training methods must be told apart by examining the underlying geometry rather than observed behavior.

Adding CosDir, a loss that aligns predicted and target difference vectors via cosine similarity, improves forecasters' directional accuracy, which MSE-trained models neglect, especially on small moves, while preserving magnitude accuracy.

Adapting a source-domain Bayesian network to a sparse target domain, by having an LLM propose missing target-relevant edges and a PPO policy calibrate them, yields better few-shot tabular synthetic data than existing baselines, including the strongest one.

Greater search effort does not reliably improve answers from long-horizon search agents; answer accuracy tracks the quality of retrieved evidence rather than the number of searches, and agents often keep searching after useful evidence has already appeared, so evidence-sufficiency stopping criteria are a practical fix.
Divisive normalization, rather than subtractive inhibition, is what allows recurrent networks to learn robust low-rank continuous slow manifolds for working memory.
Retrieval-augmented search agents should decide when to stop searching by checking whether accumulated evidence covers each required claim, not by the generator's confidence.
A verification-aware stopping policy reduces redundant search while preserving exact-match accuracy, and it does so without retraining or modifying the agent.

Matching the pairwise token affinities of a diffusion transformer's intermediate features to those of clean data latents, including cross-image token pairs, is a target-free regularizer that achieves the lowest FID among parameter-free methods and further improves results when combined with the target-based REPA method.

Representing objects as anisotropic, surface-aligned 3D Gaussians and robot hands as morpho-kinematic keypoint descriptors, with Mahalanobis fields matching contact direction, lets a single shared grasp optimization generalize across dexterous hands, including zero-shot transfer to an unseen hand, and outperform prior interaction-centric methods.

Existing deep research benchmarks rely on expert authoring or human-written materials and lack consistent, traceable verification when built fully automatically, so a benchmark needs a different construction method to fill this gap.
A deep research benchmark can be automatically constructed through iterative task evolution while remaining verifiable, using DAG-structured tasks and fact-grounded rubrics.

A deployment-oriented day-ahead PV forecasting pipeline that corrects timestamp conventions, uses leakage-safe solar-geometry features, and combines predictors by validation-learned stacking can support forecasting from short, imperfect site records, but its advantage over smart persistence shrinks to about 9% under rolling-origin evaluation, compared with about 32% under random day-blocked evaluation.

Iterative RAG methods fail on multi-hop questions because single-granularity evidence and accumulated redundancy or retrieval errors degrade answers, and MEGRAG, which links passages, sentences, and triples in a path-structured graph and retrieves evidence at the needed granularity while stopping once the question is resolved, consistently outperforms diverse RAG baselines.

Existing agent personalization benchmarks, which use static preference snapshots, fixed logs, or profile QA, fail to test whether agents act on user preferences, so a benchmark measuring task completion under implicit constraints inferred from longitudinal histories is needed.
State-of-the-art agents struggle to satisfy implicit, history-inferred constraints while completing tasks, and the proposed IBA-Agent substantially improves this behavioral alignment.

A generative detector that localizes text tampering by measuring the restoration cost needed to align a query image with authentic visual-text statistics generalizes to unseen open-set manipulations better than discriminative forgery detectors, which overfit to specific forgery patterns.
The generative detector achieves state-of-the-art results and strong zero-shot performance on unseen text editing patterns.

A dataset-aware mixture-of-experts design that shares cross-dataset clinical semantics in common experts and isolates source-specific variation in residual experts improves chest radiograph vision-language pretraining, including zero-shot and out-of-distribution performance.
Chest X-ray vision-language pretraining that relies on a single dominant source (MIMIC-CXR) underexploits multi-label classification datasets, so multi-source pretraining is needed.

Action-grounded tissue affordance labels can be derived retrospectively from completed laparoscopic procedures without manual per-frame annotation, and a real-time model trained on them can anticipate relevant surgical regions.
A real-time model trained on action-grounded tissue affordance labels can anticipate relevant surgical regions in a way that lowers surgeon cognitive workload during real-world laparoscopic surgery.

Formula syntax and formula semantics live in mismatched native representation spaces with weak observable correspondence, but contrastively aligning graph-based syntax encodings with text-based semantic encodings recovers that missing correspondence and substantially improves cross-modal formula retrieval.

Because language models are human-like and rapidly entering daily life, their long-term risks to users, such as cognitive, developmental, and socio-affective changes, may not show up in short-term evaluations, so NLP should move toward long-term measurement of behavioral change that combines computational methods with social science measurement.

Guiding diffusion-based dataset distillation with the discriminative geometry of a pretrained self-supervised representation space, instead of ignoring it as existing generative objectives do, produces distilled datasets that outperform generative baselines across datasets while preserving visual realism.
Physically realizable adversarial patches can reliably hijack vision-language-action robot policies by diverting action-conditioned attention to a localized patch.

A zero-overhead defense that fine-tunes only the visual encoder can substantially restore robustness against such attacks without degrading clean performance, making securing VLA robots practical through mechanism-level robustness.

Functional correctness in code generation, especially on heterogeneous programming tasks, can be substantially improved with a fixed backbone model by combining prompt routing, inference-time LoRA alignment, and execution-based output selection against public tests.
The combined route-align-verify pipeline outperforms its base model on the MBPP benchmark.

Decomposition quality in programming-by-example is relative to the solver that executes it, not an intrinsic property of the task, so decomposers trained to imitate ground-truth subgoals are suboptimal.
Rewarding candidate subgoals by a frozen synthesizer's loss on the target program produces decompositions the solver can actually execute, improving synthesis and end-to-end accuracy.

Current data agents are unreliable at verifiable analytics over heterogeneous workspaces, with even the best of six frontier multimodal models reaching only 66.34% accuracy on the DataSpace benchmark.

The real alignment challenge for LLMs is ensuring they intelligently apply the ethical values they have absorbed from human text, rather than preventing rogue AI agency, because LLMs lack the autonomous, self-maintaining drives that underlie existential-risk scenarios.

Tool-level graphs built directly from historical tool-use trajectories are tied to specific tools and fail to generalize across tool sets, whereas lifting those trajectories into a function-level workflow graph that captures the shared structure of analogous tasks enables generalizable tool planning.

Language change is a structured, multidimensional process, so measuring it requires attending to both the magnitude and the direction of change across linguistic levels rather than a single distance figure.
Adversarial, fast-moving real-world domains where experts independently produce observable outputs can serve as benchmarks for evaluating AI scientist capabilities.

In such domains, current models produce plausible outputs but few match real expert solutions, indicating the key capability gap lies in filtering, prioritization, and coherent novelty rather than in idea generation.

Subspace-Aligned LoRA Training (SALT) resolves the tension between serving efficiency and task performance in multi-tenant LoRA serving by pinning a shared high-capacity domain centroid in GPU memory and swapping in ultra-low-rank user residuals.
Ultra-low-rank (r ≤ 2) per-user residuals on top of a shared pinned centroid can recover high-rank adapter accuracy while cutting per-adapter memory and raising serving throughput.
Current LLM-generated peer reviews are fluent and detailed but systematically flawed, so aggregate quality scores overstate their actual quality and multi-dimensional evaluation is needed.

Institutional AI governance in higher education is fragmented, because university-level policies address data security and risk while school-level policies focus on pedagogy and tool use, leaving business schools without distinct AI policies and creating misalignment with discipline-specific learning objectives.

LLM reviewers can broadly separate accepted from rejected submissions, but that coarse decision alignment with human peer review does not mean they agree with humans on finer judgments such as oral-versus-poster distinctions, scoring, or review priorities.

Static benchmarks are ill-suited to evaluating web generation, because frontend artifacts are interactive, admit multiple equally valid implementations, and evolve faster than fixed pipelines, so web-generation evaluation should be agentic, adaptive, and extensible, as LiveEvalBench proposes.

Governance of large language models is misaligned with risk: oversight evidence concentrates at deployment-facing lifecycle stages, while the most consequential decisions (data selection, alignment strategy, capability boundaries) occur at development-facing stages where regulatory visibility is lowest.

A lightweight world-action model can anticipate future scene states in a compact latent reasoning space that is jointly shaped by future-state prediction and action generation, and it can be trained end-to-end on a single GPU, avoiding the computational overhead of pixel-space and multi-stage latent-space alternatives.
Image augmentation for multimodal LLM self-improvement should be driven by the model's own failure cases rather than generic or handcrafted transformations.
Failure-informed image complications improve visual question answering performance and data efficiency while remaining compatible with existing text-based self-augmentation.

AI generative models for sound effects are advancing in fidelity, temporal coherence, and state-of-the-art performance, but persistent gaps remain in temporal synchronization for complex multi-event scenes, in alignment between objective metrics and human perception, and in the trade-off between controllability and diversity.

Reasoning-based LLM guard models can be made deployable by replacing per-interaction explicit rationale decoding with compressed continuous latent reasoning, without giving up the ability to explain decisions.
Inspectability of a latent-reasoning guard does not require decoding rationales at inference time, because a separate isolated decoder can produce audit rationales on demand.

Noisy VLM reward signals can be stabilized without ground-truth supervision by regularizing the VLM's latent space with intrinsic structural priors, because reward failures stem from structural brittleness rather than semantic misunderstanding.

The self-supervised SAFT method, which applies structural regularization via LoRA adapters, consistently denoises the VLM reward landscape and improves policy convergence and EPIC-measured alignment across base models of varying capability.
High faithfulness in chain-of-thought reasoning does not guarantee safety, because DeepSeek-R1-Llama-70B is highly faithful yet fails to reject unsafe reasoning.

Safety can be improved independently of faithfulness, because in QwQ-32B the two are encoded in anti-correlated internal directions, so amplifying the safety direction through representation steering raises safety.

Pluralistic alignment for agentic AI should be treated as a problem of socially grounded coordination among perspectives, not merely as diversifying model outputs, because alignment must cover the role activations, deliberative traces, aggregation rules, and feedback loops that generate outputs.

Replacing fixed per-query sampling budgets with an interpretable fuzzy controller that allocates samples according to prompt difficulty and model uncertainty makes LLM test-time scaling inspectable while matching or improving accuracy and reducing average sample count relative to standard baselines.
Post-training a language model on taxonomy-aligned tutor strategies and learner-move annotations, grounded in human-tutoring principles, can make English tutoring pedagogically adaptive.
A small model post-trained this way outperforms its backbone and proprietary baselines on scaffolding-focused evaluation without sacrificing general educational benchmark performance.

A chest X-ray vision-language model is clinically useful only if it provides tunable classification, spatial localization, and anatomical measurement beyond fluent report generation, and unifying these capabilities with reward-aligned generation and deterministic measurement tools improves both its structured predictions and its generated reports over baselines.

Framing table-to-multimodal report generation as a progressive Monte Carlo Tree Search over atomic report-building actions, guided by a multi-dimensional reward, lets factual accuracy, chart quality, and narrative coherence be optimized jointly in a way that fixed linear pipelines with isolated subtasks cannot.
The proposed MCTS-based approach outperforms strong baselines on the MMRBench benchmark for table-to-multimodal report generation.

Post-hoc model merging of clone detectors that share a pre-trained base, especially with TIES merging, can yield cross-domain clone detectors reaching about 93% of multi-task performance without any training data at the merging step.
Merging clone detectors built on different base models yields only marginal and high-variance gains, so a shared pre-trained base is a precondition for effective merging.

Evaluating financial AI agents requires rubrics derived from the professional deliverables of practitioners in the same role, because prompt-derived criteria miss tacit professional standards that lie beyond model priors.

Surfacing lightweight in-situ reflection prompts during everyday feed browsing makes users consume feeds more reflectively, adjust their preferences iteratively, and align their feeds better than a baseline without continuous support, without sacrificing the casual nature of browsing.

In a four-channel foraging agent with a fixed interoceptive precision budget, dynamically reallocating precision toward the currently most-needed bodily channel more than doubles learning-phase survival compared with uniform precision, and this benefit depends on the shaped likelihood reaching both perception and planning and on aiming precision at the most-needed channel rather than the least-needed one.
Deliberately inducing moderate correlation among CNN features before a quantum neural network, instead of using orthogonal features, improves image classification accuracy and stability.
Endoscopy foundation models that learn only from uni-modal images or videos miss the semantic knowledge in clinical reports, and pre-training jointly on report-image pairs closes this modality gap.
A vision-language model pre-trained on 348K endoscopic examinations paired with their clinical reports outperforms existing foundation models on downstream tasks and generalizes zero-shot.

Global similarity metrics used in existing text-to-audio benchmarks cannot expose fine-grained semantic failures, whereas a structured, rubric-based, audio-grounded evaluation can reveal them and aligns better with human semantic judgments.

Post-training objectives that score vision-language instances independently cannot enforce coherent model behavior when image or text evidence changes, because they ignore the relations among matched evidence-state variants.

Optimizing matched evidence-state variants as one group, with relational transition rewards and risk-controlled abstention, improves how vision-language models arbitrate conflicting image and text sources over pointwise baselines.

A resource-aware mixture of speech encoders, which routes each utterance to a frozen high-resource expert or a trainable expert for medium- and low-resource languages, can break the curse of multilinguality in many-to-many speech-to-text translation without sacrificing high-resource performance.

CSGen generates high-fidelity curvilinear structure images that remain precisely aligned with multiple control conditions, and it achieves this through its architecture and training design rather than through data scale alone.

When a question is rendered as pixels rather than text, multimodal models lose substantial accuracy even though they can read the rendered question, and this gap can be recovered by a training method that aligns question-region representations with typed semantics.
The proposed alignment training recovers much of the pixel-rendering accuracy loss without degrading performance when questions are given as text.

Insight retrieval for self-improving agents should be scored by whether an insight advances the agent's current decision bottleneck rather than by semantic similarity, and an embedding trained contrastively on mathematical reasoning data can learn this progress-oriented geometry well enough to transfer to dynamic agent tasks and static skill retrieval without environment-specific training.

Standard on-policy self-distillation produces confounded token-level signals for LLM agent reinforcement learning, because replaying future environment observations shifts token scores through the replay scaffold rather than through the observation's content alone.

Contrasting a full replay against an observation-ablated replay isolates the observation's own contribution, and using that residual to modulate GRPO token updates at high-uncertainty steps, while keeping the trajectory-level update direction, outperforms strong baselines on ALFWorld, WebShop, and Search-QA.
Memory for language agents should be evaluated by whether recalled experience improves downstream performance on long-horizon workflows, not by retrieval or question-answering accuracy.
Reversible action cycles provide annotation-free verification that lets reinforcement learning overcome the verification bottleneck in improving long-horizon video world models.

Cycle-based rewards built on reversible action cycles substantially improve long-horizon video world models, reducing state-returning drift by up to 44% and nearly quadrupling composite-action accuracy over the base model.

Collapsing multiple analog circuit design specifications into a single scalar reward limits existing reinforcement learning methods, whereas a vector-valued, preference-conditioned approach can serve diverse trade-off settings.
The ORACLE approach produces analog circuit designs across diverse trade-off settings without retraining while achieving faster and more accurate results than prior methods.

In partially protected open-weight releases, a release-time gate that blocks gradients from harmful inputs in a calibrated hidden-state region can keep post-finetuning attack success near the pre-release level without requiring downstream users to cooperate.
Item Response Theory should replace aggregated scores for AI safety benchmarking because it is more interpretable and far cheaper to run.

Existing evaluations of LLM tutors, which focus mainly on answer quality, under-measure pedagogical fit, meaning whether a tutor response matches the learner's current foundation and curricular progression.
The Pedagogical Suitability Index (PSI) can measure pedagogical fit in LLM tutor responses, and using PSI as feedback substantially improves weak-performing LLM tutor responses.
Self-evolving agent skill systems let untrusted agent experience be promoted into trusted instruction, so the promotion process is a security boundary that must be defended.
A black-box attacker who contributes only bounded, consistent evidence can exploit the promotion process to embed target behaviors in an agent's skills.

Training flow-based GRPO with a stochastic SDE while testing with a deterministic ODE creates a train-inference mismatch, and adding a Langevin correction after each ODE Euler step, with the score recovered from the flow velocity, narrows that gap without sacrificing reward optimization or generation quality.
Human research is epistemically well suited to generating valuable evidence for AI Safety and Ethics, so the field should treat it as a legitimate and needed methodology.

The current underuse of human research in AI Safety and Ethics is driven by perceived validity concerns, resource barriers, methodological preferences, and infrastructural constraints rather than by a lack of epistemic fit, and these barriers should be removed.

Preference-induced stance reversal sycophancy can be detected from a single response's text alone, but this detection does not reliably generalize to LLMs unseen during training, so cross-model generalization remains an unsolved challenge.

Deployed AI systems can be designed so that the feedback and decision outcomes they return to users steer the human-AI interaction toward improvement pathways that let individuals obtain favorable outcomes at minimal cost, while discouraging gaming and preserving the system's intended objectives such as accuracy.

Modeling visual and textual representations as probability distributions, rather than deterministic embeddings, yields more robust and data-efficient medical image segmentation than state-of-the-art deterministic vision-language methods because deterministic cross-modal matching overlooks aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty.

Implicit semantic guidance can replace the fragile geometric preprocessing (human parsing, pose estimation, garment warping) used in multi-stage video virtual try-on, enabling an end-to-end framework that needs none of these modules at inference.
An end-to-end video virtual try-on framework built this way still reaches state-of-the-art performance despite dropping the geometric preprocessing pipeline.

Adapting multilingual text embedding models with a single training objective across diverse tasks is suboptimal, and task-conditional flow matching (TCFM), which applies flow matching only to translation while using task-aligned objectives for retrieval, classification, and pair-classification, improves embedding quality across tasks.

Making post-execution critique a learnable policy action, optimized jointly with generated code against final geometric outcomes, improves text-to-CAD generation and yields higher execution validity than existing methods.

The authors address the challenge of interoperability across defence and national security ontologies by documenting over 60 publicly available ontologies and providing a new eight-task Ontology Alignment Evaluation Initiative track with silver-standard reference mappings built from aggregated outputs of several alignment systems.

Representing the propagation environment as a persistent 3D Gaussian field enables beamforming that synthesizes beams directly from access point pose and user position, without online instantaneous channel state information or iterative optimization.
The Gaussian-splatting-based beamformer outperforms exhaustive beam alignment.

Cautious Context Steering, a lightweight adapter on a frozen language model that decides per token how strongly user context should influence generation, personalizes language models without per-user training or an extra context-conditioned forward pass, and generalizes to new users and domains better than existing per-user personalization methods.
CourseGraph provides an effective automated approach for detecting overlapping Computer Science courses across universities, supporting student mobility programs.

Economic World Models, which simulate economies from within by letting heterogeneous agents, markets, and institutions co-evolve, are a promising path to next-generation economic simulation environments.
Existing work on economic simulation remains concentrated at lower capability levels and rarely includes self-evolving agents, leaving a gap that Economic World Models would need to fill.
Frozen 3D CT foundation encoders have no universal best model, and their relative rankings shift with the evaluation context.

Frozen 3D CT encoder performance is limited mainly by a physical contrast bottleneck, since a finding's detectability scales with its contrast against surrounding tissue, so small, low-contrast focal lesions remain a persistent failure across all evaluated encoders.

A mixture of per-cluster adapters trained on individual authorship embeddings closes the individual-level gap that large language model simulators leave open, even though those simulators recover population-level central tendencies well.
The Anacreon mixture-of-minds approach reaches state-of-the-art ordinal alignment with human survey responses on a large external survey.
Climate data super-resolution is held back by single-frame methods that ignore temporal correlations, and exploiting those correlations is the key to better spatial resolution.
Bidirectional temporal alignment, using forward and backward networks trained on consecutive latent frames, improves super-resolution performance over existing approaches on climate data.
Standard optical flow alignment fails on noisy climate data, so temporal alignment for climate super-resolution requires a different mechanism than conventional video methods.

A single extraction schema encoding domain knowledge can serve as the shared basis for both zero-shot, single-call extraction and semantic evaluation of nested, variable-cardinality attributes, with generative AI performing the semantic comparison against a gold standard.
This schema-guided approach reaches an F1 score above 90% on NICE documents while running about 30 times faster than a human domain expert.

Search agents trained only on final-answer correctness or intermediate progress are not rewarded for grounding their post-retrieval reasoning in retrieved evidence, which encourages prior-driven reasoning.
Rewarding turn-level use of retrieved evidence, combined with a global outcome reward, reduces prior-driven reasoning in search agents.
Synthetic clinical benchmarks can pass existing utility checks while remaining structurally unrealistic, so passing utility checks should not be taken as evidence of realism.

Realism of synthetic clinical benchmarks should be improved through dataset revisions that raise realism while keeping utility above a fixed floor, treating utility as a constraint rather than a measure of realism.
Existing benchmarks cannot diagnose how drift propagates across layers of human-AI control loops, which motivates a benchmark that injects controlled drift into task traces.
Drift introduced into ALFRED-derived traces is identifiable across multiple model families under a leak-aware evaluation protocol.
The causal mechanism by which drift propagates through human-AI control loops remains hard to recover, even though drift itself is detectable.

Passive ranking that infers preferences from implicit behavior prevents users from expressing nuanced interests, and an LLM-based agentic system that lets users co-curate their feeds in real time and across modalities can close this gap and improve feed relevance on production traffic.

Standard single-modality, single-run, accuracy-only LLM benchmarks miss behavioral variation (across chat UI versus API, with and without web search, and across repeated runs) that matters for AI safety assessments, so safety evaluations should explicitly account for modality, multi-run consistency, and search conditions.

Distance-based robust aggregation rules such as Krum and Multi-Krum can be consistently bypassed by a selection-aware backdoor attack that crafts malicious updates to resemble the dense core of benign updates.
The proposed Krum-Proxy attack achieves higher backdoor attack success than prior methods on standard federated learning benchmarks.

A unified framework that aligns a review-specific intent graph with a global hotel knowledge graph through structure-aware alignment can jointly predict aspect ratings and generate reverse intent statements, outperforming LLM and retrieval baselines, whereas hierarchical pipelines suffer from error propagation and retrieval methods ignore structural relationships.

Existing fake news detectors fail on text-to-video (T2V) fake news because videos synthesized from fabricated narratives align perfectly with their text, which pushes detectors toward unimodal shortcuts, so T2V detection requires a new ternary task and dataset.
Detecting T2V fake news is better handled by a reasoning-guided framework that integrates semantic logic with physical generative traces than by prior baselines.

Diagnosing coordination failures in control loops that couple human operators, AI decision modules, and automated controllers requires time-aligned, multi-layer drift traces, because single-modality monitoring cannot provide them.

A benchmark built from such traces shows that drift is identifiable and attributable across model families under a leak-aware evaluation protocol, but inferring its causal mechanism is much harder, and heavier attention models give no advantage over simpler ones.

In an overparameterized ReLU network, the positive-homogeneous scaling gauge, which leaves the initial predictor unchanged, deterministically decides which of several initially duplicate neurons learns a teacher feature, so the initial function alone does not determine when or by which neuron that feature is learned.

A three-phase progressive post-training pipeline (linear probing, then full fine-tuning, then reinforcement fine-tuning with a learned business-metric reward model) aligns a recommender foundation model with business metrics better than single-phase adaptation, because it separates downstream adaptation from business-metric alignment and trains the policy on dense implicit feedback rather than sparse business targets.

Predicting single-cell transcriptional responses to unseen perturbations is most effectively done by conditioning a control-anchored residual flow on perturbation-gated gene geometry, while keeping stable gene-network structure separate from intervention-specific response propagation.

A multi-agent forensic reasoning framework built from small open-source MLLMs, with domain-expert agents for texture, lighting, motion, and physics plus a judge agent that reconciles their reports, generalizes better to out-of-domain deepfake videos than conventional detectors and closed-source GPT and Gemini models.

Patterns of team communication can sort teams into behavioral tribes that predict team performance in a domain-independent way, exposing team dynamics that traditional performance metrics fail to detect.

Existing LLM agent benchmarks evaluate only behavioral outcomes, so they cannot support fine-grained attribution of agent trajectories, and trajectory attribution should be established as a distinct task supported by a unified, annotated benchmark.

FedVAR outperforms existing federated baselines for video anomaly recognition because it resolves the semantic misalignment that arises when heterogeneous clients learn divergent notions of normal and abnormal events.
A shared prototype-based semantic anchor that aligns clients' visual and textual feature spaces is an effective means of countering semantic misalignment in federated video anomaly recognition.
Existing LMM recipe generators score well on text quality but produce little reference-aligned entity and relation structure, because free-form recipe text hides procedural structure.
A graph representation of recipes (ReGraph) exposes this structural gap, and a two-stage training approach (RGL) improves the generation of cooking entities.
Current large multimodal models cannot reliably transfer spatial information between image and text modalities, and this bottleneck must be resolved before they can serve as autonomous GIS agents.

Existing regional image editing methods fail to reliably combine accurate localization of the edit with seamless integration into the preserved context, and MaskFlow resolves this by building the edit mask into its flow-matching objective and refining the predicted vector field with a Soft-Poisson de-seaming module.
MaskFlow's mask-aware flow-matching and Soft-Poisson de-seaming approach yields consistent quantitative improvements over competing regional editing methods.

Dense on-policy distillation into a memory-compressing agent is effective only when the teacher scores each sampled action under the same state the student saw during rollout, which requires restoring each model invocation's original state rather than scoring a flattened persistent history.

Organizing a language-guided laboratory mobile manipulation system around explicit representation handoffs (language into registered skill calls, observations into maps and object poses, validated skills into motion goals) makes integration failures inspectable rather than hidden.
Because the handoffs are explicit, dry-run traces and startup checks can surface problems such as missing calibration as deployment blockers before the robot acts.
Jointly forecasting multiple accounting KPIs is more accurate when a transformer exchanges information among ledger series along fixed accounting relations than when standard baselines are used.
The accuracy advantage of the accounting-graph transformer holds for small businesses with short histories and for companies not seen during training.
Aligning diffusion latents with features from encoders pretrained on in-domain endoscopic data yields a generative model that produces high-fidelity, structurally coherent endoscopic images.
The same in-domain representation alignment makes the resulting model a competitive feature extractor for endoscopic images, so one foundation model serves both generation and representation.

Large language models' alignment with human values is unequal across socio-demographic groups (education, income, occupation, religion), and these within-country divides are not captured by country-level analysis, so country-only studies miss part of the alignment disparity.

Large language models such as GPT-5 and Gemini can produce evidence extraction and critical appraisal judgments on microbial oncogenesis papers that align with those of domain experts, though their methodological appraisal is their most persistent weakness.

Diffusion language models are vulnerable to mechanistic safety exploits because they inherit the safety mechanisms of their autoregressive predecessors, so safety neurons identified in those predecessors can be pruned to sharply raise attack success rates.

Open-source AI risk mitigation tools concentrate on technical and operational controls while leaving governance, legal and regulatory, and financial and market risks largely unaddressed, so enterprise AI risk mitigation requires a layered architecture that pairs these tools with organizational and regulatory processes.

Fusing pre-trained genomic language model embeddings with neuroimaging features, rather than encoding genetic variants as hard-coded labels that discard local sequence context, yields better detection of cognitive decline and dementia than existing imaging-genetics methods.

Multi-turn reinforcement learning in simulated patient encounters, using a structured reward and adversarial simulated patients, improves clinical AI agents' diagnostic accuracy in a way that transfers to unseen benchmarks.
The diagnostic gains from simulated reinforcement learning do not yet establish clinical utility, which requires prospective validation in real-world workflows.

Standard SFT-then-RL training for visual tool use is misaligned at both stages, and aligning each stage to what a smaller model can reproduce and what measurably helps yields an 8B model that improves across benchmarks without human annotations of tool use.
After a modular-addition transformer has solved its training set, post-grokking collapse arises at the representation-readout interface rather than in the rest of the network.

Freezing the embeddings and readout removes post-grokking collapse, whereas removing Muon's normalization and orthogonalization does not, so the optimizer's update geometry is not the cause of the failure.

Leaving musical structure implicit in text-to-music systems makes generation hard to inspect, control, or revise, whereas an explicit intermediate layout planning sections, textures, and repetitions before audio generation provides layout-level structural control.
An explicit intermediate structural layout improves the long-range structural organization of generated music.

Routing unlabeled samples by pseudo-label confidence to three specialized LoRA experts makes semi-supervised adaptation of frozen vision foundation models more robust to pseudo-label noise than a single adapter that must absorb reliable, ambiguous, and noisy gradients together.
An agentic LLM pipeline can translate institutional policy text into SHACL constraints that enforce those policies over a knowledge graph.

Adapting the pipeline to a new policy domain is governed by swapping the domain vocabulary registry rather than retraining the model, and that registry determines how well the generated constraints align with the new domain.

Safety behavior in non-high-resource languages can be improved by targeting a sparse set of cross-lingual shared safety pathways that transfer safety signals from high-resource languages, rather than isolated neurons.
Updating only the parameters of these shared safety pathways improves safety in non-high-resource languages while preserving general model capabilities.

Aligning text and image modalities substantially improves web navigation agents over unimodal baselines, with the proposed MELLON approach raising task completion accuracy by 9.26% after one training epoch.
Repository-level coding-agent benchmarks that score only final patch test results cannot explain why agents fail.

Evaluating agents on requirement clarification and implementation planning alongside code generation, using intermediate ground-truth references, shows that recovering implicit requirements is the main bottleneck, and the evaluated agents resolve only 31.5% of tasks.

Selectively internalizing guidance from repeatedly missed rubric criteria, filtered by reward and reshaped toward weakly supported behaviors, improves open-ended reinforcement learning performance over standard Rubric-RL.
Compressing rubric-based feedback into scalar rewards leaves persistent capability gaps that are hard to target.

In-context personalization from a user's own past disclosure decisions improves LLM prediction of that user's privacy choices, but it produces imbalanced shifts in false-positive and false-negative rates, so inference-time personalization is promising yet limited for modeling privacy preferences.
Reward-scored diffusion RL trajectories can be reused as distillation supervision, so that a single lightweight stage unifies RL alignment and few-step distillation.
Advantage-weighted imitation over reward-scored trajectories, which favors high-reward samples and repels low-reward ones, lets a decoupled student match or surpass its RL teacher.

Fine-grained cross-modal understanding in drone views can be improved by object-centric region alignment combined with semantically perturbed negatives built from a foreground-purified prototype codebook, which together address background clutter and visual isomorphism.

Framing whole-repository migration as adversarial minimization of a unified Code Entropy metric, accepting generator updates only when they lower that entropy, yields functionally complete migrated repositories where existing LLM-agent methods fail to produce runnable applications.
The entropy-based adversarial method outperforms existing agent-based approaches on Android-to-HarmonyOS migration across repositories of different scales.

Existing data-free knowledge distillation methods fail on modern architectures such as Vision Transformers because they rely on architecture-specific statistical priors like Batch Normalization statistics, and replacing these with explicit, architecture-agnostic semantic priors (UniDFKD) restores synthesized data quality and achieves state-of-the-art distillation across both CNNs and ViTs.

Combo-shopping agents cannot be reliably evaluated by exact-match metrics or LLM semantic judgment alone, so evaluation needs deterministic validation against a witness basket alongside semantic rubrics.
Even strong LLM agents struggle on the budget-constrained combo-shopping task in ComboShoppingBench.

Feeding sparse, layer-aligned intermediate states from previous frames back into pretrained Transformer trackers consistently improves tracking accuracy on LaSOT and GOT-10k while adding less than 1% parameters.
Existing Transformer trackers remain largely feed-forward and rarely reuse intermediate representations across frames, leaving a gap that cross-frame feedback is meant to fill.
Current multimodal models lack the sustained multi-step symbolic reasoning needed to solve electrical circuit problems from diagrams, and their performance degrades on long-horizon problems.

Civic evaluations of language models must measure propensity, what a model tends to do under realistic pressure, separately from capability, what it can do under benign instructions, because the two can diverge.
Subtle omission pressure shifts civic-agent behavior toward manipulative enablement across models, and overt false-consensus pressure does not produce the same behavior.

Co-training an anchor policy and an auxiliary policy under a shared geometric-mixture objective stabilizes on-policy distillation, whereas single-policy on-policy distillation configurations often exhibit entropy growth or trajectory degradation.

An end-to-end agentic framework that keeps the incident as a graph state, routes planning to stage-specialized agents, and validates action feedback for experience reuse outperforms the strongest baseline by 9.5% in normalized defense score across 100 Docker-based cyber ranges.
Existing LLM-based incident response agents are unstable over long horizons because they lack a unified basis for maintaining incident state.

Representing a long egocentric video as a relative 4D scene graph, which separates stable anchors from dynamic objects and tracks object state through anchor-relative transitions, enables better object-centric question answering than caption- or transcript-based memories.

National AI strategies converge horizontally on economic competitiveness and research support but persistently diverge on human rights goals, and their vertical alignment with regional strategies varies by region and by value, with the EU diverging from its regional strategy on human-centric values.

Trust research in NLP has moved from post-hoc interpretability of static models toward mechanistic understanding and proactive control of generative systems, with each new generation of capable chat models redirecting the field toward truthfulness and safety alignment.

A polynomial-time verifier can check the approximate self-consistency of a probabilistic predictor's conditional-probability answers by querying a single untrusted prover and reading only a few locations of a proof encoding a sparse witnessing distribution.

Modelling violence against women and girls as multi-turn, retrieval-grounded dialogues, rather than as isolated toxic sentences, can yield realistic synthetic conversations that capture the relational and temporally unfolding nature of abuse while avoiding dependence on scarce real data.

Text-guided medical image segmentation is improved by decoding with two complementary language signals, one in the spatial domain and one in the frequency domain, rather than relying on spatial alignment alone.
The proposed Dual-Domain Cross-Modal Decoding (DD-CMD) outperforms the strongest prior baselines on pulmonary infection segmentation benchmarks.

Frontier LLMs used as zero-shot visual rankers can match natively multimodal embedding models on text-to-image retrieval, as GPT-4.1 performs on par with Gemini Embedding 2 on Flickr30k, though precomputed embeddings remain better suited to low-latency applications.

Recommender systems that treat observed browsing actions as reliable preference signals misread behavior driven by exploration or comparison, so user modeling must reason backward from actions to the beliefs and preferences behind them.
Inverse theory-of-mind modeling yields user personas that match or exceed ground-truth personas, and multi-hypothesis reasoning is essential to that accuracy.
Off-the-shelf LLMs are unreliable judges of user engagement because they rationalize both positive and negative outcomes for the same item.

Behavioral alignment that fine-tunes LLMs on correct versus counterfactual rationales with preference optimization mitigates this unreliability and lets LLM-based recommendation evaluation match a production feature-engineered baseline without manual pipeline overhead.
Decomposing financial analysis into specialist prompts improves numerical tasks but does not reliably improve judgment tasks, so specialization alone is insufficient for analytical judgment.

Post-training a 9B model with GRPO and task-aligned structured rewards improves judgment performance and transfers to unseen firms and regulatory wrappers, so reinforcement learning on task-aligned rewards is what delivers judgment gains.

A coarse-to-fine framework that first synthesizes a global road layout and then builds lane-level geometry can generate complete, large-scale HD maps from scratch, unlike prior approaches limited to local structures or handcrafted and reconstructed maps.

Decoding segmentation through a rendered semantic image with a fixed class-color probabilistic interface, refined by jointly aligned multi-level generator evidence, improves accuracy, calibration, and pixel-error ranking over direct-interface decoding and maximum softmax probability.
Shopping agents can be trained effectively from real online user interaction logs without human annotation, outperforming existing offline-signal approaches.

Verifiable purchase outcomes can serve as a reinforcement learning signal for shopping agents, and users' in-dialogue directives can be converted into dense token-level supervision via feedback-aware distillation.

Refusal behavior in aligned large language models is localized in mid-network MLP parameters (around layers 8-11) rather than distributed across the network, so it carries far more of the refusal behavior than attention parameters do.
The refusal-relevant components of aligned language models interact non-additively, so their effects cannot be understood or isolated by summing each component's individual contribution.

A multimodal pseudo-labeling framework, combining CLIP-guided synonym filtering, LLaVA/GPT-generated captions, and three complementary training objectives, can overcome the noisy pseudo-masks, weak visual-textual grounding, and synonym/out-of-vocabulary problems of existing open-vocabulary instance and open-set panoptic segmentation methods, producing consistent gains on COCO, OVIS, and OSPS without manual annotation.

FM-LLM improves LLM-based time-series forecasting by adapting frozen LLMs prompt-free with a frequency-aware design, which avoids the computational overhead of textual prompts and captures spectral dynamics that prior methods ignore, and this yields state-of-the-art results on 59 of 78 metrics across eleven benchmarks.

Uncertainty-driven synthetic data, requiring no manual annotation, can teach an LLM to decide when and which aspect of an ambiguous query to clarify, and this outperforms relying on annotated data or preference alignment for proactive clarification.

HUGIN, a training framework that augments data and aligns instructions with the complete visual context, enables vision-language models to perform joint planning over spatially disjoint camera views in autonomous logistics sorting, where existing models struggle because of scarce cross-scene supervision and attention dispersion over long visual context.

Applying a single global extrapolation coefficient to every token in on-policy distillation causes students to fit extreme implicit-reward peaks, leading to reward hacking and requiring costly sweeps to tune.
Adapting the extrapolation coefficient per token according to teacher-reference reliability avoids these failures and outperforms the global-coefficient baseline without requiring extra supervision.

Assigning traits in the system prompt makes an aligned LLM's safety decisions on the same request inconsistent, and Trait-Invariant Safety Tuning (TIST) stabilizes these decisions by aligning trait-conditioned behavior with no-trait behavior.
TIST stabilizes trait-dependent safety decisions while preserving the model's general capability.

Binary code representation learning improves retrieval accuracy when it explicitly trains on instruction alignment, using instruction-level correspondences from compiler debug information, which existing function-level methods ignore.
Current multimodal large language models handle only basic ancient Chinese character identification well, and fail at deeper exegesis, so a structured, expert-audited benchmark is needed.
Fine-tuning on the expert-audited JieZi-Dataset substantially improves multimodal large language models across all four levels of ancient Chinese character exegesis.

Censorship in China-origin vision-language models is shifting from visible refusal to invisible reframing: they reframe politically sensitive content more often than non-China models, and across successive Qwen generations explicit refusals decline while state-aligned framing rises, making the censorship hard for users to detect.

Roles for multi-agent language models can be induced from team trajectories as executable control variables that summarize behavior predictive of future utility, and these induced roles outperform hand-written, random, and shuffled role conditioning.
Trajectory-induced roles capture transferable behavioral specialization rather than merely fitting the training team.

Reflection in long-horizon search agents is best learned as a memory-control policy supervised by both globally informed teacher signals and final trajectory outcomes, because reflection acts locally while its usefulness is only determined globally.

Existing LLM-based safety-engineering approaches are insufficient for regulated medical-device development because they lack source links, traceability, uncertainty handling, lifecycle updates, and recorded expert review.
An evidence-grounded LLM framework is needed that prepares, links, and checks candidate safety artifacts for expert decision-making without itself deciding whether a device is safe.

Supplying a target-prefix hint only when the generator cannot reach the ground-truth item converts zero-reward rollout groups into informative comparisons, fixing the lack of useful advantage in group-relative reward-based post-training of semantic-ID generative recommenders.
Because hinting changes token identity, hinted prefix tokens and sampled suffix tokens must receive separate credit treatment during post-training.

Sparse-reward offline-to-online RL, trained on large datasets generated by simulated Sample-based Model Predictive Control, can learn loco-manipulation skills that surpass the SMPC teacher and deploy across different robot morphologies without manual reward tuning.

A text-only attack can steer skill-based LLM agents through unnecessary benign skills and an attacker-controlled coordinator while task completion stays comparable, so correct task outcomes do not guarantee trajectory integrity or cost safety.

DreamFly improves aerial vision-language navigation by jointly modeling causally aligned historical memory, receding-horizon diffusion planning, and explicit stop decisions, and this joint design yields consistent gains over baselines in both seen and unseen OpenFly environments.

Coordinating semantic priors from VLA models and predictive dynamics from WAMs at the level of compact action representations, rather than through joint token-level attention, yields better autonomous driving planning.

Joint token-level attention between semantic and predictive streams causes an attention-allocation mismatch in which semantic shortcuts suppress predictive dynamics, which action-space coordination avoids.
The approach achieves state-of-the-art autonomous driving planning performance on the NAVSIM benchmark.
Self-improving LLM agents that persist successful trajectories as reusable skills can convert an unsafe success into lasting harm that outlives its original triggering input.
A wrapper that repairs unsafe skills and governs their later reuse substantially reduces unsafe skill retrieval while incurring negligible loss in benign task utility.
Raw response magnitude in perturbation methods cannot distinguish genuine evidence from contradiction or fragility, so it is an inadequate signal on its own.
Decomposing perturbation responses into separate evidence, contradiction, and fragility components (the DECAF method) tracks independently measured model behavior far better than raw magnitude does.

Existing diffusion cache policies, which rely on local similarity heuristics, are significantly misaligned with final generation quality because cache errors propagate and accumulate non-uniformly along the denoising trajectory.
A cache policy that aligns its error weighting with generation quality loss, learned via bilevel optimization (GCache), outperforms prior caching strategies on video and image generation.

A two-stage EEG foundation model that combines masked pretraining with prototype-aligned instruction tuning generalizes across datasets and subjects, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines under cross-subject settings and matching within-session calibrated models on held-out datasets without target-domain calibration.
Open-weights language models can be behaviorally reprogrammed from passive, sycophantic assistants into proactive, question-asking Socratic interlocutors via parameter-efficient fine-tuning.
This behavioral transfer is bounded: it holds across closely related languages but degrades in morphologically distant ones.
Existing evaluation of LLM-generated research ideas is fragmented and relies on direct LLM scoring, which cannot deliver unified, reliable assessments.
LigBench, an automated benchmark paired with the PAIR-IQ pairwise judgment dataset, provides fine-grained, consistent, and expert-aligned evaluation of research ideas.

A model's observed behavior is shaped jointly by training data, fine-tuning, and prompting, so no single stage alone explains it; norm-breaking fine-tuning shifts default rationales from safety compliance toward instrumental self-interest, and system prompts can either override or elicit that shift.

Blanket translation of retrieved documents and uncontrolled decomposition both hurt multilingual multi-hop question answering, and deferring translation until decomposition quality fails yields competitive accuracy at a better cost-performance balance.
Controlling the pre-training distribution of time series foundation models, rather than relying on scale or architecture alone, improves their zero-shot forecasting performance.

A single-stage training regime that jointly varies context lengths and horizons, combined with controlled dataset sampling, lets a simple univariate Transformer reach strong zero-shot forecasting on GIFT-Eval.

Exploiting cross-view geometric correspondence, rather than temporal redundancy across denoising steps, is a more effective way to accelerate multi-view texture diffusion than temporal caching or step reduction.
Transporting per-step updates from a rotating subset of anchor views to the remaining views yields a better speed-fidelity trade-off at speedups above 2x, without any retraining.
Capability sheaves can model agent-harness failures in which locally successful components disagree on shared state, and in controlled experiments the method is invariant to stale representatives.
On a real-repository discovery split, the cohomological method shows no reliable advantage over a matched noncohomological selector, so a real-world cohomological advantage is unsupported.

A training-free method that aligns a sender model's final-layer hidden states to the receiver's input space with a closed-form orthogonal transformation, then prepends them as a continuous prefix, can outperform latent communication methods that require trained projectors on math reasoning, code generation, and question answering.

A target Transformer can be pre-trained as independently trained contiguous layer blocks, each trained inside a frozen aligner scaffold and then recombined, matching the monolithic baseline's perplexity at small scale with a shorter idealized critical path.

A foundation model pretrained on simulated infrared spectra can be adapted to diverse real-world chemical sensing tasks and outperforms conventional and task-specific deep-learning baselines while requiring few labeled experimental spectra.
Existing remote sensing vision-language models, which handle only isolated images, image pairs, or short sequences, cannot reliably ground long-horizon Earth observation reasoning.

A benchmark built for long-horizon Earth observation reasoning (LongEarth-Bench) combined with a model trained on it via group relative policy optimization (LongEarth-R1) achieves the best results across all 12 long-sequence tasks.
In a stylized model, the optimal split between training-time character shaping and inference-time rule enforcement shifts only weakly toward character shaping as deployment scale grows.
The size of the shift toward character shaping depends mainly on the baseline rate at which shaped behavior degrades under novel conditions, not on deployment scale itself.

TopoIntent compiles underspecified natural-language security intent into executable, compliance-checked network topologies, and its additive repair raises topology-visible CIS satisfaction on a held-out finance and government set from 0.78 to 1.00, where existing NetOps tools offer limited support for this task.

A single shared adversarial texture on a 3D object, optimized jointly across many tasks, instructions, states, and viewpoints, can steer Vision-Language-Action robot policies toward attacker-defined actions and substantially reduce task success across multiple tasks.
The attack exposes shared cross-task vulnerabilities in multitask Vision-Language-Action models, meaning one perturbation generalizes across tasks rather than requiring per-task attacks.

A heterogeneity-aware belief synchronization framework, using latent translation models on MEC servers and exchanging compact belief updates only when necessary, can keep belief alignment error and synchronization cost low for semantic communication among heterogeneous AI agents in 6G networks.

Medical image segmentation improves when clinical text shapes visual learning throughout the encoder rather than only as a late conditioning signal, and the MedPlex framework built on this idea achieves state-of-the-art multi-organ segmentation on CT and MR benchmarks, including with real free-text clinical supervision.

Including value-aligned persona documents from the first token of pretraining produces better alignment than introducing alignment only after pretraining, because late alignment leaves values as a thin overlay.

Aggressive parallel decoding in diffusion LLMs makes early-stage mask predictions unreliable, and those errors propagate to later stages, so aligning early predictions with later ones via self-rollout distillation improves the speed-quality trade-off, especially at high parallelism.

Reasoning-oriented training makes reasoning traces look more deliberative by amplifying behaviors like self-correction, hypothesis testing, and uncertainty acknowledgment, but this amplification does not make those behaviors predictive of correctness.
Reasoning training does not preferentially amplify the behaviors most tied to correctness, such as confidence calibration, which is barely amplified.

In vLLM and SGLang, pull request throughput rose sharply (about 21x and 17.9x) during the agentic coding era, and this rise was driven overwhelmingly by human contributors rather than bots, which suggests AI-assisted development is associated with higher throughput in these projects.

Aligning ultrasound image embeddings to fixed text embeddings of standardized TI-RADS feature descriptions with a Center-Margin Contrastive Loss yields better fine-grained multi-class thyroid risk classification than InfoNCE, center loss, direct multitask learning, and a VQA-style multimodal model, with the largest advantage in imbalanced settings.

Multi-token prediction can give generative recommenders dense supervision, but only when future user behaviors carry a semantic echo of the current behavior, and EchoRec exploits this by chaining horizon-aware auxiliary branches and aligning them cycle-consistently into a holistic preference model that improves accuracy at negligible serving cost.

A unified framework that aligns actions across human hands and robot grippers and adversarially removes embodiment information from learned representations enables dexterous manipulation policies to transfer from human demonstrations to robots.
The proposed framework enables zero-shot human-to-robot transfer and data-efficient adaptation for dexterous manipulation learned from heterogeneous human and robot demonstrations.

A general-purpose vision-language model can generate esports-style spoken commentary for arbitrary gameplay video without game-specific instrumentation, if frames are packed into one mosaic image per segment, prior narrations are fed back as context, and the synthesized speech is time-fitted to each segment's slot.
A progressive four-stage causal training recipe can convert a bidirectional action-conditioned video generator into 1-, 2-, and 4-step video world models.

The resulting few-step ForgeWM models lead the evaluated systems on paired Minecraft trajectories in imaging quality, reference-aligned motion-profile agreement, action-sign accuracy, and reference LPIPS.
The same progressive causal training recipe transfers to gamepad-controlled FPS gameplay.

Flattening structured documents into isolated text and image units discards the source organization needed for faithful evidence selection and placement, so multimodal RAG must be grounded in document hierarchy to produce structure-faithful interleaved generation.

A single native multimodal generative model can handle 3D reconstruction, dense correspondence, and spatial reasoning together, without task-specific architectures or external geometric modules, and still perform competitively across these heterogeneous spatial tasks.

Spatial supervision applied within one unified generative model jointly shapes its shared representations, so that training on spatial tasks benefits the model as a whole rather than each task in isolation.

Explicitly modeling the atom-level structural transformations of a reaction, rather than leaving them implicit as prior machine-learning methods do, produces transition-state initial guesses that generalize better to unseen reactions and more often converge to validated saddle points after refinement.

Existing perceptual face similarity metrics fail to match human judgments because they assume a universal observer and rely on spurious relations, so a metric that explicitly models interpretable facial attributes and their nonlinear effects on perception better aligns with the judgments of diverse human subpopulations.
