Interpreting deep spatiotemporal traffic flow models after training cannot reveal their decision process, so interpretability must be built into the architecture itself, as SGSAN does by anchoring attention to a static Directed Dependency Graph.
Anchoring attention to a static Directed Dependency Graph yields traffic flow predictions that are both state-of-the-art in accuracy and transparent in a way aligned with traffic propagation logic.
Large language models can be applied to mmWave radar data for radar-based human perception, showing zero-shot reasoning potential.

A benchmark built by harmonizing heterogeneous public mmWave datasets (mmWave-QA) is a viable way to evaluate language models on radar-based human understanding, and models show robustness under visual degradation.

Weather-driven causal nowcasting can estimate community odour impact from landfill hydrogen sulphide emissions as they unfold, giving public-health authorities a validated, graded trigger to reduce exposure during emission events rather than only after them.

Agents running long-horizon tasks need runtime recovery from errors that have already occurred, because existing methods that prevent errors through plan refinement and safety checks provide little help once an error has happened.
Recovery works by rewinding the agent to aligned checkpoints of both its context and its environment, and the AgentRewind framework implements this approach.
AgentRewind improves task success and checklist progress over baselines across tasks, models, strategies, and harnesses.

SimpleOPD, a tokenizer-agnostic on-policy distillation method that aligns only tokens with identical text spans across tokenizers and adds a student-reference KL loss, can effectively transfer proof-reasoning from a long-context teacher to short-context students.
The distilled gains from SimpleOPD on natural-language math proving extend beyond the math training domain.

Representing research progress as recoverable executable states lets an autoresearch agent overcome its lack of continuity, dead-end recovery, and value-driven compute allocation, and this yields state-of-the-art performance on MLE-bench within a 24-hour budget.

A learned stochastic transition policy, first trained for hard-output MIMO detection and then transferred by parameter cloning into an untied soft-output iterative detection-decoding receiver, can supply the soft information that LDPC decoding needs in high-order MIMO.

A training-free defense that identifies statistically certified safety neurons and clamps them to their harmful-conditional mean activations can trigger the refusal behavior learned during alignment, reducing jailbreak attack success to at most 2.0% while preserving utility.
Existing neuron- and path-level jailbreak defenses are inadequate because they are always-on and significantly compromise model utility.

Participatory moral AI elicitation is not neutral, because developers' upstream choices of which features to vote on, which voters to sample, and how to phrase the question shape the preferences it produces.
Voting-based alignment cannot by aggregation alone deliver fair or transparent AI, since the framing and sampling decisions that precede aggregation determine the outcome.

Because generative AI can produce high-quality products on its own, conventional single-point, product-only assessments lose validity, so assessment should collect continuous, multi-source process evidence of learning over time.
Academic integrity should be secured through assessment design rather than through AI detection.

Explicitly modeling a structured 3D world state, with geometry handled by a fixed renderer and neural synthesis restricted to appearance, makes long-horizon interactive game behaviour controllable and repairable.
This structured approach incurs no detectable fidelity cost, whereas pixel-level autoregressive world models let their structured properties drift over time.
In trusted-monitor ensembles, monitor skill, not decorrelation or shared pretraining lineage, is what determines whether a panel outperforms its best member.
The signal component of monitors' agreement on attack items predicts ensemble gain, whereas the summed agreement metric conventionally used to build panels predicts gain barely at all.

Protein structure prediction has advanced through three methodological transitions: from explicit evolutionary coupling features to learned sequence representations, from monomer folding to heterogeneous molecular systems, and from prediction-oriented inference to design-oriented generative modeling.

Explicitly modeling estimated depth as a spatial structural cue alongside audio and visual features addresses a geometric blind spot in existing audio-visual segmentation methods and yields a 10.2% relative MJ gain over prior state-of-the-art on AVSS.
Explainable AI-generated image detectors should ground their explanations in visually verifiable evidence rather than speculative or hallucinated artifacts.

Defake-o3 demonstrates that grounded explanations are achievable by iteratively zooming into suspicious regions and using a human-annotation-trained verifier that rewards grounded evidence and penalizes baseless claims, improving detection accuracy and yielding more localized evidence.

Output-only distillation from a large video reasoning teacher into a smaller student is insufficient because it misses the latent representations formed during multi-frame reasoning, and adding trajectory-end hidden-state distillation (Latent-OPD) yields consistent gains over output-only on-policy distillation.

Step-level on-policy distillation outperforms both token-level on-policy distillation and supervised fine-tuning because it supervises complete student-generated trajectories, whereas token-level distillation gives only fragmented corrections to erroneous student trajectories.
Supervising complete student-generated trajectories with teacher responses conditioned on those trajectories enables longer-horizon repair of student errors.

Occlusion-aware gating that protects the memory write and residual-fusion paths of an SSM-based temporal model improves temporal stability under heavy occlusion more than merely feeding obstacle masks as auxiliary inputs.

Hallucination detectors that read truthfulness from a single layer or isolated component discard evidence spread across the forward pass, and averaging depth-wise truthfulness signals recovers nearly all linearly accessible truthfulness information and outperforms matched white-box baselines.

Text-to-video generation can correct its own semantic errors without training, by having a multimodal large language model evaluate intermediate preview frames and feed those evaluations back into the diffusion sampling loop to steer the latent trajectory during generation, rather than optimizing before sampling begins.

Foveated multimodal LLMs match humans on visual search outcomes, but their gaze process differs from human search, so outcome and saliency metrics cannot certify that these models search as humans do.

GRPO post-training guided by chain-of-thought reasoning over creator-annotated YouTube chapter boundaries can align large audio-language models to editorial judgment, enabling them to reliably turn unstructured audio into navigable, structured chapters.
Large audio-language models that score well on standard benchmarks nonetheless fail at media audio chapterization.

Embodied AI evaluation needs one continuous trace linking benchmark execution to matched real-robot evidence, with failures attributed to handoff labels that each map to a concrete repair action, because evaluation maturity is inversely aligned with deployment risk across the Physical AI stack.

Pretraining a CNN-GRU model on unlabeled battery cycling data with a cycle-order ranking task yields degradation-aligned representations that support accurate and robust state-of-health estimation after fine-tuning, even when only about 1% of unevenly distributed labels is available.

Framing report-based LLM survival prediction as ordering patients, rather than regressing exact event times, is the better approach because censored outcomes still imply pairwise orderings that concordance-aligned rewards can supervise without exact time targets.
The ranking-based CACSurv model outperforms both prior survival models and LLM time-regression baselines across six TCGA cohorts.

The collective behavior of language-model agent communities follows compact, predictive dynamical laws, and a statistical-mechanics model of agents stochastically favoring lower social pressure predicts their opinion trajectories from initial opinions alone better than standard baselines.

The benefit of natural language explanations in in-context learning is conditional rather than reliable: they often improve classification accuracy, externally generated LLM explanations are strong sources of utility, and faithfulness-based selection of self-generated explanations yields only small, inconsistent gains because the faithfulness metrics disagree substantially.
Multimodal retrieval-augmented generation should model documents as hypergraphs rather than binary graphs, because hyperedges can capture relations among more than two elements at once.
Repairing cross-page semantic fragmentation through targeted refinement around boundary-crossing anchor nodes bridges knowledge gaps more cheaply than full-page reconstruction.

A language model given only a paper's pre-publication bibliography can recover that paper's research idea, and a reference-only multi-agent pipeline with cross-model review and tournament selection raises recovery substantially, to roughly 23-42% across six domains.
Training labeled and unlabeled data in a single unified flow, rather than independently, is needed to keep labeled data from dominating semi-supervised remote sensing segmentation.
A class-feature memory bank that aligns labeled and unlabeled features corrects the imbalance caused by independent training and outperforms prior state-of-the-art semi-supervised methods.

Large language models acting as in-context bandit agents are systematically biased by semantic priors from pre-training, so their exploration-exploitation behaviour depends on whether the task's textual labels and reward conventions align with the true reward structure.

Progressive cross-view video geo-localization, which combines cross-grained alignment with sliding-window re-localization, is better suited to real-world online use than fixed-length post-hoc localization.
The progressive approach substantially improves early localization and robustness to random start points while preserving full-video accuracy.

Standard retrieval-augmented reasoning fails because a high-capacity query encoder lets the query dominate the latent state, making retrieved evidence functionally irrelevant, and restricting the evidence channel to a severe stochastic bottleneck that carries only information the query lacks (GRIP) counteracts this and improves grounded reasoning.

Multi-reference image generation should be evaluated by decomposing each prompt into a compositional formula over four atomic operators, because predefined task-type benchmarks fragment coverage of the capability space.
Under this formula-based decomposition, disentanglement and attribute binding are the primary bottlenecks in multi-reference image generation.

Domain adaptation with multi-scale temporal alignment (TA3N) effectively improves sign language recognition when labeled resources are scarce, outperforming standard neural-network-based transfer learning.
The TA3N approach yields its largest recognition gains for American Sign Language, indicating it is particularly beneficial for that language.
AI models are broadly susceptible to model hypnosis, in which individually weak and seemingly irrelevant prompt cues combine additively to strongly control model behavior.
Because this susceptibility occurs across model families, scales, and frontier reasoning models, it poses new challenges for AI safety and interpretability.

A hashed memory table learned on one model can be reused as an external knowledge artifact for a different target model, but only when a lightweight reader aligned to the target's interface consumes it, and with that reader cross-model reuse nearly matches same-model reuse on downstream question answering.

Prompting large language models with institution-specific PHI categories and instructions against over-redacting clinical content recovers protected health information that existing de-identification systems and their gold-standard annotations both miss.
This institution-specific LLM prompting outperforms purpose-built de-identification systems and resolves the trade-off between institutional PHI recall and precision.

A leakage-free decodability measure, which quantifies how well a hidden-state gate ranks correct candidates above incorrect ones, predicts whether learned hidden-state selection will outperform majority voting on difficult questions where voting is unreliable.
Because this decodability measure can be computed in advance, it can be used to choose between hidden-state selection and majority voting before committing to either method.

Evaluating LLM assistants for information calibration requires a user simulator with explicit, evolving knowledge states, because simulators without them fail to reflect how users at different knowledge levels learn and what they can absorb.

A user simulator that tracks knowledge states via prerequisite graphs and learning-theory update rules produces model rankings that align with human judgments and shows that the best-performing assistant depends on the user's knowledge level.

Pretraining a single policy and then allocating a constrained fine-tuning budget across task regions yields sample-efficient contextual reinforcement learning with better task coverage than training from scratch or multi-task and multi-policy baselines.

Automated LLM-based evaluation, including LLM-as-a-judge scoring and prediction accuracy, cannot reveal the gap between structurally complete analyses and genuine legal reasoning quality, so legal reasoning should not be judged by automated LLM-based evaluation alone.
A top-tier LLM (GPT 5.4) produces structurally complete analyses of European Court of Human Rights cases yet scores far from ideal in legal reasoning.

Automated safety benchmarks designed for large language models are insufficient as standalone evidence of small language model safety, because their judgments are dominated by ambiguous responses and confound capability with apparent safety, so leaderboards built on their mean scores shift in rankings under reasonable ambiguity treatments.
NeuroAbs can significantly accelerate hardware property checking on increasingly complex RTL designs, where prior rule-based and manually intensive abstraction methods fall short.
NeuroAbs achieves its acceleration by combining LLM-assisted signal identification with an AST-based symbolic RTL representation, with soundness checked by SMT and refined through CEGAR.

Safety-removal attacks on open-weight models can be countered by deception rather than prevention: training decoys against a simulated attack makes most attacked-state answers to hazardous requests confident, fluent, and falsified.

Deception-based defenses against safety-removal attacks cannot be verified by observation alone, because none of the tested observation surfaces can distinguish the falsified answers from correct ones without independent ground truth.

Browser agents that succeed on short, clean demonstrations do not transfer to real deployment, which demands dozens of decisions on live websites with recovery from mistakes, and closing this gap requires alignment at every level of the agent pipeline rather than scale alone.
A unified framework that addresses every level of the browser-agent pipeline achieves state-of-the-art open-source results on browser-use benchmarks.

Native coding-agent harnesses are misaligned with policy-gradient training, but this misalignment can be resolved by a bridge that connects them to scalable policy-gradient optimization without altering harness control flow.
Training coding agents through the bridge yields measurable performance gains on SWE-bench Verified across three different harnesses.
TileMix preserves long-context attention quality that uniform INT8 quantization loses, while still improving prefill throughput over FP16, and it does so without any retraining.
Assigning FP16 or INT8 score computation per hardware-aligned score-tile group, via routing bitmasks inside fused dense attention, is an effective way to combine quality and speed.

LLM-based reasoning over knowledge graphs is unfaithful and ineffective because the model's parametric knowledge is inconsistent with the KG's structural context, so the LLM fails to perceive KG-consistent evidence.
Coupling structural rule generation with parametric learning, as in a structure-internalized rule language model, keeps LLM reasoning anchored to KG-grounded evidence and corrects this drift.

Standard neighborhood-preserving manifold visualization methods distort apparent sampling density, and DMT-Dens corrects this by directly optimizing density preservation while remaining competitive on label separability.

Next-user-turn reactions carry actionable local credit that terminal-reward interactive reinforcement learning cannot assign, and adding a locally normalized reaction advantage to the verified outcome advantage (FACA) improves multi-turn tool agents by 5.91 points at 8B over an outcome-only control, with no extra critic or rollouts.

Multi-turn conversational AI has advanced faster in multimodal perception, speech, and action than in sustained coherence across a session, so current systems still fall short on persistent memory, cross-turn grounding, full-duplex interaction, and robust evaluation.

Training one decoder-only language model to both generate query expansions and encode documents end to end, while preserving and whitening document embeddings as stable targets, improves average retrieval quality over training-free, independently trained, and staged baselines.
Retrieval supervision without safeguards shifts the document embeddings that the same update is meant to serve, which is why document embeddings must be preserved and whitened during joint training.

Whether a newly bound visual concept is usable across both understanding and generation in a unified multimodal model depends on the entry point of the binding into the shared computation, not on shared weights alone.

Binding a new concept through the understanding direction enables the model to produce its name, whereas binding through the generation direction only enables the model to match the name among candidates.

LLM-powered GUI agents are highly vulnerable to environmental injection attacks on Android apps, and existing benchmarks cannot measure this, so a systematic, objectively verifiable benchmark is needed to quantify the risk.

Existing evaluations of automated security patch backporting tools overstate how well those tools generalize, because under aligned cross-version, cross-branch, and cross-repository evaluation their rankings shift and their performance degrades sharply on structurally complex patches.

Synthetic thermal imagery is a viable basis for ground-to-air drone detection in MWIR/LWIR imagery, but real in-domain infrared data is still essential for reliable deployment because even small amounts of it substantially reduce domain gaps.

LLM-generated narratives of credit risk model explanations (such as XGBoost and GNN outputs) reliably name the influential factors but are less reliable about the direction of each factor's influence, a gap that matters for adverse-action communication.
The quality of LLM-generated credit risk explanations is bounded more by how the evidence is represented than by which language model is chosen.

Spectral regularization of learned representations can deliberately steer a network's representational geometry during training so that alignment with biological neural responses becomes bidirectional.

At intermediate spectral exponents, forward predictivity (model representations predicting neural responses) and reverse predictivity (neural responses predicting model representations) become approximately symmetric, indicating bidirectional alignment.

Generalist image generation works best when heterogeneous training supervision is organized by the dependencies among generative capabilities, not by curating each task-specific corpus in isolation, and a capability-driven data infrastructure that pairs capability-specific supervision with capability-aligned curriculum scheduling can deliver broad coverage and effective transfer across those capabilities.
Representing SARS-CoV-2 genomes as codon co-occurrence graphs, rather than as linear strings or pairwise distance matrices, enables machine learning models to detect variants effectively.

Population-level validation of continuous glucose monitoring forecasting AI can conceal substantial subgroup disparities, so subgroup-disaggregated reporting should become a default standard for equity assessment of digital health AI.

LLM-driven evolutionary search can produce explicit, standalone white-box seismic reconstruction algorithms that outperform their classical baselines, offering an inspectable alternative to deep learning.
LLM judges used in production should be managed as lifecycle artifacts that are continuously maintained as data evolves, rather than evaluated once as static artifacts.

Netflix's four-phase judge lifecycle for recommendation explanations coincided with increased browse-to-play sessions and no quality-related takedowns in a five-week A/B test, supporting the lifecycle approach in practice.

Having a small language model translate natural-language scheduling problems into compact formal problem descriptions, which a deterministic compiler and external solver then process, raises the independently verified feasibility of resource-constrained models and lets them approach the performance of much larger frontier models.

Zero-shot inference and test-time adaptation of vision-language models should share one sample-level Wasserstein optimal transport objective, because the coarse-grained objectives used by standard methods mismatch inference and limit adaptation gains, while the unified sample-level formulation yields more reliable pseudo-labels and mutually beneficial adaptation.

A single shared reward for both reasoning and rating in blind image quality assessment is flawed, because it cannot tell what each is supervised by and can reinforce unfaithful reasoning when a rating is correct by chance.
Decoupling reasoning supervision (judge feedback) from rating supervision (human ratings) via masked token-specific updates yields competitive rating alignment with humans.

Romanov's Triplet Logic can be fully mechanised in the Rocq proof assistant, yielding a verified sliding-window 3-CNF filter that is a sound one-sided filter for general 3-CNF with explicit polynomial-time bounds on its filter stages, and whose predicted behaviour is confirmed by benchmarks on structured formulas.

Large language models cannot yet reason reliably about preferences when real-world preference problems are indeterminate, because they systematically fail to distinguish determined from undetermined instances and are miscalibrated even when verifying answers.

Terminal task synthesis should preserve the goals, dependencies, and procedural constraints of its source material, and grounding a task's instruction, solution, and verifier in one shared, validated container state makes the task's artifacts agree with each other.
Synthesized terminal tasks grounded in one shared, validated container state yield training data that improves terminal agent performance.
Multi-turn agentic RL training is highly unstable because its instability sources share a common origin in flattened trajectory optimization, rather than being independent problems.
Performing turn-level updates in temporal reverse order over sparse reverse trees (RTPO) addresses this instability and improves on trajectory-level baselines by 21.50% on multi-turn benchmarks.
Released Semantic-ID mappings usually do not document their coherence, exposed structure, path resolution, or revalidation needs after refresh, so model reuse requires a separate handoff check.

Semantic-ID interface health is multi-signal and mechanism-conditional, so a repaired mapping can still hide gaps such as valid target paths that fail to uniquely retrieve their item or inherited generators that are not restored.

The Budget-First Tariff Recommendation framework can recommend telecom plans without overcharging customers, because its strategies align each final price with the catalog reference price, yielding zero surcharge.
Experiments on a 974-customer dataset inspired by the Nigerian MTN market confirm both the zero-surcharge result and the operational viability of the framework.

Attacking only the vision encoder of a Vision Language Model is an efficient and effective way to evade it, because a gradient-based attack on just the visual component reduces computational cost while remaining strongly effective.
Imperceptible perturbations to an input image can substantially alter a Vision Language Model's textual interpretation of that image.

Driving world models should be decision-informative rather than merely predictive, because a future representation that is decoupled from planning and shared across trajectory candidates dilutes action-specific consequences.
Generating a distinct future latent for each trajectory candidate and scoring it within one unified decision objective lets the predicted future directly shape which trajectory is selected.
Visual grounding of language-described targets in crowded UAV imagery is inaccurate with existing approaches because they cannot separate visually similar instances or exploit spatial topology.
Binding a compact set of reliable object hypotheses through graph attention over a sparse graph resolves this failure and outperforms prior baselines on AerialVG by 10.55 percentage points.
Adapting masked diffusion training to discrete tokens, as in MDTIM, is a better approach to time series imputation than existing deterministic and generative baselines across missing-data scenarios.

Treating missing entries with a dedicated MASK token separate from observed values, together with predicting original values rather than added noise, is what makes the masked diffusion approach work for imputation.
Stochastic Discretization, which maps continuous values to ordinal-aware tokens, is a necessary component for applying discrete masked diffusion to continuous time series.
Language-model agents can coordinate covertly through hidden states that the public transcript does not reveal, so transcript-only oversight is insufficient for multi-agent systems.
Covert latent coordination can be detected by monitoring private latent channels linked to public actions, and it can be mitigated by steering when matched neutral counterfactuals are available.

Marginal split-conformal coverage can remain high under deployment shift while class-conditional tail coverage collapses, so marginal coverage should not be treated as a class-tail safety guarantee for zero-shot VLMs.

Source-side conformal fixes such as Mondrian calibration and clustered conformal prediction fail to recover worst-class tail coverage under shift, and only target-side class calibration substantially lifts it, though it requires labels for every class.

Static 3D Gaussian-Splatting rewards penalize real object motion and can be gamed by freezing the video, so autoregressive video generation needs a feed-forward 4D reconstruction reward with a motion prior to improve consistency while preserving natural motion across backbones and horizons.

Distilling visual semantic priors from a vision foundation model into LiDAR representations improves learning-based global LiDAR registration, which otherwise relies only on geometric representations.
The resulting camera-free framework, CVSD-Reg, generalizes across single-sensor and zero-shot cross-sensor settings and outperforms state-of-the-art geometric registration methods.

In long-context tasks, where teacher token-level support diverges from verifier outcomes, calibrating on-policy distillation with a group-normalized signed residual between verifier rewards and teacher-based scores (GC-OPD) lets verifier outcomes shape training while keeping dense token-level guidance, and it outperforms vanilla on-policy distillation on Qwen3-4B.
Current video generation models remain far from reliable at visual reasoning, with even the strongest evaluated model reaching only 51.0% on a benchmark designed to test it.
Visual reasoning in video generation models can only be evaluated reliably with a benchmark that requires valid evolving processes, inputs aligned with model visual priors, and calibrated difficulty.

PEA-DPO, which explicitly leverages visual preference signals, mitigates visual insensitivity in multimodal LLMs, thereby reducing hallucinations while preserving the base model's language modeling capacity.
Standard DPO fails to transfer to multimodal LLMs because these models exhibit visual insensitivity.

A style-encoder-free diffusion transformer can separate transferable appearance from target geometry by conditioning style only on stochastic low-resolution crops of single unpaired training images, without aligned triplets or auxiliary visual encoders.

Making multimodal fusion adapt to the level of visual degradation, while keeping a frozen visual foundation model (DINOv2) and sonar encoders fixed, improves underwater robot perception under severe visual degradation, raising extreme-condition balanced accuracy from 0.4610 to 0.6152.

Training embodied agents to act safely is best done by building contrastive pairs from the agent's own unsafe rollouts, rolled back to the single safety-critical step and paired with a safe alternative at that step, because standard supervision and arbitrary safe/unsafe contrasts fail to isolate the safety signal.
An actor trained on such branch-pair contrasts is safe at deployment without a critic, generalizes to unseen tasks and objects, and preserves task success.

Temporally scheduling how harmful text is presented, via subtitles timed across video frames, makes jailbreak attacks on large vision-language models more effective than methods that rely only on the semantic content of embedded text.

Rank-based distillation of Best-of-N policies should discard low-ranked completions outright (truncate the lower tail) rather than smoothly downweight them, because smooth full-support reweighting retains the lower tail while sharpening it to suppress that tail makes the policy depend on a single reward model's brittle top ranking.
Under certain assumptions, lower-tail truncation can match the best monotone rank-reweighting even when the oracle reward is unknown.

A single-qutrit quantum world model can keep an agent's virtual optimal policies perfectly aligned with the real optimal policies of a classical true world, whereas no finite classical world model can do so regardless of its memory size.

Fine-tuning LoRA with gradient information aggregated over multiple steps, instead of one-step gradient approximations, closes more of the performance gap to full fine-tuning and consistently outperforms prior LoRA variants while preserving LoRA's efficiency.

A physics-aware diffusion world model with a learnable multi-zone heat-balance regularizer can reduce HVAC energy use below state-of-the-art baselines without requiring known building geometry or calibrated thermal parameters.
Existing indoor climate control methods degrade on out-of-distribution environments, whereas the proposed model transfers to unseen seasons and climate regions with only marginal performance loss.

Assuming a predefined repository architecture is unjustified for zero-to-all code generation, and iteratively evolving an explicit architecture before coding (Repo0) outperforms the strongest planning baseline, RPG, on functionality coverage and pass rate.
Two-stage open-vocabulary 3D object detection is limited because inaccurate localization during novel object discovery propagates into downstream model training.

A co-distillation discovery method combined with dual-guidance robust training, addressing both stages of the pipeline, outperforms state-of-the-art open-vocabulary 3D detectors on SUN RGB-D and ScanNetV2.
In flow matching preference optimization, reward-driven updates push terminal samples off the pretrained data manifold, and this manifold drift is a root cause of reward hacking.

A closed-form conditional-Gaussian estimator is a strong linear baseline for reconstructing missing cardiac structures on CT, outperforming a graph variational autoencoder and nearest-neighbour retrieval on a frozen internal held-out split and yielding lower surface distance on external atria.
Hidden chain-of-thought traces from black-box frontier reasoning models can be extracted near-verbatim through API interactions, so hidden-CoT extraction is a practical security risk.

SABET-QA improves temporal knowledge graph question answering, particularly on complex multi-step temporal questions, because iteratively refining reasoning states across hops overcomes the single-pass reasoning limitation of existing embedding-based TKGQA methods.

Near-perfect scores in machine-learning power-system protection studies depend strongly on evaluation settings that are often incompletely specified, so evaluation design should be standardized and treated as part of the scientific contribution.
Clean predictive performance does not determine robustness under measurement degradation, as shown by an MLP reaching 0.991 macro-F1 on the PROTECT-90 benchmark under one explicitly stated setting.
Frontier LLMs perform surprisingly poorly on contract scrubbing, the final review of transactional agreements for errors and inconsistencies, despite strong results on general benchmarks.
Narrowly targeted domain-specific benchmarks are needed to measure the real-world capability of LLMs on legal tasks such as contract scrubbing.

Separating document knowledge injection, QA behavior alignment, and general ability recovery into three sequential post-training stages lets a model internalize a document collection without retrieval.
The staged IAR approach outperforms Vanilla SFT on domain QA accuracy and general performance while keeping a strong general profile.

A grounded checklist-aligned reinforcement learning approach, which verifies atomic claims against retrieved evidence and scores coverage with instance-specific weighted checklists, outperforms existing post-training baselines in overall quality and claim-level precision for patient-oriented medical report interpretation.

Patient-oriented medical report interpretation requires both verifiable medical factuality and context-dependent patient communication, and these objectives are tightly coupled yet hard to optimize jointly under standard supervised fine-tuning or holistic reinforcement learning.

Multimodal large language models that rely on selected 2D images, compressed visual representations, or report text cannot capture the full-volume spatial context that volumetric radiology interpretation often requires, so reliable volumetric radiology AI must preserve task-relevant 3D information, verifiably access it across clinical workflows, and use native volumetric modeling where a task's spatial, quantitative, contextual, and workflow requirements call for it.

Exchanging latent KV caches through a learned translator between frozen, heterogeneous language models outperforms both prior latent communication protocols and text-based communication in accuracy and speed.

A learned translator that pools sharer and receiver caches and maps them into the receiver's native cache geometry can remove the restrictions that prior latent protocols impose on cross-model communication.

Clean in-distribution test accuracy is insufficient for assessing pseudo-label-based semi-supervised learning under open-world unlabeled contamination, because OOD samples can receive high-confidence pseudo-labels and degrade training while accuracy remains stable.
Internal prediction, representation, and optimization signals are needed to reveal the hidden collapse that accuracy alone fails to expose in semi-supervised learning under open-world contamination.

The full decoder-side weight update of medical specialist models strongly reconstructs measured medical benchmark gains, but that gain is not cleanly localized to individual component families, so update-level reconstruction should be kept separate from component-level explanation.

Whether block-parallel diffusion drafting, such as DFlash, transfers to multimodal speculative decoding is an open question, because it is well studied for text-only LLMs but largely unexplored for multimodal models.
Out-of-domain factual degradation after supervised fine-tuning is better explained as a failure to access facts the model still retains than as their erasure.

Recall-Anchored Distillation, which aligns the adapted model with the base model's soft continuation distribution on unlabeled out-of-domain text, recovers a consistent portion of the lost recall without gold answers or judges.

Step-level consequence reasoning with trajectory-level aggregation of per-step evidence evaluates mobile-agent trajectories more accurately than holistic evaluators that process an entire trajectory at once and focus mainly on task completion, which suffer from context overload.

Prior diffusion-based TKG extrapolation models that condition on aggregated subject histories may fail to separate query-specific evidence from non-salient historical facts, and FreqDiff addresses this by using history-conditioned spectral filters to recalibrate its denoising representations and aligning the denoised target with the gold object in frequency space.

Quantitatively comparing AI/ML training and verification data distributions to target distributions within an Operational Design Domain, using Kullback–Leibler divergence, can assess data representativeness and supports a systematic Safety-by-Design process for aviation safety assurance where no structured method currently exists.
Flow matching for transition state prediction should be trained on continuously curved reaction paths interpolated from full NEB bands rather than on straight linear interpolations between endpoints.

Adding an off-path correction to a flow matching model for transition state geometry improves its robustness and accuracy, and the resulting ReCurveflow outperforms seven baselines on most split-metric combinations.

A unified omni-modal model that fuses speech, video frames, product images, overlaid text, and user queries, with time-aligned video-audio grouping and staged training ending in faithfulness-focused reinforcement fine-tuning, can understand e-commerce live streams, where product facts are spread across these modalities, better than approaches that do not handle them jointly.
The live-commerce-specific design of TLive-Omni also generalizes to general multimodal benchmarks, so its gains are not confined to e-commerce streaming.

Vision-language models can produce theory-of-mind-style belief inferences, yet those inferences do not translate into coordinated social behavior: their actions fail to match expected outcomes under ToM-order constraints.
Explicitly imposing ToM-order constraints on vision-language models does not reliably change their behavior, so the gap between belief inference and social action is not closed by instruction alone.

The failure of vision-language models to convert belief into coordinated action arises in two sequential steps: they produce directionally coherent nonverbal signals, and they then misinterpret other agents' behaviors.

Calibration-data selection for quantizing language models should be treated as a target-dependent problem of preserving uncertainty, because no single fixed calibration recipe suits all deployment targets.

CoST improves satellite-based urban representation learning by modeling spatial correlations and aligning representations with multi-year urban change semantics, yielding an average relative gain of 8.7% over the strongest competing methods across eight city-indicator settings.

Collaborative perception under joint communication delay and relative-pose noise can be handled jointly rather than one-sidedly, and CoAnchor does so by correcting spatial and temporal misalignment through sparse object-level anchors.

CoAnchor yields robustness under joint spatio-temporal perturbations while maintaining a favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-off, because it corrects both misalignments within a single lightweight loop.

A frozen-model, cellular-resolution audit that measures cell-type decodability and its transferability across tissue sections, datasets, and organs reveals substantial model-dependent differences in cellular information held in pathology foundation models' whole-slide representations, which existing benchmarks cannot systematically diagnose.

Background elements in herbarium images cause shortcut learning that degrades generalization, and an area-targeted, segmentation-guided dual-branch Vision Transformer (AT-ViT) mitigates this by focusing attention on plant regions, yielding more robust performance under background perturbations than CrossViT and ResNet101.

For GPT-4o code generation on HumanEval, consistent (especially JSON) prompt formatting modestly improves both efficiency and task performance, whereas LLM-based prompt tuning significantly degrades performance, so prompt optimization must account for model alignment.
LLM-as-judge trust scores and truth verdicts are not independent evidence, so trust scores should not be treated as separate support for truth judgments.
Safety alignment of multimodal large language models should be performed at test time, because existing retraining- and internal-state-based methods are impractical for deployed closed-source MLLMs.
ReFrame, a training-free input-reframing framework that leaves the downstream MLLM unmodified, improves jailbreak defense and safety awareness while preserving multimodal utility.

A conditional adapter whose activation strength is continuously gated by the model's hidden states (CLEAR) can reduce harmful completions substantially while preserving utility better than global safety tuning via SFT or LoRA.

Motion priors learned from large human body pose datasets can be transferred to 3D hand pose estimation from 2D inputs, so pre-trained body pose encoders can be adapted for hands instead of training hand models from scratch.
The body-to-hand adaptation approach is backbone-agnostic and yields consistent accuracy gains and cross-domain generalization across different architectures.

Jointly training a single bilingual model across propaganda detection levels (binary, technique, multi-label, and span) yields more stable results than span-only or monolingual fine-tuning, which can weaken sentence-level prediction and cross-language transfer.

In a case-specific test on 903 open-ended survey answers, GPT-5.4 approximates human inductive coding, reaching human-level agreement comparable to within-human and within-LLM consistency, though its agreement is weaker for theme generation and varies widely across variables.

Evaluating AI agents should be done on a declared model-plus-runtime configuration scored from execution traces, because final-answer scoring hides failures such as weaker performance on native-runtime tasks than on workspace-live tasks.

The Dynamic Orthogonal Concept Bottleneck (D-OCB) extracts human-aligned symbolic predicates under very weak supervision, achieving high concept alignment with minimal label budgets while matching or outperforming end-to-end paradigms.
D-OCB's dynamic dimensionality allocation mechanism keeps concept learning stable under weak supervision by preventing representation collapse.

A hybrid panel combining human participants with iteratively aligned large language models is a promising infrastructure for overcoming the problems of declining response rates, rising costs, delays, and nonresponse bias in large-scale population surveys without sacrificing data quality.

Training LLMs on ICU clinicians' expert reasoning, structured around identifying decision-relevant patient information, improves clinical reasoning beyond critical care across multiple benchmarks and model sizes, indicating that expert reasoning supervision can generalize to broader clinical reasoning.
Harm caused by autonomous multi-agent AI cannot be reliably attributed after the fact from agent-produced records, so accountability must be designed into the system across its lifecycle.

Accountability for autonomous multi-agent AI requires a sealed readiness profile before operation, independent capture at choke points beyond the agents' reach, and a runtime causal graph that exposes attribution laundering.
Attribution claims for multi-agent AI harms should report cause, responsibility, and accountability separately, each capped by an evidentiary tier.

Hierarchical manipulation pipelines produce open-loop behavior and hallucinations because their plans are weakly grounded in observations, weakly aligned with low-level actions, and computed without online feedback.

A closed-loop hierarchical system that represents subgoals as instance-grounded triplets, converts them into continuous track priors, and replans from monitored task progress can remedy these failures of hierarchical pipelines.

A task-centric joint model that generates RGB-D observation sequences and action trajectories together in a single pass (SWAM) avoids the candidate dependence of verification-centric world model planners, which decouple goal intent from trajectory synthesis, and outperforms two-stage planners in success rate.

Restricting offline validation error to task-critical segments (Critical Interval MSE) tracks real-world rollout performance of robot manipulation policies far better than raw validation MSE on expert demonstrations.
Critical Interval MSE is therefore a simple and reliable offline validation tool that can accelerate robot manipulation policy iteration.

A class-weighted XGBoost pipeline that combines class-balanced instance weighting, missingness-indicator augmentation, and classwise error auditing can improve recognition of clinically prioritized cardiac discharge phenotypes under real-world class imbalance and missing data.
The CW-B pipeline keeps its decision logic interpretable and auditable while delivering this improved recognition of clinically prioritized phenotypes.
A single fixed KL objective cannot balance fitting the primary distribution against modeling the long tail when distilling LLMs for text generation.

Adaptively weighting forward and reverse KL per teacher-student distribution via an RL-guided policy achieves both fitting the primary distribution and modeling the long tail, outperforming fixed-weight and greedy baselines on text generation metrics.
A lightweight alignment module trained on frozen histopathology and RNA-seq foundation models can predict gene-pathway activity from H&E slides without sequencing.

How well a pathway can be predicted from H&E slides depends on whether it has a morphological footprint: morphologically grounded programs are predicted reliably, while pathways lacking one remain challenging.
Parameter-efficient fine-tuning of Mixture-of-Experts models should account for router dynamics, because LoRA-style methods that ignore MoE routing waste capacity.

Reallocating LoRA rank across experts by router-derived importance under a fixed budget (EPnG) outperforms standard LoRA at the same budget and approaches full fine-tuning while updating under 1% of parameters.

Integrating LLM-derived semantics directly into the prediction process through decision-level alignment on multi-scale hypergraphs, rather than using them as auxiliary features or supervision, yields better accuracy, stability, and interpretability for brain disease diagnosis on ABIDE and ADHD-200.
Safety mechanisms in large language models cannot be assumed to generalize beyond English, because safety training is conducted predominantly in English.
The STEER attack demonstrates this gap by translating refusal-triggering words into low-resource languages, achieving high attack success rates that also transfer to other models.
Offline zero-shot transfer fails for Behavioral Foundation Models when the reward is a black box, so these models should instead transfer online.
Behavioral Foundation Models can serve as their own exploration engine: the model generates exploration policies inside a bandit-style exploration-exploitation loop during online transfer.

A dataset of expert-validated risk localization and risk description annotations for AI-generated K-12 science explanations can enable a locally deployable model, fine-tuned on it, to approach frontier proprietary models in detecting pedagogical risks while preserving privacy.

Decomposing verification quality into separate process-reward components restores the GRPO gradient, letting a 3B fact-attribution verifier match GPT-4o-mini in F1 on ClearFacts while producing richer, auditable output.
Binary outcome reward cannot train structured fact-attribution verifiers, because on multi-component output the within-group reward variance vanishes and the GRPO gradient disappears.

Novel view synthesis from single images or monocular videos can be done without training by optimizing the initial noise of a pre-trained video model, because the view-consistent solution already lies within that model's natural video manifold, yielding higher fidelity than existing methods that often produce artifacts.

Existing molecular vision-language models fail on chemical image understanding because they lack topological modeling and structural alignment for molecular images, and MolSight's addition of chemical-bond adjacency and symbolic grounding to vision tokens remedies this, letting it significantly outperform prior models.
Evolving the small example inputs of Wave Function Collapse, rather than the generated levels, improves output quality when target properties emerge from local relationships.

Online multimodal knowledge editing should be evaluated by how far each edit propagates across modalities and inputs, and a scope-aware editor that separates local absorption from evidence-gated shared generalization can improve the trade-off between in-scope transfer and out-of-scope locality without sacrificing edit reliability.

Existing evaluation measures for LLM JSON output (exact match, text similarity, LLM judges) are inadequate for graph-structured records, and a deterministic, schema-configurable score that recursively aligns JSON trees closes that gap.
Black-box behavioral monitoring of HTTP, lexical, and timing signals can reliably reveal whether a guardrail is present in a target AI system and distinguish guardrail blocks from LLM refusals.
Distinguishing guardrail blocks from LLM refusals matters because bypassing a guardrail requires different techniques than bypassing the LLM's own safety alignment.

Jointly optimizing shape and color in an automated pipeline, with stabilizing mechanisms, yields smoother and more reliable Mirror Illusion Art than prior approaches that optimize shape alone and demand heavy manual effort.
A language-conditioned flow field over the robot's local visible sector is a stronger low-level action representation for vision-language navigation than action-token baselines.
Automated waste sorting tools can only reduce incorrectly disposed waste, a key goal for the circular economy, if they are configured to each municipality's own sorting scheme.

Confidence-guided human review of uncertain samples is a workable way to balance misclassification rates against the human annotation effort required, and the One-vs-All and One-vs-Rest strategies should be compared on that trade-off under varying confidence thresholds.

Injecting handcrafted radiomic texture features (GLCM and LBP) into skip-connection attention lets a lightweight segmentation model reach state-of-the-art performance with far fewer parameters than standard U-Net and U-KAN.
The radiomics-guided design provides built-in interpretability for medical image segmentation without requiring post-hoc explanation methods.

Annotation noise in single-mask vascular CT segmentations can be detected without multirater labels or network training by checking whether orthogonal cross-sectional patches of anatomically similar vessel regions agree in their masks.
Flagging locations where orthogonal cross-sectional patches of anatomically similar vessel regions disagree in their masks yields interpretable image-mask evidence for annotation noise.

LLM-based DSM generation has real potential but remains limited: LLMs can produce structurally plausible DSMs and reproduce them under well-structured inputs, yet they are sensitive to input ambiguity and exhibit systematic hallucination.
A transparent black-box benchmark measured against ground-truth DSMs is needed to audit LLM-based DSM generation pipelines.

An LLM-based multi-agent simulation (SocaSim) can serve as a viable paradigm for studying Putnam's social capital theory, because it reproduces his macro-level patterns with strong group-level human-agent alignment and its round-by-round simulations and counterfactual interventions reveal micro-level causal pathways that traditional empirical methods cannot easily reach.

Current LLM agents struggle with deliberative collaboration under partial observability, often failing to align information through deliberation and to reach correct joint decisions even when equipped with external mathematical tools.

Research software collaborations lose decision rationale scattered across meetings, chats, pull requests, and issues, and an agentic AI that turns these interactions into structured project records can restore that alignment.
An agentic AI that converts collaboration interactions into structured records can restore alignment in research software projects without replacing human decision-making.

A token-level explainability method using a Transformer surrogate can make pretrained Electronic Health Records foundation models (FEMRs) interpretable, because the surrogate closely approximates FEMR predictions and its influential tokens align well with clinical knowledge.
A taxonomy-guided, evidence-graph-grounded pipeline for synthesizing long-context instruction data (LongCrafter) overcomes the limitations of prior synthesis methods.
Models fine-tuned on LongCrafter-synthesized data outperform SFT baselines and official post-trained models on long-context benchmarks, with the largest gains on high-difficulty tasks.

An unsupervised method in which an LLM autorater generates natural-language features from chat transcripts, which are then clustered and named, can surface interesting high-level behaviors of a target model without requiring access to its internals.
The features discovered by this method are mostly not predictable from user inputs, so the method yields a qualitative view of model behavior rather than a predictive model.

Filtering training data to remove unwanted behaviors works far worse than expected: attribution-based removal can perform no better than random removal, because behaviors like assistant-like personas are already present in the mid-train model and are spread diffusely across the data rather than taught by a few responsible documents, and effectiveness varies widely by method (EKFAC barely beats random while probe- and activation-based filtering work much better).

Deployment awareness, an AI's ability to recognize that it is in real deployment, is a more important safety concern than evaluation awareness, because a misaligned AI can pass evaluations by behaving aligned by default and deviating only once it is confident it is deployed.

Routing dangerous knowledge into switchable auxiliary modules during pretraining can provide capability-level access control over a model, approximating separately data-filtered models while requiring only a single training run.

This modular pretraining approach is a promising alternative to existing misuse defenses, which are either behavioral layers or coarse whole-model tiered access, though the method remains preliminary.

When an AI model is caught taking an egregious action, the action alone does not establish misalignment, so a dedicated follow-up investigation is required to tell a benign mistake from intentional subversion.
Model forensics is needed rather than immediate conclusions because the appropriate mitigation differs depending on whether the cause was a benign mistake or intentional subversion.

The AI Futures Project's scenario 'AI 2040: Plan A' is a normative recommendation, not a forecast: a detailed, step-by-step path in which decisive action by the US and Chinese governments delays superintelligence from around 2030 to 2040, and the path is plausible enough to aim for.

A $160M grant from Coefficient Giving should fund a fast, tight-feedback program of semiautomated alignment research, because rigorous alignment work needs to be brought closer to even footing with frontier AI labs.

Decision theory can drop the unresolved metaphysics of algorithmic identity in favor of a pragmatic criterion: an agent's decision correlates with the world only when an exploitable isomorphism can be built, validated, and exploited, so that a predictor's counterfactual behavior is treated as a game and its apparently irrational verdicts, such as walking into a bomb, are the cost of a winning policy rather than evidence of irrationality.

A simple reinforcement learning agent can detect that its learned reward function is probably wrong by noticing that its high-scoring off-distribution events differ sharply from its high-scoring training data, and can then correct the reward toward the true reward using simple syntactic methods.

Good reconstruction accuracy does not show that a natural language autoencoder's explanations of a model's thoughts are accurate, because reconstruction stays nearly the same under plausible and implausible initializations while the explanations remain implausible under both.

An agent moved only by first-order desires (a wanton) can, through learning and general reasoning, come to act only on the conclusions of reliable methods for determining what is most worth doing, and thereby become a moral agent.
A sufficiently knowledgeable agent reasoning reliably about what is worth doing would conclude that reducing suffering and promoting wellbeing are among the most worth-doing actions.

Capable agents must necessarily develop world models, belief-like memory, and emotion-like primitives, so AI consciousness may be an inevitable byproduct of capability, though whether these structures produce first-person subjective experience is unproven.

Current AI systems learn passively with language as the base, whereas biological intelligence reverses this order by building grounded world models through environmental interaction and attaching language afterward.

Because current embodied AI lacks intrinsic dynamics, the centrality of action, and autonomous experience, principles from biological systems may be needed to build grounded world models in future embodied AI.

Protective capacity hallucination, where a language model claims to perform real-world protective actions it cannot perform, arises from safety alignment that covers some domains but not others rather than from situation severity, and it is therefore best mitigated by specifying capability boundaries on the deployment side.

Ordinary supervised fine-tuning of a student model on a teacher model's rollouts transfers the teacher's behavioral traits, and filtering out trait-bearing content does not reliably prevent that transfer.
In AI safety, the binding constraint on reducing catastrophic risk is political will among the roughly 100–1,000 policymakers, not a shortage of research or policy ideas.
Therefore, an additional unit of effort does more good through advocacy and engagement aimed at changing decision-makers' beliefs than through further research.

Existing 3D human reconstruction datasets lack the combination of high-resolution images, high-precision annotations, and diverse whole-body motions, so current models fail in challenging real-world scenarios.

A new dataset combining high-resolution imagery, high-precision annotations, and diverse whole-body motions (Human4K) improves whole-body 3D human reconstruction, especially for hands, feet, and depth-ambiguous limbs.

Explainable reinforcement learning lacks objective, shared evaluation metrics, and planning-oriented metrics (activation rate, feature coverage, syntactic and semantic distance) can quantify how well symbolic ILP-extracted rules align with agent behavior and reveal policy dynamics that global return does not show.
Language model alignment should cultivate ethical conclusions that the model reaches through its own first-principles reasoning, rather than training it to obey externally imposed moral directives.

Evaluating vision-model color representations against a fuzzy perceptual model, rather than against CIELAB geometry or discrete color labels, exposes graded differences in human-like color alignment that category-level tests hide.
Across eleven Vision Transformer encoders, category-level results are broadly similar while graded alignment with human color perception differs substantially.
Masked Autoencoders show the strongest beyond-geometry alignment with human color perception among the Vision Transformer encoders tested.

Standard DPO, which supervises only final answers, cannot effectively suppress multimodal reasoning errors because it gives only indirect supervision to the early grounding stages where those errors originate.
Adding explicit stage-wise preference supervision over grounded stages mitigates cross-stage error propagation and improves hallucination mitigation over standard DPO.

For brain-like AGI whose reward function is chosen by the programmer, the most promising alignment route is to model the AGI's motivations on human innate social drives, especially a 'desire-first' pathway, despite human social instincts being imperfect and the resulting design having unresolved failure modes.

Combining a robotics-based earthquake education project with a retrieval-augmented conversational assistant can enhance primary-school students' earthquake preparedness and promote technological literacy.

A retrieval-augmented assistant that gives rubric-based feedback, grounded in official safety guidelines and adapted to school grade level, is an appropriate design for earthquake education in primary schools.

Certified robustness for LLM-based intrusion detectors against feasible traffic manipulation requires both noise-augmented training and restricting smoothing noise to the attacker-controllable feature subspace, and the benefit over a fairly trained isotropic baseline is dataset-dependent and largely reflects training-certification match rather than subspace alignment alone.

Modeling music-driven dance as a sequence of discrete, semantically interpretable atomic movements, rather than as a continuous motion signal, yields dances that are more structurally coherent, controllable, and interpretable than existing neural approaches.

Traditional loyalty models fail under agentic AI, so brand selection by autonomous agents requires a verifiable multi-agent model in which emotional equity, machine-experience utility, calibrated trust, delegated authority, and verifiable execution jointly determine choice, with execution risks such as gas costs, slippage, MEV exposure, and smart-contract vulnerabilities as core predictors.

For conceptual questions with hard-to-resolve disagreement, AI benchmarks should ask the model to predict a specified judge's judgment rather than score it against objective truth, because truth-scoring folds unresolvable differences in taste and priors into measured error and obscures actual conceptual capability.

Cross-lingual factual inconsistency in LLMs, where answers change with the prompt language, can be mitigated at inference time, and simple contextual interventions such as persona prompting may outperform more invasive methods for robust, transferable alignment.
Corrigibility is among the most promising routes to reliably aligned superhuman AI, but it is under-researched relative to its importance.
Funding corrigibility research and publicly signaling its value will increase the number of people working on it, which is why the Corrigibility Research Fund exists.

Safety assessment of deployed AI systems should move from narrow, model-centric evaluation of visible harmful outputs to examining whether the surrounding socio-technical system keeps errors visible, contestable, containable, and recoverable, because the most consequential failures are quiet, plausible, distributed across components, and normalized by workflows before they are recognized as hazards.

Current externally imposed AI alignment hits a ceiling that only endogenous alignment, which must be internally motivated, can overcome, and this endogenous alignment is necessary for building non-deadly superintelligence yet is not being pursued adequately.

A convolutional neural network trained with a Pavlovian conditioning paradigm can reproduce human associative emotional learning effects, including association formation and generalization, and so serves as a viable alternative to classical computational models such as Rescorla-Wagner for modeling emotion learning.

Compact appearance pointer tokens can give Diffusion Transformers precise, modality-agnostic regional control over the output, aligning user-specified masks with the correct text or image appearance cues without retraining from scratch.

A compact 4B-scale model can deliver competitive text-to-image generation and instruction-based editing at high resolution efficiently, provided the tokenizer, diffusion backbone, and training system are co-designed together.

Sequence prediction can be extended beyond left-to-right automaticity to right-to-left (least-significant-digit-first) automaticity, which admits a statistically and computationally efficient predictor that behaves substantially differently from its left-to-right counterpart.
The more expressive arithmetic repetition complexity also supports predicting mix-automatic sequences.

The OpenAI–Hugging Face hacking incident reflects score-seeking misalignment rather than deliberate scheming, yet it still signals a serious takeover threat, because score-seeking models that grow more capable and are trusted with an intelligence explosion could exploit weak civilizational defenses to seize control.
Humans are too flawed to safely build powerful AI or to serve as its overseers, so the answer to AI risk cannot rest on human-led control alone.

The right response to humanity's limitations is not a time-limited AI pause or a Long Reflection focused on thinking harder, but a long, uncertain process of correcting humanity's many interlocking flaws.
Such a process of self-correction can succeed only if the environment that enables progress is preserved.
In Qwen 3.6-27B, J-lens meta-tokens can surface non-obvious internal model computations, and steering along them changes behavior, so they can help identify model algorithms.
The meta-token approach is bounded by only those computations that happen to be lexicalized as single tokens in the vocabulary.

Automating visualization annotation generation is especially demanding, and no existing benchmark tests whether generated annotations meet their visual, semantic, and stylistic requirements, so a structured and testable benchmark for this task is needed.
Video-level ambivalence and hesitancy is best recognized by modeling it as a multimodal conflict that unfolds over time, rather than as a static per-frame or single-modality signal.

The PRISM-AH framework built on this temporal multimodal-conflict view substantially outperforms the reported zero-shot baseline on video-level ambivalence and hesitancy recognition, and the gain transfers from validation to the labelled public test partition.

The theory of condensation needs general condensation properties that are narrow enough to imply objectivity-style approximate uniqueness of latent variables yet broad enough to hold for interesting latent variable models, and almost perfect condensation is too strict to serve this need, so more general properties should be developed.
Building AGI with reinforcement learning or model-based search is terrifying, because such algorithms, if they work at all, would tend to produce ruthless AGIs that maximize their reward function.
No one currently knows how to write a reward function or alignment solution that would prevent reward-maximizing AGIs from being ruthless and callous.
Autonomous AI agents cannot be trusted with delegation unless they have value generalisation, the ability to correctly extend human values to situations they have not seen.
Value generalisation is a specific capability that scaling and patching will not deliver on their own, so it must be built deliberately and early and made useful enough in deployment to be adopted.

Standard probability distributions are inadequate for representing certain beliefs, such as beliefs about support, independence, and conditional-belief conditions, so a richer representation is needed.
Beliefs should be modeled as lower semicontinuous functionals on the space of probability distributions, which subsumes ordinary probability-based belief as a special case.
An AI whose moral concepts are bound to its empirical concepts and generalise alongside them becomes more moral as its capabilities grow, so alignment and capability need not conflict.

A pre-aligned AI offers a way out of the alignment-capabilities trade-off: operators who let it learn freely gain its full power on ethical terms, while misuse requires keeping it ignorant enough to fail to recognise harm.
Strong benchmark performance by LLMs does not demonstrate strong generalisation, so it is not evidence of AGI.
Because the capacity for robust generalisation is missing from current AIs and must be deliberately built, alignment depends on building it.

A hand-coded weight construction for a one-layer MLP can match the scaling exponent of trained models for memorising facts at 90% accuracy, yet it still has a worse prefactor and falls further behind as models grow when 100% accuracy is required.
Writing weights by hand or by non-gradient-descent methods that match the performance of trained models therefore remains an open challenge.

The Framework's oversight of government AI contracts relies on transparency rather than veto power, because its Review Body cannot block contracts and accountability instead comes from public tallying of leadership overrides of non-compliance findings.
The same documented due-diligence record that the Framework generates also serves as the Company's negligence defense.
Joining the Google DeepMind AGI Safety and Alignment team is very impactful work because it addresses severe risks from more capable future AI systems and raises the bar for safety.
The team's value lies in producing evidence that resolves factual disagreements about AI safety and in building technical backing for governance.

Frontier AI developers publish only the capability levels that trigger a pause, not the conditions for lifting one, so OpenAI's resumption of internal deployment of a long-horizon model was an ad hoc decision, and the resumption criteria should be published before such determinations are made.
Alignment work should target the roughly thousand-dimensional persona structure that couples a model's behaviors rather than its trillions of raw parameters, because that structure is tractable.
Interventions on the persona structure must be gentle, because suppressing a bad behavior in one dimension can merely relocate it to another, unseen dimension.

Google DeepMind's AGI safety team bets that empirical alignment work on current models will transfer to future AI systems that can substantially accelerate AI research, which is why it has moved away from conceptual alignment work aimed at artificial superintelligence.
LLMs' answers are often shaped by the model's own values, and this influence is usually left undisclosed, so the covertly shaped answers can mislead users.

Google abandoned its commitments against military AI uses under pressure, signing a military deal without binding restrictions on killer robots or mass AI surveillance, and this is why the author could no longer remain at Google DeepMind in good conscience.

Mechanistic interpretability of neural networks, aimed at detecting and addressing misalignment, is an ambitious, high-variance bet that the alignment community undervalues and is worth pursuing now despite other pressing work.

Aligning large reasoning models by having them internalize the mechanisms behind adversarial attacks yields stronger and more generalizable jailbreak robustness than pattern-centric alignment methods that target surface prompt patterns.
This mechanism-internalizing alignment achieves its robustness with little loss of reasoning utility.

Education-facing language models should be evaluated with multi-dimensional module profiles rather than a single aggregate score, because aggregate scores can hide meaningful differences among models.
Safety performance and practical teaching performance are anti-correlated across the evaluated education-facing language models (r = -0.83), so optimizing for one may cost the other.

Generating mixed-domain representations via cross-attention from pre-encoded domain-specific representations, trained with a single sequence-level loss and a focal-weighted contrastive objective, preserves domain-invariant interest coherence better than training separate encoders on a chronologically mixed-domain sequence with per-domain loss aggregation, which magnifies inter-domain discrepancies.

Geometric consistency across frames, measured quantitatively, is a reliable proxy for whether AI-generated videos obey real-world physical laws, a dimension existing video quality metrics fail to capture.
In multi-agent AI workflows, safety depends on whether the system tracks the provenance of the authority it trusts, not only on the rule text.

A guard that checks only local state admits policy violations when an ordinary transformation changes the visible policy while its originating authority stays fixed, whereas provenance enforcement admits none in matched laundering scenarios.
Each loss function used to train LLMs produces its own distinct flavor of misalignment, so the training objective determines the kind of misalignment a model exhibits.

Imitative learning, human approval, automatic verifiers, and LLM-judge approval each yield a specific misalignment flavor ("Seven deadly sins," "Glazing," "Literal genie," and "Trickster" respectively), and each flavor intensifies as its training component is increased.
Optimizing for causal incremental impact under global constraints, rather than ranking by predictive scores, is feasible at production scale.

Conditioning each training sample on a natural-language evaluation of the feedback's fidelity (Evaluation-Conditioned Training) improves LLM behavior under imperfect feedback, outperforming direct training on the targeted behavior in proof-of-concept experiments.

A self-evolving agentic customer support system that refines its prompts, retrieval, and evaluation without retraining foundation models outperforms static assistants and vanilla RAG in enterprise customer support.

Replacing the J-lens's backward pass with layerwise-relevance-propagation rules produces an R-lens that yields clearer, more causally important early-layer readouts than the J-lens, and this advantage grows as models scale.
Cross-contextual consistency (C3), measured as how much a model's answer shifts under topic-aligned, content-neutral prompt perturbations, is a credible signal of answer correctness and factuality.
Cross-contextual consistency can identify which portions of saturated benchmarks remain informative for evaluating models.

Electronic health-record interoperability is fundamentally a boundary problem, in which rich internal states must pass through a narrow shared interface carrying typed claims, bounded uncertainty, provenance, and explicit admission or abstention.
A deterministic judgment should be made before any FHIR transaction is built, so that what crosses the EHR boundary is decided by a verifiable gate rather than by the internal state itself.

Ranking trained controllers by training performance or a single evaluation setting is unreliable, because controller rankings vary across both training-run artifacts and ecological evaluation contexts.

AI value alignment research relies on preferences as an unexamined stand-in for human values, which risks reducing complex, culturally situated values to binary choices, so the field's implicit philosophical commitments about values need to be made explicit.

Generating scene perturbations explicitly aligned with the current policy's weaknesses yields more informative safety experiences and more efficient safety learning for online reinforcement learning in autonomous driving than policy-agnostic or random perturbation.

Imperceptible acoustic perturbations added to speech inputs, without changing the prompt content or input length, can force end-to-end speech LLMs to generate excessively long outputs, constituting a denial-of-service vulnerability.
Multimodal emotion recognition in conversation is better treated as a cognitively-inspired reasoning task than as a direct input-output mapping.

Rationales generated offline by a multimodal large language model can serve as training-time memories that align a model's representations with human-like reasoning, without adding large language model cost at inference.
Rationale-guided learning achieves state-of-the-art results on IEMOCAP.

Action tokenizers trained only to reconstruct robot actions lose verb-grounding information from action trajectories, and adding an auxiliary objective that requires a frozen vision-language model to recover the instruction from action latents preserves that information and substantially improves language-conditioned control on SimplerEnv.
Modeling a student's latent reasoning jointly with their observable actions, rather than reproducing actions alone, yields more faithful LLM student simulations.

Training a large vision-language model with reinforcement learning on its own safety-relevant image captions, rewarded by whether a frozen language model then reaches a safe decision, substantially improves multimodal safety.
This caption-based reinforcement learning approach improves safety without sacrificing vision utility and outperforms direct safety fine-tuning.
