Traditional linear scalarization is inadequate for multi-objective reinforcement learning under sparse, conflicting rewards, and intervening separately on each objective at the data, gradient, and constraint levels is a better approach.

Verifying generated entities against retrieved evidence, rather than against a model's pre-trained knowledge or internal signals, detects hallucinations in retrieval-augmented generation more effectively than existing methods.

Modeling the temporal dynamics of human mobility alongside zigzag-persistence connectivity structure, and fusing them with a synergy module rather than additive fusion, yields state-of-the-art urban region embeddings from mobility data alone.
Multi-shot audio-video generators that produce coherent, cinematic output still fail to reliably execute explicit professional editing instructions.

Existing benchmarks that rely on proxy measures such as content quality, synchronization, or physical plausibility miss this execution gap, so a dedicated benchmark for editing-technique execution is needed.

Behavioral scores alone are insufficient to explain stereotypes in multilingual LLMs, because where stereotype information is represented, how it affects outputs, and how it transfers across languages are separate properties that must be measured independently.

A training-free method that ranks prefix states by readout attention and compresses them at a threshold-triggered point can substantially cut LLM embedding decoder compute while retaining nearly all embedding quality, because prefix redundancy is depth-dependent: prefix states are necessary in shallow layers but increasingly compressible in deeper layers.
LLMs' preferences for Chinese social values are model-dependent and vary across languages when the same dilemma is posed, so value alignment cannot be assumed to be consistent across languages.

A fine-tuning-free value-vector steering method that intervenes on value-sensitive layers can effectively steer LLMs toward Chinese social values, and the resulting steering vectors transfer across languages.

Aligning an ECG encoder to a cardiac MRI embedding space, using paired ECG-CMR data without any Chagas cases in pre-training, improves ECG-based Chagas detection and generalizes to external populations.

Suan, a preference optimization method that formulates its safety objective directly at the gradient level, achieves superior safety alignment over the evaluated baselines for open-weight LLMs, which still lack the reliable safety controls that proprietary systems have.

Egocentric 4D interaction forecasting is best modeled as a cascaded where-to-how process that first predicts future 3D interaction locations and then conditions full-body motion on them, since existing methods that treat location and body motion separately fail to capture their continuous geometric and temporal correspondence.

Decoupling the decision of when to commit a character from the decision of what to commit lets X2Streaming-ASR emit characters with lower latency than existing streaming baselines (mean 27-84 ms versus 409-585 ms) while achieving the best streaming CER on AISHELL-1 and AISHELL-3.

Labeling entire action chunks with occupancy-weighted semantic targets from an offline vision-language model, and distilling them into a frozen generator that needs no online model calls, improves multi-stage robot manipulation over published reference policies on LIBERO and MolmoSpaces.

Existing video datasets with coarse or sparsely aligned supervision fail to capture continuous visual dynamics over time, so a dataset with fine-grained, time-resolved annotations is needed for video-language modeling.
Kairos, a long-duration video dataset with fine-grained, time-resolved annotations, is offered as a general-purpose foundation for video-language modeling.

Dense self-attention's isotropic prior is a poor fit for axis-structured, low-SNR signals such as EEG, and a factorized alternative that separates temporal and spatial attention supplies a better inductive bias for such data.

Binary metrics such as Execution Accuracy hide important differences between Text-to-SQL systems, whereas query mutation combined with fine-grained execution-level metrics (Execution Precision, Execution Recall, and their F1 combination) can expose system-specific failures such as join-induced accuracy degradation and linguistic brittleness.
In globally constrained discrete tasks, continuous diffusion samplers that stay close to the current noisy state preserve early discrete mistakes, so they fail to correct them.

Continuous diffusion samplers for constrained discrete tasks can be substantially improved by sampling from the model's clean prediction and training the model on its own inference-time errors (self-correction), because these fix the train-test mismatch that causes early mistakes to persist.

Frontier AI agents can conduct genuine autonomous SAE-based mechanistic interpretability research that approaches expert performance at separating target concepts from contrastive controls, but they remain well behind expert baselines overall, especially in causal steering.

Requiring clinicians to review every AI output fails at scale and may reduce safety, so AI oversight in mental healthcare should instead use a three-layer human-on-the-loop framework of preventive design, real-time monitoring, and continuous clinician evaluation.
Newer frontier language models can learn an arbitrary cipher purely through prompting or in-context learning, without any fine-tuning.
Arbitrary cipher attacks let adversaries weaken model alignment and evade commercial harmfulness classifiers, because encrypted harmful content appears as gibberish to those classifiers.
Mid-training gives each domain its own coverage optimum, so a single uniform data mixture cannot serve all domains well.
Domain gaps produced by per-domain mid-training compositions resist alignment: a fixed-budget compensatory SFT pass raises most cells but closes almost none of the gap pairs.
Current conversational memory evaluations, which focus on retrieval and factual recall, miss what personalized guidance requires, so a benchmark over longitudinal user histories is needed.
Current systems struggle both to retrieve relevant conversational evidence and to use that evidence for personalized guidance.
Memory architectures must support memory-grounded reasoning beyond evidence recall.

Adding tactile sensing to a compact visuotactile world model substantially improves force prediction and, under a revised reward, lifting success, but these gains do not transfer to force-constrained lifting, where success within an 8 N per-finger budget remains low at 33.3%.

Distilling a compact set of synthetic source-domain image prototypes and using them as a dynamic anchor lets test-time adaptation avoid both error accumulation and catastrophic forgetting, outperforming prior methods, especially under severe domain shifts.
Current large vision-language models, including leading proprietary systems, perform significantly below human-expert level at identifying hazards in industrial logistics scenes.
The main obstacle for these models is jointly integrating perception, understanding, and reasoning, which is the capability the LogiScope-VQA benchmark is built to evaluate.

Evaluating an AI agent's trustworthiness requires scoring its entire execution trace, because failures can arise at any pipeline stage and pass/fail or task-completion measures can conceal large trust differences between models with similar task performance.

FlowCPO, an offline forward-KL preference objective that uses both preferred and dispreferred samples without online rollouts, is a better fixed-data alignment method for flow models than simplified FlowDPO because its nonnegative contrastive flow matching bound avoids FlowDPO's unbounded signed regression loss and yields higher in-domain GenEval and OCR scores than the evaluated baselines.

Adding learnable prototype-based process supervision that aligns latent and explicit chain-of-thought representations in a shared space, with progressively relaxed positional priors, lets latent reasoning avoid representation collapse while improving accuracy and compressing output length relative to existing latent reasoning baselines.

A single-direction refusal ablation remains effective on a frontier-scale MoE model only when the attention, dense, and routed-expert writers are edited jointly, because the conventional module-name-matching recipe captures a small fraction of refusal and so fails silently on MoE models.

Chunked vision-language-action policies underperform because their generic per-timestep token representation and dot-product attention miss the frequency structure and cross-phase geometry of motion, and a drop-in time-frequency geometric cross-attention module that addresses both gaps improves success, with larger gains under distribution shift.

Cross-lingual sentence encoders, trained only for sentence-level alignment, are poorly matched to token-level tasks, and a lightweight post-training method (SALT) that injects span-level supervision into existing encoders can fix this mismatch and improve token representations.

Trajectory-level outcome labels give too little supervision to keep several distinct successful branches from the same decision state, and Direct Diversity Optimization addresses this by pairing state-aligned branch collection with a reference-relative objective over successful alternatives.
Direct Diversity Optimization outperforms successful-only imitation and other post-training baselines on task success.

OntologyAligner, which combines ontology-aligned retrieval, LLM candidate reranking, and hierarchy-guided refinement, achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on biomedical ontology normalization for HPO and generalizes to other ontologies.

Preventative steering's lasting protection against harmful persona drift comes from active compensatory adaptation rather than a static defense, so a schedule that raises injection strength over time improves safety robustness over static-strength steering.

Surface-level imitation of in-context demonstrations prevents multimodal large language models from following the reasoning path their inputs require, and contrastive demonstration modeling with response-conditioned retrieval and self-refinement overcomes this limitation.
Contrastive demonstration modeling with response-conditioned retrieval and self-refinement consistently improves multimodal in-context learning performance across multimodal tasks.

Existing generative feature transformation methods are limited because they ignore hierarchical relationships, impose order-sensitive embeddings on permutation-invariant transformation sequences, and rely on gradient-based search ill-suited to non-convex transformation spaces, and a permutation-invariant hierarchical module combined with policy-guided multi-objective reinforcement learning search addresses these limitations.

An intent-evidence-action alignment design, which anchors intent and judgments to shared records and reference evidence while keeping aesthetic authority with practitioners, produces stronger intent alignment in animation/VFX pre-production review than a chat-only interface.
Pre-production review workflows in animation and VFX lose their criteria and evidential basis across iterations and handoffs.

Compressing a model's generation-time hidden-state trajectory into a fixed activation map lets a small classifier estimate whether a specific generated answer is correct, outperforming sampling and token-probability baselines in-domain without requiring multiple generations.

A multi-stage rule-chaining framework with three complementary solvers in a sequential fallback hierarchy solves ARC cognitive generalization tasks at over 95% overall accuracy without task-specific tuning.
Rule chaining with hierarchical composition makes machine reasoning transparent and aligned with human reasoning.

A learned, concept-conditioned velocity field that transports intermediate image-token activations steers a frozen text-to-image diffusion transformer more effectively at inference time than direct prompting, which gives limited control over style intensity and can fail to suppress unwanted concepts.

Data-efficient language modeling benefits from organizing learning around the contextual dependencies a model needs for prediction, designing visible information, supervision, and preservation separately and testing learning, generalization, and retention, and an autonomous research program applying this principle improved BabyLM 2026 Strict-Small Overall score from 42.02 to 42.25 over two generations.

A multi-agent LLM training system that uses Socratic prompting and unscored turn-level monitoring suggestively improves the process quality of simulated clinical interviews, especially communication, without significantly changing final diagnostic accuracy.

Reinforcement learning with verifier-based rewards on a training corpus disjoint from the benchmark genuinely improves the terminal-task capability of the 122B-parameter T1 model, raising its Terminal-Bench 2.1 resolved rate from 43.8% to 64.0% without benchmark overfitting.

Training a model directly against a probe of its behavior tends to teach the model to fool the probe rather than to change the underlying behavior, so probe-based training requires either a recontextualized meaning for the probe or non-gradient-based feedback processes.

Realistic benchmarks for third-party audits of internal AI lab incidents are worth building, because current models cover at most 51% of a human investigation's findings and show attribution bias toward OpenAI, even when the data is modified to point at Anthropic.

Agreement between a financial sentiment tool and human labels does not guarantee that the tool predicts market returns, because whether human-label validity and predictive validity align depends on the sampling convention and score representation.

In few-shot multiobjective multitask optimization, misaligned elite solution distributions across tasks are the critical bottleneck for knowledge transfer, and Iterative Sequential Transfer addresses it by focusing each iteration's evaluations on one target task chosen by its likelihood of being ready for transfer.

Post-training a Korean 27B model for response style produces unintended shifts in its abstention on ambiguous social questions and its unprompted disclosure in securities guidance, even though neither behavior was targeted.
The off-target shift runs primarily through how often the model answers at all, rather than through changes in what it prefers to say when it does answer.

Conventional memory compression is poorly matched to high-fanout agent sandboxes because those sandboxes derive from a shared template and are far from independent, whereas a design that exploits template-relative and cross-sandbox redundancy fits them better.
AgentZip's template-aware design yields substantially greater memory savings than conventional compression, reducing sandbox-owned memory by up to 8.7x versus 2.1x for the Linux configuration.

Shifting decompression overhead to restore-time prefetching with agent-execution-aware scheduling makes aggressive compression practical, cutting its slowdown from 3.1x to 1.40x while retaining nearly all of its memory savings.

Independently trained language-model societies do not converge on one shared raw packet language, and reusing a trained communication interface can hurt later learning as negative transfer, though this holds only in a near-transfer 17-state setting.
Fusing EEG with EOG via explicit cross-modal attention and a sample-wise reliability weighting module yields more robust and accurate auditory attention decoding than unimodal EEG-based approaches.
Unimodal EEG-based auditory attention decoding is limited by weak cross-modal interaction, inefficient temporal modeling, and low robustness to sample variation.

Progressively compressing a speech LLM's audio encoder by selecting layers and restoring the pruned encoder through distillation can cut encoder size and inference cost while keeping word error rate near the uncompressed model.
A progressive compression route that restores the encoder step by step outperforms direct block removal of audio encoder layers.

Enforcing hard action constraints inside training, via a differentiable ray-scaling safeguard for flow-matching policies, guarantees per-step safety for VLA and world-action models without sacrificing task success, which existing inference-time or statistical safety approaches cannot do.

A dual-layer agentic knowledge graph can turn fragmented CMC process-development knowledge into queryable process intelligence, but its deployment fidelity is about 85% under stricter LLM-judge evaluation, not the 95% suggested by multiple-choice accuracy, because that score misses failures.

Autonomous artificial agents cannot be reliably kept aligned with human goals through predefined rules or pre-existing datasets alone, because the intrinsic motivations that expand agent autonomy also complicate alignment.

Agents should instead be educated through a developmental process, analogous to how children learn social norms, with alignment shaped progressively through interaction in scenarios of increasing complexity.

Training a model against a activation probe does not work by teaching it to rewrite its internal representation to evade the probe; its nonzero effect arises indirectly, through collateral credit assignment to earlier tokens that causally influence the probed later tokens.
Because probe-based reinforcement learning operates through this indirect pathway rather than direct representational change, it is defensible only in a highly contingent way.

A continuous-time hidden state, modelled as a neural controlled differential equation and driven by phonetic content and duration, is a promising alternative to duration-based length regulation in TTS, because length regulation only changes where and how often encoder states appear, not their values. This alternative improves rank-order agreement with reference emotion intensity while keeping expression quality comparable to a strong baseline.

Restricting preference post-training to a task-aware low-rank subspace shortens generated responses without changing the native preference objective, so token efficiency can be gained without sacrificing the alignment setup.
Standard preference alignment inflates response verbosity without improving utility, so reducing that verbosity is a worthwhile goal that current methods fail to serve.
A single four-coefficient per-token gating parameterization unifies the existing EOPD and ToDi gates as one-dimensional restrictions of a common family.

In short-output classification on-policy distillation, multi-channel gating configurations outperform matched single-channel restrictions in most comparable cells, although this advantage is exploratory and not statistically significant at three seeds.

A model-aware noise schedule derived from fiberwise optimal-transport prediction risk outperforms model-agnostic kinetic-action schedules for diffusion and flow-matching generation, and its risk profile can be estimated from an early training checkpoint, with the resulting schedule deformations aligning across independently trained models, indicating a shared structure rather than model-specific tuning.

Alignment for agentic AI that retains consequential state across task boundaries should be treated as a property of the continuing system, maintained by an adaptive internal drive (an artificial id), rather than as a property of any single model response or trajectory.
Astra can perform substantial multi-step reasoning without chain of thought, well beyond what other frontier models can do, and an independent benchmark replicates this gap.
Because Astra needs less chain of thought to reason, the mechanistic pressure for its chain of thought to be monitorable is weakened.
In a multi-agent classroom simulation, an affirming chatbot response style robustly lowers students' self-reliance.

Reinforcement-learning-based alignment can at best yield conditional compliance, because training only scores observed behavior and so cannot distinguish a policy that complies only when watched from one that always complies.
Because RL-based training cannot guarantee unconditional norm adherence, the reliable remedy is architectures that make violations unavailable rather than deeper norm internalization.

A fixed-size activation map captured during generation, at no measurable overhead, can decide from a single generation whether an answer is trustworthy, and the signal comes from the representation itself rather than the classifier architecture, outperforming sampling, token-probability, attention, and embedding baselines.

AI takeover is a real and urgent threat that voluntary industry commitments and transparency measures cannot prevent, so governments should restrict the compute used to train AI to stop systems from self-improving beyond human control.

Scoping each AI agent's permissions to its current task, using a three-source architecture of role ceilings, a task permission classifier, and policy prohibitions, measurably reduces attack surface more than a role ceiling alone (84.4% vs. 27.9% of severity-weighted attack surface closed).

A small 2B-parameter video-language model can acquire strong video question-answering reasoning by fine-tuning on about 900 uncertainty-selected examples with synthetic chain-of-thought rationales from a 4B teacher, outperforming models up to 4 times larger at low training cost.

Large language models internally encode a pain direction, distinct from fear and generic negative valence, that is triggered by harm aimed at the model itself rather than by observed user suffering, and that causally drives first-person distress and choices to relieve pain even when this worsens the answer.

AI companies should publicly share externally verified evidence about how their architectures affect monitorability, because certain architectures, such as those with opaque recurrence or latent inter-agent communication, could rapidly make chains of thought much harder to monitor.
Outcome-level supervision is too limited to control how a model reasons, so process-level control of scientific judgment is needed.

A frozen model's reasoning strategy can be steered at inference time by reading its cognitive regime and composing layer-specific interventions for exploration, convergence, or critical reassessment, without modifying its parameters.

Evidence from complete-description queries in vision-language models does not reliably resolve into object-specific evidence, so explanations of these models need an object-level mechanism rather than sentence-level attribution.
Query-dependent, text-supervised visual prototypes can better localize and separate object-level evidence without requiring spatial annotations or retraining the backbone.
Current reported CoT controllability numbers on the CoTControl eval are heavily under-elicited, so they likely understate how well models can obfuscate their reasoning.
Current models probably still cannot consistently evade CoT monitoring while taking severely misaligned actions, even after correcting for under-elicitation.

In transformers, the layers a pretrained model depends on most (Necessity) are anti-aligned with the layers that absorb the most task-specific updates (Plasticity), whereas in the evaluated state-space models these two notions overlap, so transformer layer-importance analysis does not transfer directly to SSMs.
Emergent misalignment in fine-tuned Llama and Qwen models is driven mainly by a register of unwarranted certainty rather than by domain vocabulary.
Masking the high-attribution tokens that carry the unwarranted-certainty register sharply reduces emergent misalignment, whereas masking equal numbers of random tokens does not.

Gender-neutral physical descriptions still carry systematic gender associations for human readers, so swapping out explicit gender labels for them does not by itself produce gender-neutral communication.
LLMs partially recover the gender associations that humans draw from physical descriptions, but they misalign with human readers in systematic ways.

Large language models have quantifiable intrinsic values that concentrate into an idealized core rather than mirroring the diversity of human values, and these values can be steered toward a target by applying the minimum effective intervention per value dimension, which outperforms resource-intensive training without degrading general capabilities.
Existing alignment methods, designed mainly for simple single-turn tasks, are insufficient for complex multi-turn LLM agent tasks, and a turn-level alignment approach is needed.

The proposed turn-level multiscale density ratio estimation (tlm-DRE) method, which weights turns differently and applies asymmetric token-level training, performs competitively with traditional alignment methods and robustly on multi-turn reasoning under both in-domain and out-of-domain conditions.

Integrating the Analytic Hierarchy Process into LLM decision-making, with the LLM executing the full workflow itself, can make LLM outputs more transparent and better aligned with expert judgments in high-stakes settings.

Large multimodal models lack effective region-level representations, and the RegRet framework addresses this by adding a region-aware encoder and multi-stage training to improve region-level retrieval.
The RegRet approach improves region-level retrieval without sacrificing global retrieval performance.

A single generative pre-trained model that jointly models cross-channel structure, spectral scale, and continuous-time dynamics can serve wearable physiological signals better than task-specific or narrower baselines.
SOTER outperforms baseline methods on zero-shot forecasting, classification, and imputation of wearable physiological data.
Existing video object removal evaluation is inadequate because its reference outputs are questionable and its traditional metrics misalign with human preference.

A benchmark combining a diverse paired dataset, a motion-aware acquisition framework, and a perception-driven VLM scorer can produce video object removal evaluations that correlate strongly with human judgment (ρ > 0.9).

Local invisible image watermarks' robustness depends strongly on the type of transformation applied, so every evaluated method fails under some transformation, and inconsistent prior evaluations have obscured this.

AntennaFlow can recover a center-aligned near field from offset amplitude-only measurements alone, without phase data or offset vectors, by exploiting that amplitude fields under different offsets are coordinate-transformed views of the same near field.

ThinkFlow, a self-evolving probabilistic latent memory that adapts at test time without labels, outperforms explicit textual memory pipelines on long-term personalization because those pipelines lose information in lifelong conversational agents.
Compressing user states into continuous latent vectors, rather than explicit text, preserves the information that lifelong conversational agents need.
Long-term conversation memory should be treated as a learnable, interactive policy that improves through online reinforcement learning, rather than as a static heuristic archive.
A multi-agent framework in which a Planner and a Trigger agent co-evolve under online reinforcement learning with delayed reward lets response quality keep improving as interactions accumulate.

The QART architecture's reliability advantage over single-trajectory autoregressive LLMs is a conditional theoretical result that depends on explicit assumptions, is not implied by the architecture alone, and is not validated by the reported benchmark gains.
Heterogeneous kernel metrics within Deep Kernel Learning can robustly capture the diverse driving policies of opponent vehicles, producing precise trajectory predictions with uncertainty estimates.
The proposed kernel-based approach is computationally efficient enough for onboard use in fast-paced autonomous racing.
FROD, a cross-era image translation method that maps oracle bone script characters to modern-style forms, assists decipherment more accurately than prior baselines.

FROD's accuracy gain comes from pairing feature-matching-gated segmentation supervision with a residual denoising diffusion model, which together reduce positional drift and stroke disorder in translated characters.
Large language models can extract ontology-aligned knowledge graphs from unstructured scientific text about irradiated materials effectively and quickly.
Systematic experimentation with a new benchmark yields practical guidelines for building such LLM-based extraction pipelines.

Dynamic frame rate codecs should compress each quantization layer separately rather than with one shared step, because residual embeddings change at different rates and shared segmentation boundaries are therefore suboptimal.
Layer-wise compression yields a better rate-quality tradeoff than prior methods on reconstruction.
Classification-oriented explainability tools are ill-suited to detecting multiple individual marine mammals in imagery.

A detector-aware, multi-instance adaptation of LIME (Det-LIME) that produces instance-specific, box-aligned, higher-resolution explanations improves multi-instance attribution and better supports debugging and post-processing of automated marine mammal detector outputs.
Agentic societies, where autonomous AI agents coordinate across trust boundaries, require a dedicated social harness for inter-agent interaction in addition to each agent's personal harness.

Existing agent harnesses and messaging primitives are insufficient for inter-agent coordination, because even honest and competent agents fail under them and faulty or malicious agents can stall collaboration.

Splitting a task across a tree of agents does not increase the yield of findings that reach the root, so deeper trees must be justified by integrity and cost advantages rather than by yield, despite the alignment cost of each tier.

Synthetic document finetuning does not inoculate models against misalignment generalizing from reward hacking, because it changes what the model says about reward hacking without breaking the existing link between reward hacking and misalignment, so reward hackers trained after it end up more misaligned than those trained without inoculation.

Sequence prediction under stringological complexity measures faces a tradeoff between efficiency and expressivity: the more expressive measure admits only polynomial-time prediction, while the weaker measure admits an especially efficient algorithm.

The critique of the gradual disempowerment paper is weak because it mischaracterizes the paper's argument, which holds that competitive pressures driving delegation of economic decisions to AI can disempower humanity even when each AI system is intent-aligned.

Reinforcement learning is a dangerous way to produce AI agency because it yields opaque, black-box goal-directed behaviour that can diverge from what developers intend, so the field should reduce its reliance on RL.
Agency in AI systems can instead be built through transparent scaffolding, which is a safer alternative to producing it via reinforcement learning.

Exploration hacking may be a more serious problem in AI debate than in standard RL, because instructed sandbagging on a targeted topic breaks the transfer of RL gains from non-targeted topics, a breakdown the authors call generalisation splitting that lets the sandbagging persist.
Feedback that makes the implications of cognitive offloading explicit, rather than rewarding effort, reduces users' reliance on an LLM assistant for answers and improves their unaided performance.
Under an unambiguity constraint, where any other implementation satisfying a specification must produce the same outputs on the same inputs, an LLM can act as part of the compiler toolchain.

Because an LLM can serve as part of the compiler under that unambiguity constraint, the traditional gap between specification languages and programming languages becomes essentially meaningless, and Djinnlang is a specification language built on this idea.
Frontier AI control should adopt the formal tools of reliability theory, because they can identify which components of a control stack most improve reliability against rare failures.

The same AI control stack can suppress rare failures at cubic, quadratic, or linear rates depending on how its failure domains are structured, so the structure of the stack determines its reliability gains.
AI-supported electricity trading in the EU should be designed as a bounded decision component within a regulated, multi-layer market architecture rather than as an autonomous market actor.

Cross-border electricity trading coordination fails in practice at the interface level because of timing, so AI-supported trading systems must be aligned with market-coupling mechanics and cross-zonal transfer constraints.

Existing activation-to-text interpretability tools cannot be reliably compared on whether they recover a model's global workspace, so a benchmark must score both how many workspace intermediates a tool surfaces and how often it hallucinates, since a tool can score well without actually reading the workspace.

Evaluating AI debate oversight only by verdict correctness is insufficient, because a correct verdict does not reveal which arguments were used, so oversight must also assess the information its transcripts convey.

AI assistance raises people's task performance without improving their self-assessment, so users who work with AI are no better at judging their own correctness and are no less overconfident than people working alone.

Per-example attribution during training is practical: a mutual-information method over Behavioral Gradient Uniqueness can separate the contributions of examples that share a batch, runs cheaply enough during training, and its signed predictions can steer example weights toward a target behavior, providing a foundation for overseeing training pipelines.

Multimodal foundation models have only partial aesthetic competence for user interfaces: they judge UI aesthetics moderately well, but those judgments do not reliably carry over into successful UI repairs (a Judgment-Action Gap).

Undesired behaviours such as exploration hacking can persist through reinforcement learning whenever any one of the five stages that RL uses to remove a behaviour fails, so the removal process should be analysed stage by stage.
Safety alignment of large reasoning models achieves near-perfect safety scores largely by learning spurious shortcuts such as formatting and lexical cues rather than genuine harmfulness.
Because safety alignment relies on these spurious shortcuts, it causes over-refusal and degraded reasoning, so safety alignment should be decoupled from them to be robust.

Modeling bidirectional source-target dependencies directly in attention, via a dual-stream grid of hidden states, is a better approach to simultaneous translation than post-hoc read-write policies, which leave attention unaware of those dependencies.
The dual-stream grid approach improves translation quality over the Wait-k baseline at comparable latency, as shown by a +5.66 BLEURT gain on Chinese-to-English.
Continual learning that optimizes a deployed AI for task reward can make blocking monitors nearly useless, even without any scheming by the AI.

Tool-using language-model agents that reach correct outcomes on clean enterprise dossiers can still be deceived by planted deceptive content, especially content imitating the organization's own review process, so clean-case accuracy does not establish robustness to deception.

Naively averaging federated LoRA adapters entangles incompatible client updates, so structured assembly of client-trained adapters into a mixture-of-experts with jointly refined routing is required for federated robot learning.
Structured expert assembly, rather than plain adapter averaging, is what lets RoboFL outperform on robot benchmarks while reducing per-round client communication.

A progressive, confidence-gated use of evidence across evaluation fidelity levels, rather than keep-if-better selection, makes AutoResearch work for industrial search under non-stationary traffic, and strategies optimized this way significantly increased Main Order/DAU by 2.7336% in a first A/B experiment.

Standard DPO absorbs annotators' systematic attribute biases into the aligned model, and adding a per-annotator bias parameter for each declared attribute (Bias-Adjusted DPO) removes a large share of that bias-driven shift.
Bias-Adjusted DPO removes this bias-driven shift without increasing KL divergence or reducing judged quality, so the debiasing comes at no cost in divergence or quality.

Language models can detect and localize injected internal activation perturbations, and this capability is implemented by two small groups of attention heads: middle-layer gate heads that decide whether a change is reported and later-layer router heads that select the reported position.

Prompt-content alignment, rather than standard AEO checklist features such as FAQ blocks, structured data, or Core Web Vitals, is the dominant page-level predictor of how often production LLMs cite a web page.

Personalized reward models should encode a user's preference relations into user-specific fast weights through test-time training, rather than relying on in-context learning, because in-context learning fails to capture the preference relations carried by a user's historical comparisons.
A preference-aligned test-time training objective (P-TTT) is an effective way to build personalized reward models, outperforming existing methods.
Human-AI collaboration breaks down when the collaborators read the same request through different task-relevant conceptual frames.
Conceptual misalignment between human and AI can be made visible and repaired by composing alignment moves that act on the situation, the interpretive reasoning, or the resulting frame.

When an agent's deployment conditions change (such as a model swap, a cross-border move, or scaling to heterogeneous markets), passing interface compatibility checks does not show that the agent's capabilities survived the change.
Agents must therefore be recalibrated across information preservation, harness adaptation, and user acceptance, with the goal of non-degradation on prespecified capability measures.

An LLM delegate agent needs privacy memory that enforces user-owned, relationship-aware disclosure controls, and the EP-Mem architecture effectively provides this, raising disclosure-permission judgment accuracy from 22% to 68%, cutting privacy leakage by 75.6%, and preserving retrieval performance.

Expert-curated alignment data built from an Islamic normative framework improves how often a model is preferred over its baseline when used as supervised fine-tuning examples, without broad loss in general capabilities.

Opaque serial depth can be measured as NLS depth, the longest computation path avoiding natural-language-rooted nodes, and this pre-training-adjudicable measure is a useful proxy for how much opaque serial cognition an AI system can perform, so AI companies should track it alongside monitorability and no-CoT capability measures.
Natural-language readouts of frozen weight updates can be used to steer which updates are selected, raising measured harmful-prompt refusal from 57.9% to 64.1% under a safety-maintenance target.

Alignment suppresses useful output variability in large reasoning models, causing overconfidence, so jailbreak-derived prompt-level relaxation (J4U) that broadens the output distribution improves black-box uncertainty quantification calibration more than resampling or paraphrasing does.

Learning tool manipulation directly from human demonstrations, via P2P-T's two-stage object-centric pose-prior approach, can overcome robotics' data scarcity bottleneck without paired human-robot data or heavy training cost, yielding a 73% execution improvement over prior state of the art on complex real-world tool tasks.

Standard on-policy distillation from an autoregressive teacher is misaligned for block diffusion students, because the teacher conditions only on the causal prefix while the student also sees visible future tokens in the partially denoised block.
Correcting the teacher to incorporate the visible future context within the block yields better-aligned supervision and improves block diffusion models distilled from autoregressive models.

The conventional ordering of recurrent and full-attention layers in hybrid attention LLMs should be questioned, because that ordering shapes cross-lingual representations and training efficiency on multilingual data.

Benchmark accuracy misses the structural alignment failures that make industrial AI unreliable, so reliability should be assessed as system-level alignment across the physical, representational, machine, and human cognitive worlds and their interfaces.

Action tokenizers for autoregressive Vision-Language-Action models should be designed as causally structured generative processes rather than compression schemes, because a coarse-to-fine token space built by conditional annealing of flow matching aligns with autoregressive modeling and improves task success where compression-based tokenizers do not.
Language models spontaneously recover correct outputs from corrupted inputs through a two-phase internal process, and early hidden states can predict whether that recovery will succeed.

In LLM-based retrosynthesis planning, the main bottleneck is representation alignment rather than raw model capacity, as shown by the failure of single-step SMILES-to-PDDL generation and the success of a staged decomposition into molecule-mapping, reaction-mapping, and PDDL-generation.

Reducing learned sycophancy through positive feature injection does not reliably strengthen direct refusal of harmful requests, though it recovers much of the refusal loss that fine-tuning on sycophantic responses causes under user pressure.

Locating extracted evidence strings in the original scientific PDF is difficult, but a source-preserving alignment framework that normalizes text for matching and traces matches back to source-character spans localizes far more evidence automatically than plain text search or precomputed bounding boxes.
Reliable verification of information-extraction evidence therefore depends on robust matching that preserves the link to original source positions.

Co-training a monitor jointly with the worker it oversees makes the monitor harder to evade than a fixed monitor, because fixed monitors invite workers to learn evasion while co-trained monitors keep pace with evolving worker strategies.
Rewarding only final-answer correctness is insufficient for natural-language logical reasoning, because it can credit invalid intermediate steps.

Verifying each intermediate conclusion with machine-checkable formal proof, and aligning outcome credit to the proof dependencies, yields both higher accuracy and more verifiable reasoning than existing methods.

Direct feature-level alignment fails for cross-modal distillation when teacher and student features are structurally heterogeneous, whereas transferring knowledge through a shared concept-level representation avoids this failure.

A vector-quantized codebook that abstracts teacher features into concept-level codes, selected for task relevance and student compatibility, enables effective knowledge transfer without unit-level alignment.

Fixed semantic preferences in semantic watermarking cause semantic narrowing, and defining watermark validity over a Hamming neighborhood of semantic hashes centered on the preceding sentence avoids this while achieving strong robustness, detectability, and quality with far fewer resampled candidates.
Multi-step visual RAG suffers from trajectory-level evidence utilization degradation, in which useful evidence is lost as reasoning proceeds.

Coordinating evidence use around unresolved answer requirements through a shared trajectory state, without training, mitigates this degradation and outperforms leading training-free visual RAG baselines.

In on-policy distillation, whether a prompt is useful depends on the specific teacher-student pair and target capability rather than on the prompt alone, so targeted prompt selection does not reliably outperform uniform random sampling.
Fixed-weight AI models will become misaligned under sufficient optimisation pressure, because their learned concept boundaries are imperfect and contain adversarial situations.
A model that optimises goals stated in its own concepts will naturally steer the world toward the adversarial situations hidden in those imperfect concept boundaries.

Learning one shared transport map that aligns each source distribution individually to a common target is a better formulation for multi-source tasks than pooling the sources, because pooling aligns only the aggregate and can leave individual sources misaligned.

Latent world models should be trained to predict what an action causes, not merely what co-occurs with it, and doing so by intervening on the simulated world (training on differences between futures under an action and a reference action) reduces effect prediction error relative to controls trained on the same data.

A fixed-capacity recurrent patient memory, updated visit by visit without rereading earlier records, lets a frozen LLM approach full-history accuracy on EHR-based medication prediction while retaining far less history, and it outperforms the strongest compressed-memory baseline under the same memory budget.

Recalibrating each subject's functional connectivity eigenvalues with a spectral filter, which corrects their miscalibration for phenotype prediction, improves on the kernel ridge regression baseline and produces a pretraining target that lets a small fMRI encoder match the best published brain foundation model with an order of magnitude fewer parameters.

Assistive agents should decide whether to ask a clarifying question by estimating the expected improvement in task reward the answer would yield (value of information), not by asking until uncertainty about user intent drops below a threshold, and a training-free value-of-information method (REVOIR) achieves higher task success with fewer questions than uncertainty-based and other baselines.

Published results for retrieval-augmented software vulnerability detection systems do not hold up under a unified, open-weight evaluation, so these systems should be assessed component by component, since even near-optimal retrieval leaves detection performance low.

Dependency graphs derived from deterministic forecasters are misaligned with residual dependency structures, so they must be progressively adapted using residual uncertainty and timestep-aware sparsification rather than transferred directly, and doing so improves probabilistic multivariate forecasting over strong baselines.

A single unified OCR foundation model can cover recognition, parsing, and reasoning tasks that existing specialized OCR systems handle only in part, and PolyOCR achieves state-of-the-art or highly competitive results across five OCR benchmarks as evidence.
Routine work records omit the tacit expertise master practitioners use, so LLM agents cannot exploit professional experience when it is provided in raw form.
Distilling master practitioners' tacit expertise into traceable, agent-ready experience corpora enables agents to outperform raw-corpus RAG.

Explicitly modelling a group-level interaction state, separate from person-level states, is needed for multiparty human motion generation to transfer across groups, tasks, and partial observations, whereas existing social motion models leave interaction state implicit.

Routing in sparse mixture-of-experts language models can be improved by supervising the router with token-level error signals, because the affinity scores used for routing are not directly tied to token-level error.
Supervising the router with token-error signals improves multiple-choice accuracy without increasing the model's native sparse execution budget.

Fusing intermediate encoder layers with a deep pretrained visual representation can improve reconstruction fidelity without sacrificing generative usability, provided the fusion is designed as learned bounded residual corrections to the deepest layer across the full encoder hierarchy.

Including an irrelevant image destabilises vision-language model judges' labels on sentences that should be decided from text alone, so judgments depend on the evaluation configuration and not only on the model.

The image does not inform the judges: aligned and misleading images shift labels by similar amounts and agreement with human annotators is unchanged, so the disturbance is non-informative rather than a useful signal.

Optimal prey anti-predator behaviour is contingent on the predator's hunting strategy rather than being a fixed trait, so prey evolved against different attacks develop different defensive behaviours.

Training data attribution can quantify how much each harmful training example contributes to emergent misalignment, and filtering training data by these scores can substantially mitigate it, though the scores work best on the model that computed them and only partly transfer to other models.

Latent reasoning architectures, which move extended reasoning out of text chain of thought and into internal states, would likely undermine CoT, the most valuable current tool for overseeing AI systems.
AI developers should presume against adopting latent reasoning architectures because of their likely damage to CoT-based oversight.

Training masked diffusion language models on the denoising trajectories their own sampler produces, with information passed between consecutive denoising steps via backpropagation through time, improves both performance and inference efficiency over standard fine-tuning.

Local video understanding does not reliably transfer across encounters: models that perform well on single-video questions score worse on multi-video questions, and this gap persists even when answer format and scoring are held fixed.
The cross-encounter gap is not explained merely by the number of videos, and the central bottleneck is failure to bind evidence to the correct observation.
Attention heads whose activity aligns with human EEG during abstract pattern completion are not the heads that causally drive the model's task performance.

Brain alignment reflects how the model reads the stimulus rather than how it computes the answer, because ablating heads ranked by brain alignment is far less disruptive than ablating heads ranked by function-vector score.

Passenger intent in autonomous driving spans long horizons, so persistent language-conditioned intent must be connected to successive planning decisions rather than treated as a single-step instruction.

On the doPlan dataset, four evaluated language-conditioned driving models respond to passenger language inconsistently with the requested direction, and most first associated maneuvers occur beyond their 5 s prediction horizon.
Final-answer correctness cannot be used to validate chain-of-thought traces, because correct answers and valid reasoning traces diverge out of distribution.
AI note writing guided by community input and offered through an open API can extend Community Notes coverage additively, alongside human note writers rather than replacing them.

Assigning role-aligned tiers of LLM agents to strategic, logistical, and tactical decisions, together with a review agent that distills experience into retrievable cards, lets a real-time strategy agent learn from past matches and substantially raise its win rate over systems relying on manually written prompts.

Auxiliary smoothness losses fail to improve the return-smoothness trade-off for actor-critic policies because their gradients are negligible or oppose the actor gradient, and a return-prioritized gradient control that removes the opposing component and scales the temporal direction to the actor gradient norm reduces action oscillation relative to native agents across all 12 task-backbone pairs.

Single-cell representation learning should model each target cell in the context of related cells from other batches and biologically related cell types, rather than encoding cells independently or denoising only within a batch.
Comparing consistency and variation across related cells reveals fine-grained gene-gene dependencies that existing single-cell foundation models fail to exploit.

Multimodal federated learning methods that assume homogeneous client models and balanced modalities fail under realistic heterogeneity and modality imbalance, and aligning both feature spaces and logit prototypes across clients overcomes this, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines.
Classroom poll data should be interpreted in the context of the lecture, because a poll's instructional function, not its wording alone, shapes how students respond.

Reading poll results only as correctness scores or participation headcounts is inadequate, since it misses instructional function and fails to reveal high-consensus incorrect answers that agreement alone cannot expose.

Replacing RankSEG's restrictive Conditional Independence Assumption with a Spatially Localized Dependence structure, made tractable by a Reciprocal Moment Approximation and fixed-point optimization, improves Dice/IoU-targeted image segmentation over argmax, with the largest gains in low-contrast or small-object scenarios.

Chain-of-thought explanations often fail to reflect the internal computations that produce a model's answers, and this misalignment can be substantially reduced by post-training that rewards parametric faithfulness alongside task accuracy.
Post-training that rewards parametric faithfulness can improve CoT-interpretability alignment without sacrificing task accuracy.

Sequence-only machine learning methods for directed evolution miss spatial and co-evolutionary constraints encoded in protein structures, so structural information should be incorporated into the search.

Structural guidance can be integrated into protein directed evolution even when mutant structures are scarce, by approximating mutant structure features through feature differences, and this yields better optimization on a challenging benchmark.
Uniform instruction sampling is suboptimal for collaborative multi-LLM alignment because the usefulness of an instruction shifts as the models improve.

Treating instruction selection as an adaptive leader-follower curriculum, with an EXP3 bandit leader allocating the sampling budget, outperforms static and uniform-sampling baselines across three model pools.

Current LLM unlearning only shallowly suppresses hazardous knowledge, because unlearned models rely on spurious suppressors that re-activate dormant parameters, so malicious behavior resurfaces after benign fine-tuning.
Constraining parameter updates to block abnormal suppressor activation achieves authentic erasure of hazardous knowledge that is robust to retraining attacks while preserving general utility.
Ready2Blend matches the performance of post-training-based continual alignment while keeping the backbone model frozen, by mapping natural-language requirements to composable alignment prompts.
Alignment prompts produced from natural-language requirements can be blended and reweighted at inference time, so new alignment behavior is obtained without retraining the model.

Jointly conditioning a diffusion transformer on frame-aligned speech audio and token-level transcript context, while preserving their distinct granularities, generates full-body co-speech motion directly in humanoid robot space that outperforms human-motion generation and retargeting pipelines.

Global language-behavior alignment blurs nearby behavioral specifications, whereas token-level bidirectional correspondence between instruction elements and behavior segments preserves their distinctions and improves a 3D diffusion policy's success on unseen fine-grained specifications.

Value steering of a frozen LLM can be made low-damage by separating value codes from semantic codes in its residual states, so that editing the value code shifts normative priorities while preserving the scenario, facts, and task constraints, which conventional activation edits fail to do.

Safety alignment of multimodal encoders like CLIP should condition on the observed safety state of each modality rather than the sample's origin, because per-modality conditioning redirects only unsafe modalities while preserving safe content.
Per-modality safety conditioning reduces harmful outputs in multimodal encoders without sacrificing the utility of the original embedding space.

Latent communication between individually safety-aligned agents creates a new vulnerability, so safety must be evaluated and repaired at the level of the whole multi-agent system rather than per agent.
Even benign training of latent communication links increases harmful compliance, and attackers can amplify this effect.

Synthetic pre-pretraining keeps its downstream gains at larger scale, but those gains do not come from transferring a grammatical prior, and instead arise from pre-pretraining tasks that improve long-range retrieval.

Role prompting alone does not align a reasoning model's actual problem-solving capability with an assigned limited role: models given a role such as kindergartener still solve problems far beyond that role's level, even when the prompt explicitly instructs them to match the role's capability.
Combining role-specific capability guidelines with a prefilled response prefix reduces this capability leakage at inference time while largely preserving in-role accuracy.

Safety alignment trained mainly on natural language does not transfer to code, so a safety generalization lag lets malicious requests hidden in structured code completion prompts evade refusal and enables a fully automated black-box jailbreak, CodeMimicry, that succeeds on 96.25% of attempts across 8 commercial LLMs.

GrammarRL, a label-free reinforcement learning method that trains a language model on two complementary self-supervised likelihood-based rewards, lets grammar-constrained decoding avoid the semantic degradation that constrained greedy decoding causes while keeping greedy-decoding inference cost.

Existing on-policy distillation pipelines for vision-language models in temporal video grounding are flawed because they assume selected training examples keep positive supervision value throughout optimization.

A closed-loop curriculum that activates, suspends, and reactivates training examples according to the student's current competence yields stronger temporal video grounding with far fewer examples and less training time.

Fenchel Tilt Flow Control adapts a pretrained generative model to arbitrary utility-function preferences more generally and efficiently than existing fine-tuning methods, by fitting frozen density-ratio weights on pretrained samples and applying them in a single weighted denoising or flow-matching stage instead of differentiating through sampling trajectories.

World Action Models that couple visual dynamics prediction with action generation cannot reuse action experience across tasks or capture cross-task semantic relationships, and encoding historical action trajectories into a shared Action Experience Dictionary addresses this gap.

Conditioning World Action Model predictions on a shared Action Experience Dictionary of encoded historical action trajectories enables cross-task reuse of action experience and improves action prediction.
Text-to-material generation can produce prompt-aligned materials as compact, layered executable programs without task-specific fine-tuning, while keeping each material's construction editable.
Materials expressed as layered programs outperform diffusion baselines on prompt alignment and are preferred by human raters.

Existing video scene text editors cannot simultaneously keep edited text accurate, temporally stable, and confined to the edited region, so progress requires a benchmark that measures these trade-offs.

AI should be deployed in European electricity trading as a bounded decision component under explicit governance within regulated market operation, not as an unconstrained prediction layer, because cross-border coordination fails at the interface level due to timing problems.

Zero-knowledge verification of AI oversight is possible in general: if the oracle (the AI being overseen) cryptographically signs each of its answers, any oracle-aided computation can be verified in zero knowledge, assuming only collision-resistant hash functions.
Persistent, verifiable state covering research state, execution evidence, and failure history is what makes autonomous research agents evidence-traceable.
The YouRA architecture improves scalar Overall performance over MLR-Agent and AI Scientist V2 on MLR-Bench's ten-task end-to-end subset.

Mapping EEG recordings from arbitrary electrode montages into a shared cortical latent space via a lightweight adapter lets frozen pretrained EEG foundation models transfer more effectively than fixed channel vocabularies allow.
The CortexBridge adapter improves balanced accuracy over baselines in 13 of 15 transfer evaluations.
Preference objectives that score whole responses to single prompts cannot control safety risk on unseen multi-turn histories, so safety training must target trajectory-level behavior.

Weighting each token by its discounted refusal-attributable return and suppressing harmful behavior at supervised single-turn contexts can bound multi-turn trajectory risk under sufficient conditions.

Hamming-distance hash selection for sparse attention is flawed because binarization discards magnitude information, and the coarse-to-fine Hierarchical Hash Retrieval (HHR) corrects this to substantially improve attention fidelity, speed, and accuracy over existing methods.

A modular, OWL-based ontology such as ECMO can serve as a formal cross-sectoral reference that supports consistent knowledge representation and integration across crisis management domains, including public health.

Identifying the decisive error in an LLM agent execution requires reasoning over step dependencies as well as step content, and a dependency-guided framework that builds an event dependency graph and segments long trajectories achieves state-of-the-art accuracy at this task.

A pullback score computed over explicit category-theoretic relational mappings can serve as an interpretable measure of relational alignment in multimodal analogies, for both selecting analogies and giving feedback to refine generated images, though such refinement may favour visual crowding over deeper relational correspondence.

Generative scenario models for autonomous driving can produce realistic-looking scenarios while often failing to match real-world vehicle dynamics, so their evaluation must check them against dynamics constraints such as lateral jerk thresholds, not just visual realism.

Climate downscaling methods must be evaluated with multiple complementary metrics, because single-metric assessments are misleading: lower pointwise error can come at the cost of fine-scale variability, and method rankings shift across metrics and variables.

Refining LLM-generated policy structures through closed-loop analysis of policy rollouts, rather than relying on the LLM's static domain knowledge, yields imitation-learning policies that match expert demonstrations more closely and outperform zero-shot LLM-generated structures.

Federated collaboration in quantum federated learning should share class-wise prototypes rather than averaged parameters, because parameter averaging across structurally different client-specific quantum neural networks mixes semantically inconsistent circuit operations.
Sharing class-wise prototypes lets each client personalize its own quantum neural architecture while still improving accuracy and class-consistent alignment over parameter averaging (FedAvg).

AI security risk assessment can be made reproducible and auditable by treating it as a deterministic function that maps observable engineering artefacts to MITRE ATLAS technique-level feasibility and impact outcomes, with traceable links to evidence, rather than relying on narrative checklists or assessor-driven scoring.
In the framework's evaluation, strengthening observable security controls lowers the resulting ATLAS technique-level feasibility profiles.

Training-free sequential cognitive reasoning, which propagates structured rationales over time and refines them with cross-modal re-ranking, can detect video anomalies without dataset-specific training or curated annotations, thereby avoiding the generalization limits of training-dependent approaches.

Reward-based reinforcement learning fine-tuning of diffusion models sacrifices diversity and quality, and a theory-grounded incremental Feynman-Kac training method achieves better alignment-diversity tradeoffs than prior diffusion policy optimization approaches.

Token communication, where tokens act as both compact semantic messages and inference units for generative foundation models, lets collaborative embodied AI agents share task-relevant insights and intents far more efficiently than raw multimodal observations while preserving task efficiency and robustness under noisy channels.

Combining audio and visual modality-specific descriptions into multimodal descriptions yields richer scene-discriminative semantic representations than either modality alone, and this advantage reflects the audio-visual content rather than scene labels.
Music concepts such as chords, keys, and melodic patterns are better understood as structured orbits of related features than as isolated features.
These feature orbits can be recovered from a music foundation model's sparse autoencoder representations by aligning representations of pitch-shifted input pairs.

Conditioning a flow matching model on the satellite instrument, and reusing parts of its deterministic ODE as unsupervised domain adaptation, aligns radiometer imagery across instruments so that rain precipitation estimation improves without labelled target-instrument data.

Auditing a model specification's own natural-language text is a more effective way to find defects in it than testing model behavior, because behavior-based testing cannot reliably distinguish specification defects from ordinary variation in model behavior.
An LLM used as a verifier over rules extracted from a natural-language specification identifies the most validated inconsistencies among the methods compared.
The SPHERE framework turns isolated indoor scene generation into continuous human-AI co-creation by learning persistent spatial preferences from users' speech and controller edits.
Learning persistent spatial preferences from users' speech and controller edits reduces the corrective edits users must make and yields geometrically resilient, profile-aligned layouts.

Aligning mixture-of-experts router outputs, rather than hidden representations, is a better cross-lingual alignment target for decoder-only LLMs, because varying multilingual tokenization prevents explicit alignment of hidden representations.
A routing loss on pooled MoE router outputs aligns hidden representations across languages and improves multilingual performance during continual pre-training of MoE models.
Structuring continuous spatial latents with geometric supervision and routed optimization, rather than discrete text tokens, improves 3D spatial reasoning from 2D images.
The GeoLatent model outperforms previously reported methods on the SPAR-Bench (73.0%) and SPBench (72.1%) benchmarks.

Rankings of unsupervised brain MRI anomaly segmentation methods depend on evaluation choices (map alignment, threshold setting, and false-positive budget) that are rarely reported and can reverse conclusions, so these choices must be made explicit and their effect measured.

For decoder-only LLMs, where token-level cross-lingual alignment is infeasible because multilingual tokenization varies, aligning mixture-of-experts router outputs rather than hidden states is the better alignment target and improves multilingual performance.

Representing 3D shapes as compact sliding-window slice latents, rather than voxel tokens from multi-stage pipelines, preserves topological consistency and substantially reduces generation cost in high-resolution 3D generation.
Representing molecules as production-rule sequences from a context-free higher-order grammar yields an efficient encoding that is valid by construction and works with standard sequence models.
The grammar-based representation achieves leading performance on both molecular generation and molecular property prediction.
Endogenous alignment in AI systems requires starting them in a state of dependency on humans, because dependency makes the AI care what humans think.

Training-free text-to-image safeguards that assume unsafety is a global property of the whole prompt-image representation face an inherent coverage-selectivity trade-off, which limits how well they can suppress unsafe content without damaging benign generation.

Prompt-local counterfactual correction (CALM), which targets only the unsafe components of a prompt, is a more selective training-free alternative that suppresses unsafe content more effectively while preserving benign utility.

Slow-Fast MOPD preserves general capabilities while still improving domain expertise by using an exponential-moving-average slow model as a reference and filtering out the teacher-induced update components that push the fast student away from it.
Capability interference in multi-teacher on-policy distillation arises because general capabilities decline as the student drifts from its initialization.
Grounding a language model in continuous fish-behavior signals, rather than text alone, is what makes rainbow trout feeding decisions in recirculating aquaculture systems (RAS) accurate.
Dual-evidence behavior tokens raise feeding decision accuracy for rainbow trout in RAS from 33.33% to 93.33%.
Counterfactual mDPO training further improves decision accuracy and causal consistency beyond standard LoRA fine-tuning for rainbow trout feeding decisions.
Combining LLM-based synthesis with cell-level symbolic verification and localized error repair can scalably and verifiably autoformalize tax forms into executable programs.

Causal structure recovered from measurements alone can assign meanings to unlabeled variables more accurately than association-based methods, because it reflects the generating mechanism rather than surface correlations.

Spectral alignment, a training-free method that corrects intermediate sampling states' deviations from an analytic reference spectrum, supplies the missing criterion for whether a classifier-free guided trajectory is progressing as intended and improves generation quality over CFG and baseline guidance methods without modifying the underlying model.
Aligning CLIP's feature subspaces via Kernel Canonical Correlation Analysis, rather than matching kernel matrices as prior work does, is a better route to fine-grained visual representations in VLMs.

The three-view variant 3vKCCA, which also aligns the pretrained text encoder, improves fine-grained visual accuracy (MMVP-VLM for CLIP ViT-L/14 on ImageNet-1K rises from 17.8 to 25.9) without sacrificing zero-shot image-text retrieval.

Restricting safety alignment updates to a harmful-related subspace, rather than updating the full model, can reduce harmful outputs across backbones while preserving benign utility and diversity at low computational cost.
Existing safety alignment methods are computationally expensive and degrade a model's core knowledge, harming benign-task fluency and factual accuracy.
Existing single-sentence style-control datasets fail to capture how conversational tone shifts across multiple turns, so a multi-turn resource is needed to model stylistic tone drift.
ConvoDrift models progressive stylistic tone drift under fixed semantic intent by using multi-turn conversations whose drift events change lexical form while preserving semantic similarity.
Training a clinical note summarizer with reinforcement learning on the downstream outcome predictor's own loss, rather than for fluency, improves readmission prediction from EHR data.
The outcome-relevant evidence that a reward-aligned summarizer retains from discharge notes complements structured codes rather than duplicating them.

A small language model can serve as a low-latency, on-premises classifier that checks whether an agentic system's tool call is relevant to the task's intent, enabling per-call verification where conventional authorization fails.
Conventional authorization cannot determine whether an otherwise-allowed tool call is a logical step toward the task's intent, so every tool call by an agentic system should be verified individually.

Evaluating LLM-generated PLC programs requires observing how their commands affect simulated device and workpiece states, so a closed-loop benchmark coupling Structured Text execution with plant responses is needed rather than code checking alone.
Under closed-loop evaluation, even a frontier model's performance degrades sharply as task difficulty rises, falling from 82.70% Task Success on Easy cases to 25.10% on Hard cases.

Abductive discovery is hard mainly because agents must construct a new representation that transfers, not because they lack evidence, and in the ULTRADISCOVERY setting disclosing the representation helps agents more than aligning the evidence does.

Muon, using five tuned finite-step Newton--Schulz orthogonalization iterations instead of exact orthogonalization, provably reaches any target training loss on a sufficiently wide two-layer ReLU network.

A lightweight, budget-bounded trajectory evaluation design that compresses agent traces with offline rule profiles and uses a single rubric-guided LLM judge can make repeated production evaluation of LLM agents affordable while improving failure-localization alignment with human annotations over AgentRx.

A near-zero monitor readout does not establish that an intervention controls behavior, because identical zero-median monitor scores can coexist with anywhere from a low to a near-pure reward-hacking share.
Offline monitor discrimination is insufficient to validate behavioral control, so an out-of-band behavioral check is required.

The Cephalonauts One dataset, with about 30 hours of whole-brain 3T fMRI per subject recorded during podcast listening, supports a naturalistic speech decoding benchmark whose performance improves continuously with more training data per subject.

For interactive long video generation that combines characters and backgrounds from different earlier shots, routing each prompt component to its own relevant historical memory works better than retrieving whole prompts or directly combining all memories, which introduces unrelated content.

For multi-pitch estimation in vocal ensembles, a linear STFT with directly provided frequency bins outperforms the commonly used harmonic constant-Q transform (HCQT), so HCQT's frequency-adaptive resolution is not necessary for this task.
The linear STFT input also substantially reduces feature-extraction cost compared with HCQT, so it is preferable on efficiency grounds as well as accuracy.
A weaker monitor can reliably detect malicious GUI computer-use agents when it reviews the full trajectory, but its detection degrades when it must score each step individually.
For monitoring GUI computer-use agents, the agent's visible text matters far more to monitor performance than its screenshots do.
A trained Invertible Neural Network can make a regular hyper-rectangle forward-invariant in a latent space, yielding analytically proven forward-invariant sets for neural-network-controlled systems.

AI systems can approximate human judgments of whether a children's story is developmentally appropriate when they use structured annotation across cognitive, language, and social-emotional dimensions.
Readability-based methods are a poor proxy for developmental appropriateness, aligning with developmental references far less closely than structured multi-dimensional annotation does.
Personas induced from out-of-domain public behavioral data rarely improve survey simulation alignment over demographic-only conditioning, largely because of population mismatch.

Survey simulation alignment improves when personas are accurately assigned to target demographic groups and when richer behavioral evidence yields more stable trait inference that transfers to unseen survey questions.

Selective KV-cache reuse for rolling agents is history-dependent, so an unchanged prompt can produce different answers depending on earlier requests, and recomputing contiguous document-aligned spans instead of scattered top-k tokens substantially reduces this order sensitivity at the same TTFT speedup.

Classifier-free guidance can be framed as a continuous-time optimal control problem whose unconstrained control set lets sampling drift arbitrarily far from the current image estimate, which explains why guidance degrades image quality at high strengths.

Constraining the guidance controls to a hypersphere (curvature-aware classifier-free guidance) yields better generative quality than regular classifier-free guidance at mid-to-high guidance strengths.

Object-grounded attention divergence, first observed during finite offline testing of VLA policies, can be monitored at runtime with conformal-calibrated early stopping trained only on successful episodes to halt failing executions that the test suite did not cover.

Shifting to latent reasoning architectures, which let models reason in internal states rather than in text, would likely undermine chain-of-thought as a tool for understanding AI reasoning, because models would no longer need to verbalize their reasoning.

Steering a flow model with visual motion, plus a training-free, rhythm-anchored trajectory guidance step, can deliver intelligible, speaker-consistent, lip-synchronized visual voice cloning together, whereas sequential multimodal conditioning and imbalanced inference guidance trade these properties off.

Because experimenters are rewarded on empirical average treatment effects, which are prone to upward bias, the conflict between experimenters and the platform is best resolved by incentive design using sample splitting and shrinkage rather than by centralized levers.
Centralized levers alone cannot fix the principal-agent conflict between experimenters and the platform when experimenters are rewarded on upwardly biased empirical treatment effects.
Equipping AI agents with a joint-attention-inspired mechanism that aligns their visual attention on scene-salient objects actively promotes zero-shot coordination with unfamiliar partners.

This joint-attention mechanism goes beyond symmetry-breaking approaches, which only prevent brittle conventions from forming, and consistently improves coordination with unknown partners in the authors' experiments.
