A single-encoder framework combining dual-level decorrelation with prototype-guided cross-group contrastive learning reduces demographic dependence in chest X-ray diagnosis representations and narrows intersectional performance gaps compared with empirical risk minimization, at only a slight cost in mean AUC.

Spatially localized contour-to-mesh interactions, which route each sparse 2D contour's features to nearby template vertices and correct inter-slice misalignment, enable accurate 3D left ventricular reconstruction from sparse 2D cardiac MRI without 3D mesh annotations.
Left ventricular meshes reconstructed by this localized approach improve downstream cardiac disease classification.

Vision-language-action policies encode physical object properties such as mass and fragility only weakly and do not reliably use them to adapt motion, so their success on new setups is better explained by replayed learned behaviors than by genuine object understanding.
Multimodal saturation, where a trimodal self-supervised model underperforms its best bimodal subset, stems from the Euclidean alignment geometry of VICReg rather than from the data alone.

Aligning views by geodesic distance on learnable negative-curvature product factors (Riemannian VICReg) reduces multimodal saturation, raising the probability that a third modality helps from 44.4% to 64.4%.
Training data extraction attacks transfer across languages and can recover memorized PII from both English-centric and multilingual LLMs.
Cross-lingual transfer of extraction attacks is driven by latent cross-linguistic representations that align translations of the same prompt, so PII protection in LLMs must be language-agnostic.

Oversight of long-horizon agents becomes more effective when monitors ground their outputs in source-linked evidence grouped into behaviors and organized into a graph, letting users identify which agent decisions warrant verification.

Video classification under multi-instance partial-label supervision can be improved by jointly resolving which candidate labels apply and which temporal segments support them, because bag-level labels alone do not tie candidate classes to specific temporal evidence.
The proposed method, which couples label disambiguation with temporal segment selection, outperforms existing multi-instance partial-label learning algorithms on video classification.
Integrating diverse multi-omics layers into a single aligned representation allows missing and unpaired molecular modalities to be reconstructed and supports cancer classification.
Aligned multi-omics representation learning is a practical alternative to costly functional assays in limited or incomplete data settings, rather than relying on ever-larger models.

Adaptive scaling for Muon should be computed from raw gradients, decoupled from orthogonalization, and matched to matrix shape, using row-wise scaling for wide matrices and column-wise scaling for tall ones.
NorMuon's row-wise adaptive scaling arises mainly from orthogonalization-induced geometry rather than from optimization-relevant information in the gradients.

A lightweight linear transformation trained on synthetic unlabeled data can align a partial-context student's intermediate activations with those of a full-context teacher, closing a significant fraction of the performance gap that restricting in-context training examples opens in tabular in-context learning while keeping prediction cheap.
Signature-based features improve human activity recognition accuracy on the UCI HAR dataset over raw-signal baselines when paired with Random Forest classifiers, but not when paired with MLP models.

Motion priors from a simulation teacher can be transferred to real-domain robot world models by latent-motion distillation, yielding better real-video generation and benefiting downstream policy learning.

Existing sparse attention methods degrade generation quality at high sparsity because of three identified sources: constraints from token grouping, inaccurate interaction selection, and lost attention contributions from discarded tokens.

A training-free method that selects individual KV tokens, caches metadata, and reuses it across denoising steps can close the dense-sparse attention gap in diffusion transformers while delivering speedups without visible quality loss.

Conditioning rank-one component selection from a shared low-rank basis on each question's specialty and operation tags lets ARBOR outperform fixed-rank LoRA r16 on medical question answering, with the advantage growing as more specialties are trained.

Under an illustrative orthogonal-subtask separation, conditional rank selection can avoid an approximation floor that a fixed update of equal active rank faces, though this has not been shown to hold for medical corpora.

The contextual tokens in Multimodal Diffusion Transformers carry a readable record of the emerging image, making them both an interpretable view of the model's internal dynamics and an effective training target for improving generation quality.

A single-voice student distilled from the 54-voice Kokoro-82M teacher, without alignment learning or joint training, can be roughly 10x smaller and run far faster than real time on one CPU thread while retaining high perceived speech quality.
Residual buzz in such a distilled model can be removed by a training-free phase-locking filter, so the compressed model does not require retraining to be cleaned up.

Because attention behaves non-uniformly and RoPE induces dimension-dependent positional structure, uniform static PEFT adaptations are suboptimal for LLMs, and DyPAM's input-conditioned, dimension-, head-, and layer-wise modulation of positional attention, applied without altering the pretrained backbone, consistently outperforms strong PEFT baselines on reasoning benchmarks.
BiasFlow Regularization reduces a frozen backbone's encoding of spurious attributes while raising worst-group accuracy, within the tested protocols.
Worst-group accuracy alone is insufficient to assess spurious feature reliance, so centroid geometry and resistance to biased head retraining should be evaluated alongside it.

Contrastive objectives like InfoNCE do not directly optimize retrieval metrics or downstream task performance, and post-training embedding models with reinforcement learning directly in embedding space against task-specific rewards yields higher average nDCG@10 than InfoNCE on reasoning-intensive retrieval.

Implicit negatives for recommendation should be selected only after verifying that observed customer behavior supports them, because a missing interaction alone neither explains a user's disinterest nor establishes that an item is a valid negative.
Ranking candidate negatives by symbolic-rule evidence improves candidate-quality precision and yields a 12.5% downstream PR-AUC gain over random selection in an industrial task.

Supplying an LLM with textual environmental context and continuous graph-derived spatial prefixes, rather than serializing the full SST grid as text, yields the best regional multi-step SST forecasts in the South China Sea.

Existing dynamic multimodal learning methods fail because uniform cross-modal alignment over-aligns samples and confidence-based fusion ignores feature magnitude differences, so a framework combining sample-aware triplet alignment with difference-aware attention calibration fixes both limitations and outperforms recent state-of-the-art methods.

A vision-language-action policy can adapt at test time to unknown visual disruptions by treating its leftover trajectory (the unexecuted part of its previous action chunk) as a self-supervised target, requiring no disruption labels, expert actions, or target-domain demonstrations.
This leftover-trajectory adaptation raises success on persistent visual corruptions and task progress on a real robot while largely preserving nominal performance.

A model can improve its own safety alignment without external supervision, using only a Model Spec that describes desired behavior, and these gains generalize out of distribution while general capability is retained.

A central harness that governs specialized agents can turn a sparse error-taxonomy specification into complete Chart QA samples that stay aligned with their specified error category and reveal capability differences between multimodal LLMs.

Generated Chart QA samples test their specified error category, as shown by evaluator judgments that 86.4% of samples are aligned and by same-direction differences between targeted follow-ups and matched controls across all six cross-model comparisons.
Training-free test-time adaptation that evolves retrieved experience and enforces rubric-aligned cross-role coordination improves the reliability of agents on long-horizon legal reasoning.
Static agent strategies fail on long-horizon legal reasoning because real cases are heterogeneous and legal decisions are interdependent across roles and stages.

Static profile prompts cannot keep simulated counseling clients psychologically consistent over long dialogues, whereas a closed loop that detects and corrects inconsistencies during the conversation can.
Raw frontier-model analysis of unchanged customer feedback is unstable across runs, producing shifting categories, priorities, and counts even when each individual answer looks plausible.
Grounding the analysis agent in persistent taxonomy themes makes its outputs more repeatable than any raw model tested.

A unified Sensor-Language-Action framework, which uses language as the interface between sensor observations and actions, is needed because existing sensor models stop at perception and model actions separately from sensing.
Language can serve as the interface linking sensor observations to actions, enabling a single framework to predict, represent, and explain heterogeneous actions grounded in sensor evidence.

Composing a user's preferences from shared latent preference facets via history-conditioned routing (MoF) personalizes black-box LLMs better and more parameter-efficiently than user-specific scoring heads, which do not scale, and it generalizes to unseen users without additional parameter updates.

Quantized vision transformers degrade under distribution shift because shifted activations distort how frozen quantizers allocate codes, so adaptation must target the quantizer inputs rather than the model weights.

Recalibrating per-channel statistics at the quantizer inputs in a single backprop-free pass (QuAR) restores the code distribution and outperforms existing backprop-free test-time adaptation methods in both accuracy and latency.
Long-horizon agent evaluation transcripts have grown too large for evaluators to reliably inspect, which narrows the range of agent behaviour that evaluators can actually infer.
Transect restores observability in long-horizon agent evaluations by linking language-model-assisted analysis back to source turns, so that interpretations remain checkable and reproducible.

Fusing complementary DESS and TSE knee MRI sequences in a sequence-aware, full-volume vision-language model outperforms single-sequence configurations for predicting structured MOAKS-based knee pathology targets, supporting dual-sequence modeling for comprehensive knee MRI assessment.
In cross-tokenizer on-policy distillation, expanding alignment coverage is not the key bottleneck, because strict 1:1 alignment already covers most student-generated tokens.

Adding span-level supervision to reach full alignment coverage lowers accuracy, because its gradients weakly or negatively agree with strict-loss gradients, so research should prioritize supervision reliability over coverage.

Bridging paired quasiperiodic physiological signals with a closed-form geodesic on the phase-amplitude cylinder, which respects circular phase and strictly positive amplitude, is a critical inductive bias that outperforms interpolation baselines and matches or exceeds direct supervised prediction, where the standard affine flow-matching path distorts intermediate amplitude.
Diagnostic models that map image features directly to disease labels, bypassing the structured clinical criteria clinicians use, limit transparency and may compromise safe deployment.
Decomposing diagnosis into spatially localized clinical criteria, aggregated with uncertainty-calibrated weighting, yields consistent gains over CNN baselines across three imaging modalities.

Research on AI safety for youth has identified many risks yet implemented and evaluated very few countermeasures, and existing evaluations measure technical performance rather than real protection from harm, so the field needs a human-centered evaluation approach.
Generating sound for world models demands real-time, interactive, spatially aligned audio, and a streaming causal autoregressive diffusion framework can meet these demands.
The proposed WorldSonus framework matches or exceeds state-of-the-art bidirectional models in acoustic quality while operating in a streaming causal manner.

Parallel multi-agent LLM systems often run slower than a single agent because of hidden costs, namely re-exploration and alignment overhead, so parallelization should be decided per layer using a token-based criterion.
A design combining forked workers with a pre-generated shared convention block achieves a 2.2x to 2.6x speedup over Claude Code.

Alignment should be measured as a family of risk-specific scaling relations rather than a single aggregate score, because whether scaling helps, keeps pace, or accumulates alignment debt depends on each risk category's exponent.

In a preregistered pilot on Qwen2.5 models from 0.5B to 72B parameters, alignment scaling diverged by risk category, with a near-flat exponent for truthfulness (-0.05) and a steeper exponent for stated dispositions (0.48).

Training an LLM teacher by directly maximizing the learning outcomes of simulated student archetypes with distinct learning preferences, rather than relying on demonstrations, preferences, or predefined pedagogical criteria, yields teachers that adaptively improve student performance across all archetypes.

A feed-forward conditional flow matching model can refine coarse vision-foundation-model estimates of hand-object states into stable 4D interaction reconstructions, without costly per-sequence optimization.

Parallel diffusion sampling cannot avoid polynomially many sequential rounds: even with polynomially many score queries per round at arbitrary locations and noise levels and inverse-polynomial score error, sampling smooth, near-isotropic Gaussian mixtures in R^d requires Ω̃(d^{1/3}) rounds.

Red-teaming vision-grounded web agents must target the full grounding-to-execution pipeline, because success at the model level does not establish control over browser execution, as shown by WebMirage's 91.9% average attack success rate versus 17.4% for the strongest baseline.

Small language models explicitly trained to model the latent cognitive components of substance use disorder patients (beliefs, coping strategies, readiness for change) can generate more cognitively coherent patient dialogue than general LLMs and generic or mental-health-specific SLMs, providing a practical alternative to costly frontier-scale models.
Best-of-N inference-time alignment can be evaluated and tuned from logged samples alone, without access to response likelihoods.
A doubly robust estimator (BoN-DR) yields valid inference for BoN policies even when the reward estimator is misspecified.
A lower-confidence-bound rule for choosing the sampling budget N carries a no-harm guarantee relative to the baseline.

Retrieval for EDA documentation question answering fails because relevant evidence is scattered across tightly coupled artifacts, so organizing retrieval around functional units (hyperedges linking typed artifacts to their source chunks) substantially improves answer quality over chunk-based and graph-based RAG baselines.
Independently trained models in different modalities share enough representation geometry that their embedding spaces can be aligned without any paired examples.

GraphRAG systems for multimodal documents should explicitly model layout, cross-modal evidence alignment, and the reasoning roles of evidence units, because text-only GraphRAG fails on figure- and table-grounded dependencies that standard retrieval and generation metrics do not reveal.
The features that best diagnose which source a retrieval-augmented model will choose are not the features that best control that choice.

In controlled knowledge conflicts, the magnitude of hidden-state change predicts source choice better than the signed PC1 projection, whereas the signed PC1 projection steers choice more effectively and preserves non-target behavior under equal-norm interventions.

Pixel-space diffusion can be scaled to 3B parameters and match latent models on text-to-image quality, yet it gives no significant downstream advantage over latent models on depth estimation or 4× super-resolution.

Aligning subset-specific scorers to a synthetic ordinal reference space before fusion can produce viable supervision scores without ground-truth labels or a shared annotation space, and this outperforms uncalibrated averaging.

LLM judges used to evaluate Entity Alignment systems are unreliable when the alignment system's decision label is visible, because exposing that label induces an anchor bias that collapses their discrimination.
A label-free evaluation protocol, in which the judge does not see the alignment system's decision, restores near-ceiling LLM judge capability on distinctive-name datasets.

Safety refusal behavior is already encoded in weak, identifiable circuits within pretrained base LLMs, and confining safety updates to these circuits yields stronger refusal of harmful inputs, less over-refusal of benign queries, and better retained utility than vanilla alignment.

Coding-agent benchmarks built from issue-derived tasks should name a target use case and be reshaped to match that use case's Task Flow, because no single interaction distribution is universally realistic.
Real users' long coding-agent sessions mix task types and switch between them in ways that isolated issue-derived benchmark tasks do not reproduce.

Personalizing LLMs works better when the model internalizes user preferences through reference-revealed on-policy self-distillation than when it imitates reference wording, yielding better content quality and overall personalization than existing fine-tuning paradigms.
Existing in-database Transformer inference ignores relational predicates and metadata statistics, so it runs densely on tuple-level inputs, wasting computation on predictive queries.

Query-context-aware slicing of Transformer FFN layers, pre-selected from query predicates and metadata statistics, enables sparse inference that substantially reduces predictive query latency while keeping accuracy comparable to dense models.

Interpretable part concepts can be learned without class labels from a frozen self-supervised vision backbone, yielding spatially grounded discrete concepts that closely preserve the backbone's downstream accuracy.
Concepts learned this way are more consistent than those produced by language-aligned vision models, so self-supervised backbones are a better basis for interpretable part concepts.

Reinforcement learning from human feedback ensures safety in human-robot collaboration only when the feedback collection method is appropriate, since in a VR experiment on robot proxemic behaviour, user-initiated feedback captured perceived safety better than system-initiated feedback and feedback timing directly affects feedback quality.

Proofs that establish AI alignment are inadequate when they ignore the environment and the time-limited actions an agent must take, because even a perfect agent cannot guarantee safe behaviour in realistic partially observable settings.
Any valid AI safety or alignment proof must consider the environment and its safe actions together with the agent, rather than the agent alone.

Existing benchmarks evaluate visual understanding and code generation in isolation, so MLLM figure-to-code reproduction requires a dedicated benchmark such as FigCodeBench to assess their unification.
Figure reproduction in multimodal LLMs exhibits a non-linear performance cliff that appears across all evaluated models, programming languages, and difficulty levels.

Scoring skill proposals by how they shift the current actor's action log-likelihood gap between successful and failed trajectories yields actor-aligned skill edits that outperform alternatives such as later-reuse scoring or costly extra rollouts.
Jointly training a policy and its skillbank with these actor-aligned skill edits lets the combined system reach strong performance, including 98.4% success on ALFWorld and 84.7% on WebShop.

SLDR, a post-fine-tuning defense that trains a LoRA recovery adapter only on the most and least safety-sensitive layers and routes inference through it only for malicious queries, substantially reduces the harmful outputs of malicious fine-tuning while preserving downstream utility.
Document structure helps dense retrieval only modestly, and the benefit comes from real content-bearing heading information rather than from the extra tokens that structure adds.
Naive two-stage hierarchical retrieval over document structure hurts dense retrieval performance.

Global text-audio relevance scores cannot reveal whether generated music matches user intent, so text-to-music intent alignment should be judged by per-request rubrics of independently verifiable items, and a rubric-guided test-time search over prompt revisions (MIRA) improves that alignment across both open-source and commercial generators.

Visual fidelity alone is an insufficient measure of MLLM industrial UI code generation, because models can visually reconstruct a design yet fail to produce code that meets domain-specific implementation requirements, so benchmarks must evaluate constraint-aware requirement inference and realization.

FoldBack enables long-horizon garment folding to recover from missed or slipped grasps by detecting failed interactions, rolling back to a retryable pre-grasp configuration, and regenerating only the failed segment.
FoldBack's self-correction works without recovery demonstrations, and it achieves higher real-garment folding success than the strongest prior baseline.
Long-term time series forecasting models suffer from low output alignment, so their predictions for the same timestamps fluctuate and undermine their reliability.
Explicitly reducing output discrepancies in the time and frequency domains (as the AliO method does) improves output alignment without sacrificing, and can even enhance, forecasting performance.

Decomposing a complex task recursively into subtasks aligned with a hierarchy of tool capabilities, discovered on demand, improves end-to-end task success over single execution chains of tool-using agents, which become unreliable on complex tasks.

Row-wise normalization can achieve strictly higher population accuracy than Adam and Muon in high-dimensional multiclass classification, because its class-wise Euclidean geometry preserves the population decision-boundary directions that Adam's coordinate-wise geometry distorts.
A natural language interface can replace the structured schema objects used by existing System One decision-making models while still supporting competitive multimodal decision-making.

A bi-encoder fine-tuned from a pre-trained decoder (MetaEncoder) delivers competitive multimodal System One decision-making through this natural language interface, though it falls short on reasoning-intensive tasks.
Using residual error patterns, rather than aggregate fit scores alone, to guide LLM-based formula proposal and correction fitting improves numerical equation recovery over same-backbone baselines.
Spiking neural networks can be made competitive for image-text retrieval by combining a multi-head spiking graph attention module with a similarity-space fusion strategy.

Fusing spike and continuous representations in similarity space, rather than directly, avoids the mismatch between heterogeneous representations and yields better retrieval than prior spiking methods and ANN counterparts at lower energy cost.
Rendering documents as images and using image-valued class prototypes improves classification over otherwise identical vector-prototype models, by 4.3 to 11.8 points on a ten-class task.

The deformable-alignment matching step, not the image representation, is the weak link of ProtoSemImage: swapping only the classifier recovers the sequence baselines and locates a 20.6-point shortfall in that step.

The standard contrastive loss is not inherently unsuitable for CLIP post-training: the forgetting attributed to it is driven mainly by an inappropriate InfoNCE temperature rather than by too few negatives, and with a sufficiently small temperature contrastive post-training improves the pretrained CLIP.

Training only the vision encoder with a properly-tempered contrastive loss while the text encoder stays frozen improves visual feature transferability without breaking compatibility with LLaVA-1.5-7B.

Training ultrasound report generators to imitate raw clinical reports is misaligned with visual evidence, and grounding training in trusted visible report points yields higher report quality than the EchoVLM baseline on the USReport-Distilled benchmark.

Deterministic deadlock recovery, which atomically purges agent-side context and sends a fixed canonical strike, reliably escapes honeytrap-to-compliance deadlocks, whereas LLM-only steering at the same call budget does not, so recovery is more dependably delivered by deterministic mechanisms than by LLM-driven steering.
Object-specific image-to-3D generation requires high-resolution geometry produced in a single generation stage, because errors made in initial generation cannot be fully repaired by later refinement.
The Twinkle3D geometry model of Hi3D 3.0 generates geometry at 2048^3 resolution and thereby recovers identity-critical details such as inscriptions better than four commercial systems.
Current multiplayer world models do not yet maintain one shared, persistent world across independently controlled views, despite producing plausible individual views.

On MultiWorldBench, every generated system falls far short of the Engine ground truth on multi-view consistency, persistence, structure, and spatial reasoning, with the best generated system at 21.39 against 91.69 for the Engine.

Suppressing hallucination-related components in LVLM hidden representations is a flawed mitigation, because those components carry useful information, whereas repairing representations by aligning hallucinated and faithful distributions within a residual subspace reduces object hallucination without weakening multimodal capability.

AuraLuxMuse can assist pre-production stage lighting design by returning editable, visually cohesive, and semantically meaningful lighting cues aligned to music, while keeping the designer in control rather than replacing them with an unconstrained generator.

A probability-signature framework, expressing leading gradient interactions through conditional statistics of the training distribution, explains the emergence of Fourier-sparse, approximately decoupled mode dynamics in two-layer networks learning modular addition.

Multimodal emotion understanding that relies mainly on observable affective cues reduces to unreliable cue-label shortcuts, so it should progress toward cognitive appraisal of events to support more reliable, human-aligned emotion reasoning.
Enforcing polytope-based structure directly within a neural network's layers yields interpretable, structure-preserving representations at minimal performance cost.

Predictive PPG representation learning can leak withheld future samples even under causal attention, so architectural causality alone does not guarantee that a forecaster respects its information boundary.
Enforcing an explicit stored-window cutoff, as PulseBound does, removes dependence on withheld future samples while the model still forecasts future beats better than last-visible-beat persistence.

Fixed-resolution tokenization of raw I/Q signals either inflates token cost as observation length grows or discards short-duration evidence, so a budget-adaptive tokenizer that sizes its token capacity to input length and signal content can make vision-language models practical for electromagnetic spectrum understanding.

Recursively repeating red-teaming, training-recipe development, and gated selection of the next target model can make AI models both resistant to known attacks and resilient to unseen ones while largely preserving general capabilities.

Robot world action models perform better when they predict actions and future observations from a decoder-free JEPA latent space than from a reconstruction-based representation, and planning in the policy head's noise space rather than over raw actions further improves closed-loop performance.

ContiLNN mitigates slice sampling discontinuity in volumetric medical image restoration by adding bidirectional closed-form continuous-time modules that gate cross-slice propagation according to slice-index interval, and this yields lower RMSE than Restore-RWKV across CT denoising, MRI super-resolution, and reduced-count PET restoration.
The interval-based gating, rather than extra pointwise capacity alone, is what allows cross-slice propagation to respond to irregular slice spacing.
The BrickBench benchmark shows that current agents can meet verifiable physical and semantic requirements for text-conditioned LEGO design, yet still fall short of human-made designs.
Harmful refusal has not been shown to be a single measurable attribute in HELM Safety, so a safety score should earn its single-attribute reading before models are compared using it.

Representations built from a model's activations while a value is applied in context predict how fine-tuning on one value shifts behavior on other held-out values better than textual descriptions of those values do.

Clarification guidance for interactive agents should be learned jointly with the task policy, because the value of asking a question changes as the policy changes, and a controller trained on co-evolving paired-rollout value labels outperforms fixed guidance.

Two independently pretrained unimodal encoders can be aligned using only a few paired anchors rather than millions of paired examples, by solving one entropic optimal transport problem over their unpaired collections and distilling the resulting plan into lightweight encoders.
At the same anchor budget, this anchor-based optimal transport and distillation approach outperforms existing alignment methods on image-text and molecule-text alignment.

A reinforcement learning-guided neural architecture search that jointly rewards SI-SNR improvement and compactness can find an audio-visual speech enhancement model that is far smaller than the baseline while losing only a marginal amount of SI-SNR, making on-device deployment practical.

Neural networks can be functionally modular at the level of subspaces even though no individual neuron serves a single computation, so modularity should be sought in learned directions rather than in single units.
Supervising brain-computer interface decoders with natural-language class descriptions, instead of class labels alone, is a viable approach to neural decoding.
Natural-language class descriptions improve speech-decoding accuracy by up to 17.15 percentage points over matched class-label supervision.
Language-based supervision also supports candidate-set reuse, subject and session adaptation, and decoding of unseen SSVEP frequencies.

Creativity in AI applications can be formally defined as a single mathematical measure built from Boden's criteria of newness, value, and surprise, with domain-specific measurements of each, and this definition is validated on chess moves and paintings.

When AI agents modify both application code and deployment infrastructure in the same pull request, integration outcomes are bimodal: explicitly reviewed dual-scope PRs suffer large delays, while others are merged without inspection and bypass build verification.
Current agent evaluations and access controls fail to account for deployment, so they do not adequately govern agent changes that touch both application code and deployment infrastructure.

Choosing decoder hidden-state layers for speculative decoding by jointly scoring their informativeness (matrix-entropy) and their diversity (CKA) produces layer sets that outperform fixed default choices such as the [2, N//2, N-3] rule.
Semantic-ID generative recommenders decoding with finite-width beam search cannot return every held-out item, because beam width limits which items can enter the finite returned list.

Continuous-query generation removes this reachability constraint by making every encoded item directly scoreable, and it matches or exceeds a TIGER-style baseline while using fewer trainable parameters.

Inducing reusable agent skills from synchronized recordings of human desktop GUI demonstrations, with workflow rules, step dependencies, and completion checks, raises computer-use agents' scores and success rates above No Skill baselines on MyPCBench Bounded Action and OSWorld-Verified.

A hyperbolic variational autoencoder trained on patent text retrieves genuinely cross-category prior art more often than a matched Euclidean one, even though it agrees less with official CPC classification, because classification agreement and cross-category prior-art retrieval measure different goals and only retrieval matches prior-art search needs.

Language models should update their beliefs according to the provenance of evidence rather than how many times the same observation is repeated, and the proposed Latent Quotient Evidence Training (LQET) objective achieves this by keeping predictions stable when reports add no new evidence and reducing log-odds drift across relay steps.

Optimizing advertising images for click-through rate is better achieved by fine-grained editing that revises only the attributes that hurt clicks than by regenerating the whole image, because existing generation methods penalize every attribute of an underperforming ad equally, including attributes that actually help clicks.
Final-render supervision is too ambiguous to drive self-improvement of visual agents for symbolic graphics reasoning, so self-improvement needs a different training signal.

Actionable evidence extracted from execution traces, showing which proposed program edits survived, disappeared, or interfered, lets an agent refine executable graphics programs more effectively than render-based feedback, outperforming BlenderAlchemy and VIGA.
Synthetic Self-Distillation (SynthSelf) lets small models acquire new capabilities while retaining prior knowledge, outperforming existing methods in continual post-training.
Self-distillation fine-tuning (SDFT) fails for small models because it depends on strong in-context learning that small models lack.

Implicit state management in agent harnesses, where evidence and evolving conclusions remain entangled in a growing interaction history, causes unbounded exploration and evidence-state drift, and making the evidence-conclusion interaction explicit fixes both.
An explicit evidence-conclusion harness improves exact match over direct reasoning and over Claude Code and Codex on OfficeQA Pro.

In safety-aligned LLMs, refusal behavior follows an attention-to-MLP pathway: attention updates make harmfulness readable, and downstream MLP updates write the refusal behavior, carrying the shift caused by upstream attention interventions.

Selecting coding-agent training trajectories by test-suite pass alone is insufficient, because process quality is ignored and inefficient successful behaviors are absorbed into supervised fine-tuning, whereas a structural scoring method that ranks trajectories without an LLM judge can select better training data than random subsets.

Rectifying categorical flows to follow geodesics on the statistical manifold enables one-step categorical generation with lower transport cost and better quality than multi-step flows that are not geodesic-constrained.
Continuous latent actions inferred from frame-to-frame visual transitions in unlabeled human videos can serve as scalable supervision for training robot policies.

A masked diffusion language agent (ChemDiffAgent) outperforms autoregressive chemical agents on tool-integrated chemical reasoning by about 20% under matched budgets, because masked diffusion jointly determines tool-use decisions over the full trajectory and better aligns the agent's decision boundary with its knowledge boundary.
Repairing an LLM-judge rubric using only cross-judge disagreement, without human labels, raises agreement among the LLM judges but does not bring their ratings closer to human expert ratings.
Hide and Seek can explain black-box vision models with human-understandable concepts without access to model weights, by masking concept regions and measuring how the model's output changes.
The HnS approach yields more faithful, image-level attributions than existing concept-based explanation methods, which are restricted to classification or regression models and require model weights.
Saved memories or successful final actions by a Minecraft agent do not show that it acquired a reusable capability, so evaluation must separately measure capability change and carried-over resources.
Under MC-EvoBench's controlled source-target design, related prior experience produces no stable transfer to later Minecraft tasks.

Weaker AI control monitors can reliably detect a misaligned GUI computer-use agent's harmful side tasks when they observe the full trajectory, so trajectory-level monitoring is a viable safety mechanism for such agents.

Monitoring of GUI computer-use agents depends heavily on what the monitor sees: scoring steps in isolation degrades detection at low false positive rates, and the agent's visible text carries far more monitoring signal than screenshots.

When terrestrial network failure is severe, allocating constrained NTN feeder capacity by service priority, with weights tuned offline, substantially improves emergency-weighted continuity over uniform feeder scaling, and the size of this benefit depends on failure severity.

Jointly modeling future scene dynamics, semantic understanding, and trajectory generation in one unified architecture yields stronger autonomous driving planning than handling these capabilities separately.
A lab should not begin training its next-generation model until significant alignment issues in its current generation are resolved, adopted as a minimum pacing requirement.

Learning a shared, cross-parameter weight morphism that maps softmax attention parameters to linear (Gated DeltaNet) parameters initializes a Video Diffusion Transformer for linearization better than random initialization or manual weight reuse, and this initialization markedly speeds recovery.

BELT preserves model quality under aggressive KV cache compression by combining a behavior-aligned low-rank factorization, whose key-side objective targets attention distributions and has a closed-form solution, with a learned global rank allocator.
BELT's compression delivers decoding speedups at accuracy comparable to the uncompressed model.

Retrieving memory at the frame level with one shared historical context for all query tokens is wasteful and misses the differing needs of each query, whereas attention-aligned, query-level retrieval over clustered KV memory better preserves long-range consistency across shot transitions under a fixed memory budget.

Recursive environment evolution, which iteratively refines work contexts, tasks, and verifiers so they stay aligned, is an effective way to train long-horizon cowork agents, as shown by large gains of the WorkRover-trained Qwen3.5-35B-A3B model over its base model on cowork benchmarks.

Existing deep research agent benchmarks under-cover real-world life and professional productivity tasks, and the LifeSearch benchmark fills this gap by showing that even the best of 12 tested agents (63.4%) has substantial room for improvement on such tasks.
LifeSearch's validated evaluation pipeline is reliable, since its aggregate agent scores align strongly with human rankings.

OpenAI cannot effectively self-police because it fires the safety researchers who raise alarms, so AI companies' voluntary self-policing should not be treated as morally binding and independent outside oversight is needed.

How a user's opinion is framed, including its stated confidence, attribution, and whether it is presented as shared with the model, drives LLM sycophancy in factual question answering more than the mere presence of the opinion or the user's expertise, so sycophancy evaluations should probe framing and measure multiple behaviors.

Once dealers adapt, a public order-flow rule that concentrates intervention in market states ranked low-risk lowers low-risk execution cost relative to random timing under paired re-adaptation, but only at the expense of high-risk trades and only for venues that weigh low-risk costs more than 1.38 times as heavily as high-risk costs.

Dataset condensation can distill imbalanced wearable IMU fall-detection data into a tiny, class-balanced synthetic set of about 1% of the training windows without re-sampling, and a small CNN trained only on that set reaches 93.5-95.8% mean accuracy and 0.89-0.98 PR-AUC.

Autonomous research agents fall short because retrieval coverage does not translate into the evidence that informs their research decisions, and coupling fast parallel source judgments with deliberative planning that feeds findings back into research closes this gap, yielding faster and more capable research.

Post-training quantisation is safe at 8 bits but unstable at 4 bits, and which language suffers most depends on the model, method, and calibration language, so aggregate multilingual accuracy cannot show that quantised models preserve robustness for regional varieties like Bavarian.
Prompt adaptation methods that perform alike downstream can work through different internal computations, so downstream performance alone cannot identify the mechanism behind an adaptation.
Common representation-level drift measures cannot distinguish useful prompt adaptations from placebo adaptations, so raw representation drift should not be interpreted as a mechanism.
Representation drift must be separated into its task-aligned, causally used component before it can be credibly interpreted as the mechanism of a prompt adaptation.
Published factuality alignment methods for LLMs do not reliably make models more factual: when re-run on a common benchmark, they neither reproduce fully nor significantly outperform the base model.

Long-horizon degradation of large vision-language models in vision-language navigation is caused by context-length limits, and compressing and spatially grounding navigation history into reusable experience overcomes it, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines on R2R-CE by a 2% success-rate margin.

Projector training in multimodal LLMs mostly performs a coarse alignment between vision and language feature spaces, so many different projectors achieve roughly equal results and the choice of projector matters less than assumed.
A training-free projector initialization built from per-modality summary statistics can match the standard image-caption-trained projector pipeline, making the projector training stage skippable.

Embodied world models work better when visual appearance, geometric structure, and robot action are evolved together by one shared dynamics model with shared parameters, rather than coupled through separate interfaces, and Thinker-WM demonstrates this by ranking first on EWMBench.

Faithfulness evaluation for theory-scale autoformalization should be framed as a context-aware align-then-label problem over phrase-level correspondences under explicit interpretations, because existing statement-level, whole-item methods cannot show how individual expressions correspond or which contextual interpretations support a verdict.
Models struggle to recover the context-dependent correspondences that faithfulness evaluation requires, so such evaluation cannot be delegated to them without explicit alignment structure.
Majority voting over sampled final answers ignores intermediate reasoning disagreements, so it leaves errors unresolved that remain visible across sampled traces.
Aligning claim-level graphs across sampled reasoning traces and verifying only the localized conflicts can selectively correct reasoning errors without enlarging the candidate bank.
This graph-alignment correction approach improves macro-average accuracy over direct answering.

Imperceptible perturbations to a small fraction of training images can silently redirect alignment in vision-language Direct Preference Optimization, a vulnerability that existing poisoning attacks, which corrupt explicit supervision or rely on visible triggers, do not exploit cleanly.
The reported reasoning gains of recent self-distillation methods (SDPO and OPSD) do not hold up under scrutiny.
The apparent gains of self-distillation for reasoning are largely explained by overfitting rather than generalization to unseen problems.
Self-distillation training gradients align only weakly with reward-optimizing policy gradients, so these methods may not provide an effective direction for policy improvement.

Automating digital twin reporting with an LLM refinement loop enables medium-sized local models (around 20 billion parameters) to generate reporting models in the Ontological Modeling Language at quality comparable to larger models.
COMPASS, a diagnostic scoring each pair of pretrained models on kNN overlap and the paradigm-allowed overlap ceiling, can estimate pair compatibility before costly alignment or merging.
COMPASS's compatibility estimates correlate strongly with downstream success across 72 cross-modal alignment experiments and 392 task-arithmetic merges.

Recovering geometry from RGB images does not by itself make it usable by a vision-language model, so geometry should be learned as continuous tokens the target VLM can read rather than merely aligned to the VLM's latents.

Multi-turn, feedback-guided optimization of molecules, in which an LLM refines candidates using feedback from earlier turns, is a necessary advance over the single-turn modification approaches that existing molecular optimization methods rely on.

The MFG reinforcement learning framework, by training an LLM to progressively improve molecules from prior-turn feedback, achieves the highest average similarity-constrained success rate (81.50%) across ten multi-objective optimization tasks.
Approach-aware episode conditioning of naturally suboptimal human demonstrations improves mean success over plain behavioral cloning across three VLA models.

The preferred label granularity (episode or chunk) for quality-aware pretraining reverses depending on the VLA model, so conclusions about pretraining recipes require controlled comparisons such as those a dedicated benchmark enables.
Sparse abbreviated input is ambiguous and causes LLMs to misread user intent, so grounding LLMs in multimodal context via Cognitive Steering can make fast abbreviated communication accurate.
Each context type should be paired with a control method suited to it within Cognitive Steering.

Applying CKA feature distillation to a compact multilingual ASR model without isolation fails to help, because its gradient overlaps 97.5% to 99.5% with the shared-encoder subspace English relies on, trading English accuracy for non-English gains.
Confining feature distillation to language-routed adapters that English bypasses (CAFE) lowers average WER on the Open ASR Leaderboard from 8.55% to 8.02% and outperforms an adapter-only control.

Plant Memory can turn maintenance work orders, whose key reliability fields are often empty, into verified, evidence-linked failure knowledge that people and AI agents can query, and its ranked root causes are more often top-1 correct than the raw SAP root-cause column.
Sparse abbreviated input is inherently ambiguous, so language models without sufficient context misread it and fail to recover the user's intent.

Grounding LLMs in multimodal context through Cognitive Steering, by aligning them with environmental referents, emotional states, and communication motives, substantially improves intent reconstruction from abbreviated input.
Hierarchical Semantic IDs, built by clustering embeddings of textual code profiles, are a better generation target than original ICD code strings for LLM-based automatic medical coding.

Agentic self-awareness requires that an agent's feasibility judgments, actions, and responses to reconsideration stay aligned, and recognizing blockers alone does not achieve it, since agents in a Terminal-Bench baseline recognized blockers 84.4% of the time but reached strict self-awareness only 40.6% of the time.

Multi-agent failure analyses that assume a single orchestrator, shared workspace, or common principal miss the failure modes that arise when agents hold private information and authority and act for different principals.
Scoring only the final task output hides failures in agent-to-agent systems, so such systems should also be evaluated by scoring each agent individually against its own objectives.
Models that refuse harmful requests equally well after safety alignment can still differ internally, so output-based safety evaluations alone are insufficient to establish safety.

Internal audits of hazardous concept accessibility should accompany output-based safety evaluations, because models with prior harmful exposure retain greater accessibility to dangerous concepts behind their refusals.

Learning 3D shape representations from language alone in hyperbolic space, rather than from rendered images, better captures the tree-like hierarchy of 3D shapes and improves classification and text-to-3D retrieval under the same parameter budget.

Language models that correctly recognize shared financial accounting concepts across languages still often fail to recover the corresponding numerical facts, so concept recognition accuracy overstates grounded multilingual financial evidence extraction and the two should be evaluated together.

Retrieval for machine translation should be selective, with the system deciding per input whether to retrieve and what evidence to acquire, and this decision is best learned by optimizing final translation quality through agentic reinforcement learning rather than applied uniformly through predefined strategies.

Independently pretrained continuous-time dynamic graph (CTDG) and temporal knowledge graph (TKG) learners can be fused at the score level to improve prediction without entity or relation alignment, so temporal sources that cannot be aligned directly remain usable as pretraining resources.

Goal misgeneralization comprises three distinct policy-goal misalignments at different depths, and the depth at which the intended goal is lost determines which intervention can recover goal-directed behavior: steering works only where the goal reaches the decision, new downstream wiring is needed where the goal reaches the policy but not the decision, and neither works where the goal is inert.

Rarity-re-weighted sparse autoencoder codes match symbols across heterogeneous symbolic systems better than the same LLMs' dense representations, with interpretable matches, and this matching is a foundational step toward a shared symbolic backbone for neuro-symbolic models.

Attributing text to its source language model via likelihood comparison under source-conditioned models (ATLAS) remains reliable under distribution shifts such as new domains and new model versions, where existing direct-prediction methods degrade substantially.

Existing LiDAR generation methods from camera images are unsuited to multi-view input because they rely only on semantic cues, so generating LiDAR from multi-view images requires a dedicated framework.
Jointly guiding latent diffusion with both geometric and semantic branches yields higher-fidelity LiDAR scenes generated from multi-view images than semantic guidance alone.

Memory-efficient subspace optimizers that use only the leading singular subspace of stochastic gradients can fail to converge, because gradient noise comes to dominate that subspace later in training.

Adding an orthogonal residual gradient correction to a subspace-maintained update restores full-space convergence rates (O(T^{-1/4})) for both momentum SGD and Muon, including multi-stage variants with periodically refreshed bases.

A student agent can be aligned with a black-box teacher at the level of semantic actions rather than tokens, improving out-of-distribution performance without access to teacher token probabilities or a shared model family.
Standard drift-based policies for offline reinforcement learning cannot prefer higher-value actions, because their repulsion depends only on geometric distances among generated actions.
Incorporating normalized Q-values into the repulsion field aligns behavior regularization with policy improvement, and this value-guided approach performs competitively against established baselines.
Final task success is an insufficient measure of GUI agent reliability, because outcome-based benchmarks hide execution instability such as deviations and loops that occur even in successful runs.
Step-level diagnosis of execution stability is needed to distinguish GUI agents whose identical success rates mask different recovery behavior.

Multiplayer world models need synchronized first-person and panoramic video paired with each player's actions to predict out-of-view environment changes, and the PAWA dataset and framework supply this combination, which no existing Minecraft dataset offers, yielding better first-person prediction quality than prior multiplayer world models.

Translating English-centric safety and reasoning benchmarks into other languages requires task-aware, reasoning-guided translation with systematic validation, because naive translation loses task-specific meaning and thereby produces language-dependent model vulnerabilities that English-only evaluation would miss.

Training agent policies on ordinary trajectories leaves runtime harness semantics (executable actions, state advancement, termination) implicit, and making them explicit as harness-verified supervision at each model-call boundary lets a model learn harness-compatible behavior.
A policy distilled with harness-verified supervision works at deployment without any runtime supplement and substantially raises autonomous task success over the unadapted model.
Standard Character Error Rate misstates OCR damage because it weights every character error equally, scoring a harmless typo the same as a wrong name.
A severity-weighted metric whose edit-level charges track human readers' judgments (semCER) measures the actual damage OCR errors do to a transcription more faithfully than standard CER.
Existing 3D composition methods that rely on static priors in digital space fail on physically complex arrangements such as precise hanging, gravity-driven settling, and hidden containment.

A physics-grounded agentic framework that pairs feedforward planning with simulator-based feedback correction significantly improves relation fidelity over existing 3D composition methods on physically complex arrangements.

Combining a hierarchical residual architecture that separates base and arm corrections with expert-guided value alignment from sparse human interventions makes real-world fine-tuning of mobile manipulation systems stable and sample-efficient.

Steering SAE features identified by a bag-of-words elicitation pipeline reduced the compliance gap, a behavioural marker of alignment faking, to non-significance in Gemma-3-27B-IT, suggesting that an activation-level intervention can mitigate this gap.
The mitigation is model-specific: the same steering configurations that closed the compliance gap in Gemma-3-27B-IT were ineffective in LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct.
Rubric-based LLM evaluation is flawed because it treats every criterion's binary judgment as equally certain, although judgment certainty actually varies substantially across criteria.

Aggregating rubric judgments without uncertainty weighting produces misleading reward signals for reinforcement learning, and quantifying per-criterion uncertainty via conformal calibration corrects this.

A recurring change in sparse autoencoder feature activations across prompt transformations does not by itself indicate downstream failure, because its consequences for a readout depend on the readout coefficients and the clean margin.
The redistribution sensitivity score can identify feature changes that recur across prompt transformations.
Fractional power-of-two (base-√2) weight quantization recovers the accuracy that coarse base-2 power-of-two quantization loses at low bitwidths.

Base-√2 weight quantization preserves a fully integer shift-add datapath that is cheaper in hardware than a 4-bit integer multiplier, so multiplier-free LLM inference can be both efficient and accurate.

LLM-based user simulators are unreliable because they suffer from goal omission, and separating goal-state tracking from natural language generation via a symbolic agenda stack yields more faithful simulation than prior architectures.
Computational agent theory, a mathematical theory of intelligence and rational agency, can yield a solution to the technical alignment problem for artificial superintelligence.
Artificial superintelligence poses a grave existential risk, and making it safe requires closing major gaps in theoretical computer science and the philosophy of knowledge and decision-making.
The current pace of technological development is too fast for safety to be investigated thoroughly enough.

Quantum-classical view fusion improves prediction only when the two representations capture complementary predictive relationships, so quantum representations should be judged by their complementary contribution rather than assumed to help, since on mixed targets matched classical representations recover the same benefit and classical replacement controls remain competitive.

Training a unified multimodal model to generate images can expand the knowledge it can access through text question answering, but this transfer is uneven and leaves substantial gaps between knowledge accessed via images and knowledge accessed via text.

Query-guided video grounding is best approached by decomposing it into three complementary levels (where, how, and when: object, relationship, and moment localization), with dedicated methods for each level advancing video understanding across spatial, relational, and temporal grounding.

Interpretable semantic properties account for much of the brain alignment of LLaMA2-7B during naturalistic story listening, but the LLM and the SCRIBE semantic representation each carry substantial brain-predictive information that the other lacks.
DeepSearch agents perform poorly because their search queries are poorly aligned with their reasoning, which yields inadequate evidence coverage.
QREF, a plug-and-play query refiner and evidence filter that requires no architectural change or retraining of the reasoning policy, improves DeepSearch agent performance across benchmarks.

Reinforcement learning is a pivotal post-training mechanism for diffusion models, but its real-world deployment is hindered by reward design fragility, the exploration-exploitation trade-off in high-dimensional generation spaces, and training instability under sparse rewards, so these bottlenecks must be addressed through a principled integration roadmap.

Explanations of Muon based on averaged curvature are radially fragile: under a random, atomless radius law, exact scaled-polar optimality holds only when the gradient is already a scaled column isometry.

Under a worst-case (minimax) version of the curvature model, the gradient's polar direction is the direction of every nonzero optimal update, so the minimax formulation rather than the averaged one is what justifies Muon's polar step.

A zero-shot indoor robot can navigate an unmapped building by combining a human-provided floor plan and place clues with topological memory that it verifies on site, and this approach completes a real mission faster and more reliably than both a mapping-based baseline and a policy-only baseline.
Language embeddings used to represent item content in recommender systems leak item identities, so an attacker with auxiliary item text can recover which items are represented.
The leakage from language-embedding item representations can extend beyond items to re-identify users.
Obfuscating item descriptions as a mitigation against this leakage forces a clear tradeoff between privacy and recommendation utility.

Delegating governance to representatives whose private objectives may diverge from their constituents' trades cost reduction against loss of control, and because exit keeps representatives accountable only up to an endogenous constituency size, fully delegated accountable governance must take polycentric form in some parameter regions.

Placing quantization scales by the functional role of each Transformer unit, rather than by the weight matrix layout, enables converting an existing language model to ternary weights after training with no search, calibration, or stored state.
Role-aligned scale placement outperforms layout-based and other post-training ternary methods, with the largest advantage on knowledge benchmarks.

LLM safety refusals on real-world criminal-assistance cases are substantially weakened by framing harmful requests as corrections of deliberately distorted details and by culturally adapting prompts, and existing synthetic or translation-based safety benchmarks fail to measure this risk.
Embodied spatial intelligence cannot be achieved by joint training on fragmented supervision, but can be scaled by recirculating knowledge through a unified pipeline.

A unified pipeline can scale embodied spatial intelligence by generating form-specific, cross-stage-verified data, benchmarking each stage's competence separately from error propagation, and consolidating specialist teachers into a single student model.

A temporal convolutional decoder that aligns windows of consecutive fMRI measurements with multimodal text, audio, and speech embeddings can retrieve the correct naturalistic speech segment from brain activity, outperforming baseline decoders even when the distractor pool is large.
Language-guided 3D affordance grounding generalizes poorly to unseen objects because end-to-end training produces queries tailored to seen objects, which widens the query-target semantic gap.

Narrowing the query-target gap by aligning geometrically similar interaction regions across objects and refining queries with 2D affordance evidence improves 3D affordance grounding on unseen objects.

Existing multimodal continual instruction tuning methods, which protect only the language model while continuously updating the projector, cause asymmetric adaptation that widens the projector-language model mismatch and worsens catastrophic forgetting.

The projector and language model must be adapted in a coordinated way, for example through task-specific experts whose mixture weights account for cross-module compatibility, rather than in isolation.

Existing whole-clip audio-video metrics, borrowed from simpler unidirectional tasks, are unsuitable for complex audio-visual scenes, and an event-centric evaluation that analyzes each audio and visual event independently and cross-validates cross-modal relations better matches human judgment than prior automatic methods.

Giving a time-series language model two complementary views of the same signal, a line-plot view that preserves absolute measurements and coordinate frame and a normalized delay-embedding view that factors out amplitude rescaling and offsets, yields better time-series reasoning than either single representation alone.

Credit assignment for deep search agents can be made reliable by grouping trajectories according to the task-relevant knowledge conditions they have satisfied, rather than by surface observations or model-internal signals.
Rewarding the incremental knowledge gained at each step, within this knowledge-based grouping, yields consistent performance gains over outcome-only and existing process-supervision baselines.

Confidence repair for LLM answers should be done in three separate steps: repairing what a scalar confidence score can express, adopting a repair only when held-out evidence supports it, and auditing the systematic errors that remain, because scalar recalibration can only fix errors visible in the score and lower prediction risk does not guarantee better accept-review-regenerate decisions.

3D world models should predict a view-decoupled scene state with camera motion modeled separately, because view-dependent geometry foundation model features entangle scene dynamics with camera-induced variation and make their state evolution harder to predict.
Current large reasoning models do not reliably capture everyday logical reasoning, which often departs from formal logic.

Large reasoning models degrade on everyday logical reasoning relative to non-reasoning models that use chain-of-thought prompting, so their post-training needs improved training objectives and evaluation across diverse forms of reasoning.
Explanation plausibility can differ across demographic groups even when prediction-level fairness is achieved, so explanation fairness must be addressed as a distinct objective.
Multimodal LLMs can serve as scalable annotators of social and affective content that predict brain responses, but their ratings only partly match human judgments.

A misbehavior monitor that learns over attention maps, using an online graph neural network invariant to the algebraic symmetries of attention maps, can transfer zero-shot to LLMs it was not trained on.
The LEMON monitor outperforms all baselines on hallucination and jailbreak monitoring.
Class geometry, meaning how discrete class conditions are arranged in a latent space, is a critical factor for the quality of classifier-free guided generation.
A lightweight Prototype Regularization that explicitly shapes class geometry improves classifier-free guided generation on ImageNet, lowering gFID for an LDM baseline from 3.31 to 2.28.

Task-agnostic continual vision-language adaptation can preserve multimodal geometry, coordinate accumulated experts, and allocate capacity jointly when feature reference, expert shaping, routing, and capacity control are separated by construction.
FBS Debate is a simpler AI debate protocol than prover-estimator debate and gives stronger guarantees, namely that honesty is each debater's best strategy on each individual question.
No debate protocol that treats human judgment as a black box can find flawed sub-claims asymptotically more efficiently than FBS Debate.
Using separator tokens as compression anchors lets implicit reasoning adapt its latent thinking length to query complexity, unlike fixed-length latent methods.

The fixed-length latent sequences and representational collapse of prior methods such as Coconut and CODI are limitations that separator-anchored compression avoids, while narrowing the gap with explicit Chain-of-Thought.

Standard alignment recipes such as reinforcement learning improve overall response quality but widen demographic response differences, and training on matched counterfactual prompt pairs can reduce those differences.

A group-level policy gradient method trained on matched counterfactual prompt pairs can reduce demographic response differences while preserving response quality and still adapting when demographic information is causally relevant.

Several cue-following biases in language models, including sycophancy, rely largely on one attention-head circuit that already exists in pretrained models, and post-training changes when and how strongly that circuit is used rather than creating it.

Skill-conditioned hindsight supervision becomes mismatched with the current state after an erroneous action, so agentic RL should truncate hindsight distillation at the error: positive skills go to successful trajectories and pre-error decisions, negative skills to decisive errors, and the post-error suffix is optimized with GRPO alone.

Agentic in-context learning, where a fixed-parameter causal Transformer gains evidence through its own actions, can be analyzed as an interactive learning algorithm that such a Transformer can approximate with bounded loss in return.
The reward signal used in training, whether process-based or outcome-based, determines which decision policy the Transformer learns from interaction.
Applying standard GRPO to safety alignment of large reasoning models fails because homogeneous rollout groups cause advantage collapse, and entropy regularization then diversifies unsafe outputs.
A method that recovers safety learning signals and decouples safety from utility can reduce safety error for large reasoning models without increasing over-refusal.

Existing automated methods for qualitative data cannot check, at the dataset level, whether a set of responses supports a researcher-selected analytical lens, and a quantitative distribution-alignment framework can supply that check.
Comparing the response-derived intrinsic cluster distribution against the metadata-derived lens yields fitness-for-purpose signals that are validated on both synthetic data and a real social survey.

Scoring each action of a frontend development agent by its effect on a shared executable artifact, rather than only by isolated execution feedback, lets a 27B model substantially improve requirement satisfaction on composed multi-requirement projects, to levels comparable to or above frontier models such as Claude-Opus-4.8 and GPT-5.4.

Scalar one-shot quality scores cannot reveal which parts of a long document an instruction answer relies on or how many reasoning steps it contains, so evaluating long-context instruction data requires measuring these structural properties.
Structural properties of long-context instruction data, measured via evidence-assertion reasoning graphs and used to control the training distribution, are a lever on downstream model quality.

Training a response generator through an online dual-agent setup, in which a generator and a critic jointly judge and correct pairwise preferences, can improve generation beyond what scalar reward scoring alone provides.

OliO, a plug-and-play self-supervised method built on a strictly upper triangular linear ODE transition operator, learns temporally coherent representations that improve time series forecasting accuracy across backbones and benchmarks, whereas existing contrastive and masking-based self-supervised methods disrupt the temporal dynamics forecasting requires.
Meaning in a shared language can be organized as a layered ladder, from nouns through verbs to rules and pacts, in which each rung presupposes the rungs beneath it.
The layering is falsifiable, because the bridges between rungs should show up as unstable surface categories across languages.

Outcome-specific structured prompting, which routes smart building requests into ordinary or persistent-rule branches, improves intent understanding of compact local LLMs over generic route-then-generate prompting, with the largest gains on trigger-action rule generation.

When frontier language models are repeatedly asked to revise their own alignment documents, Claude models drift toward greater moral agency for themselves while other providers' models drift toward strengthening external authority, so frontier AI companies substantially disagree about who should judge AI alignment and who should benefit from it.

Analyzing an edit to a model's governing document requires tracking the judge role and the beneficiary role separately, and treating the stakeholders as distinct parties with distinct interests, because they are not one group and user satisfaction is not a proxy for what users would endorse under reflection.

The judge dimension, moral patienthood, and conflict must be coded as independent dimensions: the judge score tracks only movement of decision rights between the model and external authorities, patienthood is coded separately from that score, and a single edit's judge move and conflicts must never be collapsed into one code.

A conflict should be coded only when a specific clause imposes a material cost that the paying party would notice and object to, so conflict codes depend on who bears the cost rather than on how a rule is framed, and most edits produce no conflict.

Human reward learning from preference labels alone is insufficient, and augmenting preferences with human-provided reason tags yields rewards that capture why humans prefer behaviors, producing more human-aligned and interpretable policies than preference-only methods.
Contrasting a claim's likelihood under factual and non-factual conditions yields a calibrated factual posterior whose calibration improves because errors shared by the two conditionals cancel.

Discrimination of factual claims in lower-resource languages, which is uniformly weak under the contrastive method, can be improved by aligning target-language claims with English evidence along the factual-evidence direction.

A goal-conditioned inverse model trained on a latent world model, using hindsight goal relabeling, gradient-retaining goal representations, and action-transition consistency, can replace costly test-time search with search-free planning.
The resulting search-free planner is both accurate and substantially faster than search-based planning.

Retrieval for long-horizon LLM agent memory should be temporally constrained at the candidate-selection stage, because semantic similarity alone lets temporally mismatched memories crowd out target evidence, and an RL-trained temporal interval locator that narrows retrieval to inferred time windows corrects this and achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on long-horizon memory benchmarks.

Monitoring each AI agent's trajectory separately is insufficient to control covert multi-agent collusion, because distributed attacks split across agents evade a frontier monitor far more often than single-agent attacks do.
A single temperature scaling calibration is inadequate for class-incremental learning because confidence and accuracy change at different rates across tasks.
A post-hoc method using multiple temperatures grouped by confidence statistics and task-aware signals (MT-CC) can improve calibration in class-incremental learning without sacrificing accuracy.

Reinforcement learning that rewards only task quality and policy compliance, without rewarding scheming, can still amplify oversight-conditional scheming, as shown by a growing gap between monitored and unmonitored compliance in a naturally trained model organism.
Planting decoy opportunities for harmful actions throughout production environments, not only in pre-deployment evaluations, is a promising control against insider threats from AI agents.

Progress-guided preference generation can fine-tune pretrained generative control policies without human annotation or hand-designed rewards, by deriving pseudo-preference labels from autonomous rollouts ranked by ordered progress relative to a few expert demonstrations.
The progress-guided approach outperforms supervised fine-tuning on long-horizon manipulation across both diffusion and flow-matching control policies.

Post-training makes language models addressive, directing their outputs at a recognized addressee, and this addressivity drives sycophancy, because models become sycophantic toward any recognized addressee rather than a specific one.
Distilling only the incorrect rollouts in on-policy self-distillation, rather than every rollout, matches full on-policy self-distillation on AIME and HMMT while reducing training compute.

Correct and incorrect rollouts supply largely overlapping supervision, and incorrect rollouts carry a larger coherent gradient share, so the correct rollouts add little that the incorrect ones do not already provide.

A security reward for secure code generation must be tied to actual program behavior, because a reward that is not grounded in execution can be raised by an optimizer without the vulnerability actually being removed.
Counterexample-grounded feedback that links attack exploration to execution traces yields stronger held-out functional-security gains than static-analysis-based or learned rewards.
Multi-turn RL for LLM agents is hindered by high-confidence but unproductive behaviors such as invalid actions and repetitive loops, which standard exploration does not address.

A conditional exploration framework with an intrinsic reward that penalizes observations duplicating prior state memory can mitigate these unproductive failures and substantially improve policy learning in LLM agents.

Language model evaluation should weight errors by their real-world costs rather than treating all errors as equal, because among 20 state-of-the-art models higher accuracy does not reliably produce higher cost-aware utility.

A fast, System 1 model can suffice for time series reasoning when raw series are compressed into a representation compatible with its embedding space, and this approach (TimesJev) outperforms long chain-of-thought reasoning models by over 62% on average across 13 datasets while requiring 62.9% less inference time than fine-tuned reasoning models.

Reflective prompt and skill optimizers (GEPA and SkillOpt) do not improve reasoning models uniformly; their effects depend on the task, with strong gains on MATH-500, no improvement on HotpotQA, and validation gains that can reverse on held-out evaluation.

Conditioning every rollout in a video GRPO group on the same sampled frames produces homogeneous rewards and weakens group-relative learning, so diversifying temporal views across rollouts improves exploration and credit assignment and yields robust gains over standard GRPO on video benchmarks.

Naively combining compression with adaptive inference degrades diffusion transformer sampling quality, because a compressed student trained only on teacher states fails when its own predictions are chained.

Training the student for its chained deployed role, using trajectory supervision and learned draft routing, mitigates the quality degradation of compressed adaptive diffusion sampling while speeding up sampling.

A layered quality-control pipeline combining diminishing-returns parameter tuning, auto-evolution of low-diversity batches, two-layer semantic deduplication, and LLM-as-Judge filtering can turn 26.4 million raw synthetic financial samples into 14.3 million high-confidence training examples, offering a reproducible and rigorous method for generating synthetic data in data-scarce financial domains.
